reviews.author: Mike Graham
reviews.text: If I could post minus scores they would certainly get a minus score. I have a serious condition which is causing me excruciating pain. 9 weeks ago I had an appointment with a doctor from this clinic. He promised me that a letter would be sent to the hospital so I could have some scans. Due to no correspondence coming from this surgery other than to fill out surveys from Surveymonkey, I have to call repeatedly. Most times nobody will answer the phone. After no letter being sent I requested an emergency appointment and complained. As soon as I complained I was given an emergency face to face appointment. The doctor and receptionist apologized unreservedly and admitted my care was poor at this clinic. They promised me the letter would be sent as priority that day . Almost two weeks later after another 5 calls to the clinic I am told that the letter still hasn't been sent. Doctor has given me no pain relief and does not know anything about my condition. I cannot go to the hospital as I need a referral from a GP. We wonder why the NHS is in a poor state and underfunded and then look at this clinic and you see your answer. They do not care for you correctly. They allow your condition to deteriorate and do not make the correct referrals to the hospital at the right time . This means that the cost of your care increases massively and the length of time you suffer and the time it takes for you to get well again increases which in turn shortens your life span. They ignore the telephone. The receptionists are rude . They get prescriptions wrong all the time and seems like they alter your prescription without authorisation. The doctors seem to lack knowledge and common sense. The clinic is constantly empty but there are doctors and nurses there and yet they can never give you an appointment. The NHS need to do something regarding this type of doctor service. DO NOT USE THIS CLINIC. Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your feedback. reviews.author: John Mccormack
reviews.text: Only recently moved to this general practice and I regret moving at all. I’d prefer the 40 minute drive to my previous GPs over the below woeful experiences the last several weeks. Attached image of a confirmation text from the GPs. Booked the morning off work, arrive to the appointment to be told I’m booked in for September. Today is Friday the 15th August. Not Monday the 15th September. Secondly, advised over the phone to register my daughter for the GPs I’ll need to come physically into the building to scan a QR code that isn’t on the website. Scanned, completed and registered. Popped in to see if this has progressed as we’ve heard nothing - nothing on the system, come in with your child to register her. Another morning off work. Finally, the biggest disaster - I’ve had a kidney stone for several weeks, agonising pain. Hospital discharged me with a scan booked that due to a motorway accident I couldn’t attend (things happen, life…). I ended up back in hospital again with kidney pain and was advised to raise with my GP to rebook a scan, raised via patches and requested “update via telephone” (though I’m not sure why you’d bother given they’ll either just update in patches with no notification to you or text, they don’t honour the requested means of contact). No update for a week, I log into patches to find the request has been cancelled due to “more information required” from the GP. Bear in mind the request outlines a doctor at the hospital has outlined I require a kidney scan and to request this from the GPs. Symptoms = kidney pain likely stones (not confirmed yet as need the scan, could be more malicious!) and noted worsening pain. I raise another patches request and am advised to come in later that week. At this point I’ve no more tramadol a new born baby and I can’t move. I’ve rang the GP to ask for help, they advised ring 111, I ring 111 who advise speak to the GP. 111 ring the GP who advise they can’t see me today, so I end up back in hospital. With agonising pain. Avoid entirely. I’ll be moving myself, my partner and our child to another GPs that doesn’t have such shocking reviews. And I can see why. One gentleman behind the reception counter is genuinely lovely and helpful, one male doctor (with a slight lisp, apologies on the description but credit due where credit is due his expertise and professionalism were exceptional and I don’t know his name!) the rest of the staff that I have encountered should take note of the above as my experiences have been of incompetence, unhelpful, rude, demeaning and frustrated tones over the phone. Almost as though it’s somehow MY fault information isn’t being passed between health care “professionals” via hospital > GP and / or completed forms disappearing into the void. The reception staff (excluding the outlined gentleman above) are the embodiment of “every GP receptionist thinks they are a medical expert”. This practise would be laughable if it wasn’t a case of people’s lives and welfare at stake. More than embarrassing, an utter disgrace. Practice response date: 6 months ago Practice response: Thank you for your feedback. We are sorry to hear you have been unwell and are experiencing issues with some members of staff and the patchs system. Your comments have been passed on to the practice manager. If you would like to discuss your feedback further, please either contact the practice directly and ask to speak to the practice manager or contact our patient services team via gtd.feedback@nhs.net.

reviews.author: Devon Tynan
reviews.text: Shocking GP service. I have been a patient here since being a child, I’m now 24 and only in the last year or 2 has this GP service really gone down hill. My main concern at this GP practice is a fairly new member of reception staff called Farzana, she is extremely rude and unhelpful. I recently rang to review my sons records he had blood tests 6 months prior to this phone call where she told me there was a problem with my sons blood results and I needed to make an appointment with a doctor to discuss these where she offered me an appointment for in 3 weeks time. I went to the GP practice to collect a copy of his blood results so I could see which of his bloods were out of range, when I got there she told me I couldn’t collect my 6 year olds blood results without ID, this is not GP policy you only need ID to collect somebody else’s results if they are over 16. I demanded my sons bloods were reviewed by somebody clinical that day as six months had gone by since the bloods were done. Farzana was extremely argumentative. Another receptionist heard and was helpful and understanding and went and got a nurse to review his bloods. The nurse reassured me and said his bloods had been put as no action by a doctor which was completely different to what Farzana had told me on the phone. Farzana did not apologise for the mistake she had made or the panic and upset she had caused me. A couple of weeks later I had to ring again after my son had been bit by a dog, I asked if she could look if he was up to date with his immunisations so I knew if he was covered for his tetanus vaccine, she told me I would have to wait 2 weeks for a nurse to action this. Here are only 2 examples of how unsafe it is for this woman to work on reception. She makes clinical decisions which I would deem as unsafe and are not within her scope of practice, and overall is a very rude unpleasant person to communicate with. Other than the receptionist, waiting times for appointments are extremely long, the doctor is different every appointment which is unfortunate for patients with long term health problems, also the gp practice appears to no longer be offering blood tests, patients are having to go up to tameside hospital to have their bloods done which can be very time consuming. I have had an ongoing problems with my health since October, each doctor I have seen has given me a different opinion, and I feel I am no closer to a diagnosis. As far as I am aware the NHS is supposed to facilitate informed decision making and involving the patient in their own care something I feel this GP practice does very poorly. I have had to take a lot of time out of work to be treated at the walk in centre due to the lack of care given. I am now unfortunately considering moving GP practice which is a shame as I have been a patient for a long time along with my 3 children and a lot of other extended family members.

Nevertheless, how you answer this question usually results in not receiving the said 'emergency appointment' and you are back to the appointment a week away. I know that the NHS is going downhill and this surgery probably is reflective of this. As a working patient I struggle to gain a good service from this surgery. They explained today that they have over 4000 patients which makes a good service difficult. I do have some understanding and It is fine having all the understanding about figures and data and staff. Ultimately, as a patient i just want a good, effective service that supports me 'the patient' and the reality check is that his is just not happening!

My mum has been suffering a bad chest infection she rang lindley medical practice last week to ask for an appointment to be told she’s no longer registered at this medical practice since August 2023. When asked why she was told they sent forms off last year and received a form back to say she’s gone away. Lies Lies Lies as no letters received here. Now my mum is suffering and is in desperate need of antibiotics as she struggles to breathe. Rang 111 was told an out of hours GP will call back in 2 hours waited 6 hours for the phone to ring only to be told a GP will call within the next 6 hours. Now I have to take the day off work to take her to A&E tomorrow. What a joke my mum has worked all her life paid tax and NI contributions and for what this absolute horrific service. Since the pandemic happened its almost impossible to get face to face for my young baby too, it takes 3 to 4 days of phoning at 8am to even get a phone appointment. After 3 telephone appointments for my under 1 year old In the last 3 weeks I asked for a face to face app today because my baby is not getting better.GP said I can bring baby in within an hour, I tried to explain I need alittle longer but GP didn’t care to hear it she insisted I attend within the hour or baby won’t be seen so I agreed. So when I finally did get a face to face appointment there was 0 flexibility offered which is not good when have other children to get to school. I must say the GP’s and reception staff in general are lovely and GP’s used to be really thorough when seen face to face, but that is unfortunately not the case anymore and the telephone appointments with the GP’s are just pointless and rushed. I will be changing GP, I know the pandemic has put an added pressure on NHS but I can honestly say after 3 years of going from bad to worse Lindley have no excuse for their lack of care & appointments for patients especially the vulnerable elderley patients and young children. I do believe Lindley can return to a really good practice like they once were if patient feedback is taken on board and they actually make changes and manage the practice properly.

reviews.text: Appointment with Dr Zaluki (amazing doctor by the way) on Dec 16th who requested to see me in 4 weeks to review medication. Receptionist was rude and couldn't help, rolled her eyes at colleagues when I insisted I needed the appointment. Eventually was given the earliest available appointment of 3rd February at 11am with Dr Ben Hamida (also a good doctor). This would be a 7 week wait for an appointment, which is appalling but I didn't have much choice (and isn't the first time I've had such a long wait). Arrived today, after taking time out from work as a teacher where my role has to be covered, to be told I had no appointment scheduled. How can this have happened other than if the receptionist on the 16th never booked the appointment in? Also now in a race against time to get repeat medication before my current set runs out. Some decent doctors here if you can get to see them but the practice is terribly run. I will be leaving after today.

reviews.author: Lauren Fisher
reviews.text: I feel this practice is the best example of why the NHS is so stretched and patients have to wait so long for an appointments. They don't seem to follow a good system therefore so many appointments are getting wasted and putting unnecessary pressure on the NHS. I was unable to get an appointment and due to my symptoms was advised to go A&E who done tests and referred me back to my GP for 2 further tests, which were clearly requested on the form so should have been able to book in directly with the nurse for these. The practice couldn't do this, said i needed a routine app with the gp to decide (5 weeks wait) then be referred back to the nurse (within the next 7 days - so 6 weeks minimum). I couldn't wait this long with lower body numbness so visited the walk in (2nd app in NHS) referred for bloods as A&E had advised. I attended the bloods appointment (3rd appointment in NHS) where they were unable to take said bloods which had now been documented as required twice. I was then advised i needed to see another GP to be referred back to the nurse - if I had stayed with this practice that would be 5 appointments, 5 mornings off work (self employed dental therapist so cancelling NHS patients of my own). I registered at a practice on Tuesday and have had my new patient check and the bloods that were requested by A&E within 2 days. Thee nurse at my new practice read the discharge note from A&E and done bloods as it was clearly stated by the Doctor that it was required. Please look into the way you run your practice, I totally understand practice protocols as i have managed a dental practice myself and worked in a GP surgery. The way you operate is ineffective and is straining the NHS therefore inconveniencing your patients. On a positive note i feel all the staff i have met in the short time at the practice have been very nice, pleasent and do try to help there just bound by the lack of appointments of protocols they have to follow

reviews.author: M. Jones
reviews.text: One gp here was nice because he listened to me when I had problems with my mental health. But the other GP (the arrogant and overpowering one) just re-traumatised me when they made me talk through a horrific assault I'd experienced in another healthcare building from a professional. At the time I should have said no to talking through this trauma, but at this time I was so weak because of the PTSD I wasn't putting my own wellbeing first. I got copies of my medical records years later and discovered that this GP didn't type into my records the details of the trauma I had told them of. So that GP had me talking through this trauma (which worsened my mental health and exhausted me) for nothing. Also , it meant that there was less evidence in my medical records. (I was traumatised for years, the NHS minimised this trauma, so did GMC, and I reported too but they failed to act. You're not safe anywhere, and supposedly safe buildings are ideal for predators to work in. Avoid going into appointments on your own if you need something doing. I can't go near most of them now for fear, and many talk down to us anyway while dismissing patients.) This GP also likes to pressure patients ignoring the fact they are fragile, and is the competitive type. Astonishing that they don't understand PTSD and that you can easily worsen the patient's mental health if you are verbally thoughtless. Another thing about this surgery is that the GP's here are not very knowledgeable... I was going in to this surgery coughing non-stop, and they didn't even explore what could have been causing my cough. Well over two years later an open minded respiratory consultant sent me to ENT and we finally discovered that I'd been suffering from LPR for over 2 years. This type of reflux isn't very rare and I'm still shocked that the GP's here didn't even think of this. They would just type "coughing day and night" consistently into my records each time I went into this surgery, and I'd then go home after making no progress. At least I stopped buying useless pills they kept pushing me to buy. Aloe Vera juice worked much better to relieve my symptoms. I'm glad I refused pills for anxiety and depression - they are very bad for the body. Sometimes all doctors do is destroy us.

reviews.text: this place needs a 0 star option. I know it's hard to get placements at GP's but for your own sake avoid this place like the plague. I've been dealing with an illness for the past few years, and Corkland road surgery, more specifically it's reception staff have only ever made things ten times worse. They lose prescriptions. They forget to hand in prescriptions. They tell you they've done things that they haven't and then pass the blame on to other members of staff that aren't in on the day that you speak to them. usually I'd feel bad about condemning an entire practice and it's staff, but over the last few years I've dealt with all of them and I'm not exaggerating when i say that every one of the rotating cast of women on reception is rude, dismissive, and completely inept. They can't carry out the most basic of tasks, and they couldn't care less that the people they're serving come to them often in times of desperation and experiencing pain. Maybe it's a bit idealistic to expect everyone who works for the NHS to actually care about patients (and thankfully I've had experiences at other practices that prove this wrong), but you would hope that they'd at least pretend to care as that's what they're paid to do. i've had to complain about them multiple times in the past already but nothing changes, they keep their jobs and they keep making vulnerable people's lives harder. But it gets worse. When you're at your lowest and simply want to get hold of prescriptions you handed in ages ago, that they "forgot to put through" and you go in to see them in person, be prepared for all four of the girls on reception to laugh in your face. I would name and shame as it's gotten to the point where I've had to take most of their names but honestly they're all as bad as each other. This isn't only the worst GP that I've ever experienced, it's the worst service i've ever experienced bar none. the only silver lining is that I only have to look after myself. God forbid that you leave the care of your children or vulnerable loved ones in the hands of these people.

The receptionist had clearly had enough of this "doctor" too as this wasn't the only mess up she'd had to rectify. We learnt nothing from this appointment, no tests (aside from a blood pressure one which showed as being low, to which she looked at my partner and said "make sure she's eating properly") Not even a confirmation of pregnancy... just straight to a midwife referral. This was an absolutely unreal experience and I will be changing surgeries at my soonest possible opportunity.

reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for a number of years , unfortunately I have to say over the last 12mths the service and professionalism has significantly deteriorated. it is almost impossible to obtain an appointment with out 3 weeks notice if you work in a job where you can not take time off for a GP appointment and have to arrange in your own time . The reception managers attitude to this problem appears to be that its the patients problem and you should take the time off work to fit in with them. . for many years I have been prescribed medications to cover 2 or 3 months supply. However, now I can only get 1 months supply at a time this means I am now paying between £400 and £500 per year extra for prescriptions. Today I have been informed from another GP that I could buy a pre payment certificate for £104 per year that covers all my medications. ??? There is no information available in the surgery about this. Why have they not informed me ?? I believe we need to increase NHS funding and I have no issues with an increase in taxation to help with this as then we all pay more for the fantastic service the NHS provides .but this practice does not seem to want to help its patients and provides a very poor service . That said the girls on reception are excellent in tough circumstances and poor management

reviews.author: Hina Mistry
reviews.text: I have edited this review as one of the drs asked me to change it: I am deeply disappointed with the care at this practice. Despite experiencing severe symptoms—including persistent tinnitus and excruciating ear pain—I struggled to secure a timely appointment. On multiple occasions, I was told no slots were available and advised to call 111, only to later receive conflicting information about GP availability. This poor communication delayed my treatment unnecessarily. After resorting to out-of-hours services, I was finally seen within minutes and diagnosed with a middle ear infection, reinforcing concerns about mismanaged scheduling. Some of the GPs at this practice do not seem to take patient concerns seriously, making it difficult to receive necessary referrals. One GP refused to refer me to ENT despite my ongoing symptoms—only for an out-of-hours GP to confirm that an ENT consultation was required to rule out vascular issues. Additionally, my interaction with a staff member, Katie, was unprofessional—she was abrupt, dismissive, and hung up on me without cause. The lack of clarity regarding referrals, particularly with ENT, further highlights ongoing issues with patient care. While I did encounter a helpful receptionist, the overall decline in professionalism and responsiveness at this practice is alarming. I am also concerned that my previous Google review may have been hidden, which raises further questions about transparency and accountability. Patients deserve better communication, respect, and timely medical attention.

reviews.text: I am sitting in a hospital room with my mother whose been diagnosed with the worst case of pneumonia the doctor has seen. I would say that if a person phones to say that the three days of antibiotics and steroids haven't worked it doesn't help when asked if it's" urgent to speak to a doctor because you've already spoken to once this week." If it was possible to give less than the 1 star available then I would as I think my Mums lack of treatment shocking!

reviews.text: This is the best, most positive practice i have been a patient of in 65 years. The reception staff are so cheerful and friendly, the nusing and administative staff are so understanding and helpful. The doctors are true caring family doctors, who have the time, knowledge and expertise to deal with your medical and/or mental needs. The facilities, services and care they provide for their 10,000 patients is first class. There are some patients who simply dont realise what a brilliant family practice they belong to and make demands that are not always possible, practical. The national statistics show that The Dunstan Partnership is one of the leading practices in Bolton by far, with many above ratings by far.

reviews.text: I usually really like being part of this doctors as when I used to ring to make an appointment I'd be put in a que instead of having to keep calling and once through I was able to make an appointment straight away. Now they've changed it and they want you to book your appointment online, even if you're having trouble doing so they then want you to ring after 11 so they can "help you" what ever happened to just being able to ring up and make an appointment over the phone, easy and reliable but now everything is done online like they just can't be arsed to do their jobs. I'll be glad to move from here now.

reviews.author: Paula Serrano
reviews.text: Dear Practice Manager, I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a receptionist during my calls to the surgery on 22/09/2025 at approximately 08:30am. During the call, I provided my son’s date of birth correctly ( date birth ). The receptionist repeatedly insisted that I had given the wrong date, despite me clarifying several times. This interaction became unnecessarily argumentative, and instead of acknowledging my clarification, she accused me of raising my voice, which was not the case. Feeling distressed, I called back and asked for my call to be transferred to another colleague who might better understand the situation. The same receptionist refused to transfer the call, insisting she had already corrected the date, which I found unacceptable and unprofessional. This is not the first time I have experienced rudeness from this particular staff member. As a parent of a young child, I expect to be treated with respect and professionalism when contacting the surgery, especially when the matter concerns my child’s health. I kindly request that this incident be investigated, that appropriate action be taken to address the receptionist’s behaviour, and that I receive a written response regarding the outcome of my complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely and I will make this formal 100%

reviews.text: My partner is with this doctors, she's been having some checks done, ultrasound and bloods, they messaged her to book in a telephone appointment to discuss her results, she did this and the "earliest appointment" was in a month's time. My partner suffers from depression and anxiety and having the weight of not knowing when we already know is something serious is definitely not doing her any good. This is all prior to them ringing her last month to tell her over the phone they think she has endometriosis or polysistic overises now instead of asking her in to discuss this properly they thought it would be okay being told over the phone, now my partner struggles anyway with phone calls but personally I think this is something they should have brought her in to discuss properly with her. They've prescribed her with some meds but as the call was a lot on its own she's actually unaware on what she's supposed to be taking and when as they perscrib3d her with a few different types of medications. I just think they've gone about it all wrong and leaving her a whole month to wait to see what her second lot of bloods came back like, it's a joke really.

reviews.author: Jean Hughes
reviews.text: I have not had such a thorough and comprehensive appointment with a doctor, ever! Dr Choxi was so very kind, put himself out to make sure I had an appointment with him today. In house, all the tests were done, instead of having to wait for referral after referral, and, from the receptionist all the way to the nurses and this amazing doctor, I cannot say enough about how positive this experience was. He took so much time to explain everything, looked back on my records to get the big picture of my health and, while this should really be common practice, these days it is very rare. I am delighted and extremely impressed with this practice. I feel lucky to have found this doctor

reviews.author: DAVID GRUNDY
reviews.text: My partner made an appointment for me and was told the appointment could only be a telephone appointment, the MyGP app also confirmed that the appointment was a telephone GP consultation, the appointment came and went with no phone call so I called the surgery and the receptionist told me that it was a face to face appointment, I would have to call back on Monday for another appointment. I recalled having verified it on the app that it was telephone appointment but was just told it must have been some kind of mistake and there were no more appointments, I would have to call back another day. Makes me wonder how often this is done and if the NHS is still being charged for their time.

reviews.author: Joanne Moore
reviews.text: Had a telephone consultation on Friday 10th May at 5.10p.m.I had a text reminder on Wednesday. It didn't happen at that time but I thought I would wait because appointments very rarely happen on time.It got to 6 p.m I thought I ring the doctors .I explained what I was waiting for I was told that the person who should have rung me was off sick. Apparently I had had a phone call & text message the day before.Which I never did. I've got to admit I am totally disappointed with the surgery.

reviews.author: F Patel
reviews.text: Honestly, I would give 0 stars if I could! I had the worst experience as a whole.. I moved into the bl3 area just before I had a baby, so I thought it’d be ideal to change surgery. Worst decision ever made! Never needed to call the surgery before my baby was born.. but EVERY single time I have called, nothing has ever gone smoothly! My last experience was the worst by far. Had to wait for my call to be answered for over 30 minutes, then the receptionist said I had to wait for a phone consultation. That’s absolutely fine. Then when the doctor called, told me to come into the surgery immediately. Imagine with a 6 month old baby I rushed everything and got out of the house within 5 mins. Then when I got there, the doctor made me wait over 50 mins to see my child. Then eventually he came and said my baby’s name and which room to visit.. I was near the door with a small pram, he saw this and closed the door in front of me.. so I was on my own trying to juggle the door & pram.. Then I walked in to the room, and the doctor started another phone consultation IN FRONT of me! Not like I waited 50 mins outside already, I had to wait another 10 mins inside of the doctors office! ABSOLUTELY UN CALLED FOR! I’ve waited long enough with my baby, who was by that time getting wingey! Also DATA PROTECTION, as I heard the whole conversation. I know exactly what he spoke to them about. He Spoke to the patient, and his wife and I knew exactly when he booked the appointment for and why. This was my last time visiting this surgery!

reviews.author: Anita Casserly
reviews.text: Not even worth 1 star. Disgusted at the surgery. A seriously ill elderly man who should have had a home visit had to be taken to the surgery cause the doc had no time. I had to watch whilst this doc pulled up the clothing of a man with shingles as if it was bandaid. The doc new he was in pain & getting him up & down of the bed was horrendous & I had to tell him to wait as he came of. It was disgusting, I'm disgusted at this doctor but better still he didn't even bother to wash his hands. When an elderly patient requests a home visit then this should be given. If a patient is seriously ill then you don't ask them to go down in a taxi.

reviews.author: Anmole Shah
reviews.text: I never take out the time to write negative reviews but this place really needed one with their extremely poor service from the receptionists. I called the reception at 8am at 39 weeks pregnant with cold and flu symptoms and was told by one of the ladies (who had a extremely unprofessional tone) that the GP can’t do anything and I should call my midwife. Common sense says that midwife’s don’t give prescriptions out for colds and flus. I told the receptionist this and she totally dismissed me and said there’s nothing they can do after I was on hold for 15mins. I then proceeded to Call maternity triage who said they don’t understand why I had called them as the GP normally deals with cold and flu symptoms, pregnant or not (surprise surprise). She told me to call the Gp back. So I called the GP surgery back and a different lady answered the phone this time and said ‘We wouldn’t have told you to call the midwife as we know they don’t give out prescriptions’. I told her someone at the reception DID tell me to call the midwife and turned me away and I ended up wasting an hour calling everyone back and fourth. I told her the call should be looked into and she didn’t even apologise, completely dismissive and told me that she will book me in for a telephone consultation. I will definitely be changing my GP surgery. The unprofessionalism is unbelievable in this place.

reviews.author: Zahraa Badat
reviews.text: As much as I love this GP the receptionists are absolutely rude! They need to learn basic customer service. They talk over you and speak in a very condescending manner. Very very disappointed. Telling me I have to pay for a urine sample collection at the pharmacy for my antenatal appointments?! I don’t even have to pay for prescriptions or dental treatments, why should I pay for a urine sample when I was advised I can collect it from the GP?! Sort your receptionist’s customer service skills out.

reviews.text: If I could give this place minus or half star I would. Disgusting behaviour of the receptionists. Talk about god complex. The way they talk to patients is just horrendous, especially the elderly. Not capable of treating people with dignity, shame on them all.

reviews.author: Ayesha Pathan
reviews.text: My experience with Swan lane Medical centre has always been very pleasant. All the Gps and the medical receptionists are good. Especially Dr Arya as she is so caring and compassionate, as though she feels our pain As I went in , Dr Arya carried out a thorough check and prescribed the correct medication,followed by a very much needed abdominal ultrasound. She advised me to eat well as I was losing weight and was very concerned for me. She said I should be seen again the next month so she can check my weight if I progressed further. Dr Arya always makes me feel better because she has a little chat generally about things which calms me down and I don't feel anxious. Keep up the good work Dr 👍

reviews.author: Janet L
reviews.text: Well my younger daughter had a persistent rash which didn't respond to any treatment. The condition spread thru the extended fam. The symptoms looked more and more like scabies. Vacced all furniture. Beds. Washed all towels /clothing/bedding on hot. Tumbledried on uber hot. Followed by freezer in batches. Exhausting!! 3 year old granddaughter ripping her skin to bits, finally got an appointment for the lil un after a multitude of phone calls only to be diagnosed by some medical muppet with a virus???? So vigilance suspended the lil critters were free to run feral on the whole extended family only to get a later affirmation of Scabies. By which time we've been scrattin and loosing sleep for months. Treatment?????? No script for this.......... advised merely to self purchase at nearly £20 a small tube, and there's none to be found...... Out of stock cos there's a bit of a scabies outbreak. And then had to repeat all the decontamination protocol again.😭😭😭😭 Not a happy bunny. If a mere mortal such as my humble self can diagnose a scabid bod how did a medical practitioner get it so wrong with contagious consequences. Good job it wasn't owt terminal. I suggest a good dermatology reference book....🤔😬. Or even just Google it like the rest of us. 😉

reviews.text: Reception staff are unhelpful in the last few years they have become less and less helpful, all the while hiding behind the zero tolerance to anger posture, when they are the very people that cause the anger and frustration, I see no point in them answering the phone because when they do, they do nothing but point to idiotic rules they have created in an effort to "help", help who? Practice response date: 6 months ago Practice response: Dear Steve. Our reception team try to help our patients and guide them through our systems set by the NHS and the practice to ensure all our patients receive safe care. They do not create the rules. Often anger is aimed at them, and that is why we protect our staff with our zero tolerance anger policy. A zero tolerance policy towards violent, threatening and abusive behaviour is now in place throughout the National Health Service. The staff in this practice have the right to work in an environment free from violent, threatening or abusive behaviour and everything will be done to protect that right. At no time will any violent, threatening or abusive behaviour be tolerated towards staff, patients or other visitors to the practice. This relates to any form of abuse from patients or staff which includes (but is not limited to) sexism, racism homophobia, biphobia, transphobia and ageism, or harassment or abuse on basis of disability, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, religion or belief. Our Practice staff aim to be polite, helpful, and sensitive to all patients’ individual needs and circumstances. They would respectfully remind patients that very often staff could be confronted with a multitude of varying and sometimes difficult tasks and situations, all at the same time. The staff understand that ill patients do not always act in a reasonable manner and will take this into consideration when trying to deal with a misunderstanding or complaint. If you are still experiencing an issue please contact Diane, our Governance and Patient Experience Manager at the practice who will provide assistance. Many thanks

reviews.author: Greg Roberts
reviews.text: This place is a disgrace from top to bottom. Booking appointments to seeing an actual doctor is an imposibility, I had to wait 50 mins to see a ACP????, only to be asked well what treatment do you want🤣. This place clearly needs a CQC investigation into its practice and into the competence of the practice manager, who for as far as I can see has the intelligence of a glass if water. Practice response date: a year ago Practice response: Dear Greg, Firstly, I am sorry to learn that you are unhappy with the care that you have received from the practice and the distress the situation has caused you. I am grateful that you have brought this to our attention. As I understand it you are complaining because of a recent consultation with our ACP. The practice takes all complaints seriously and your complaint has been investigated in line with our complaints procedure. This involved me speaking to our ACP, who provided me with an account of their recollections of what happened, as well as reviewing your medical records. From your records I can see you completed a triage form request for an appointment on Thursday 17th October at 3.28pm stating you had a chest infection for one week. This form was triaged by the duty doctor, Dr Yelland, who actioned this request and he felt it was appropriate for you to see our Advanced Care Practitioner with an urgent appointment for your symptoms. Our ACP’s are fully qualified clinicians and are more than capable of treating a chest infection without the need to see a doctor. At 3.39pm on the 17th a member of our reception team booked you an appointment for later that day, 17th October at 5pm. You arrived before your appointment time at 4.43pm, and was seen at 5.35pm. This was a 35 minute delay. The ACP apologises for this delay and explains this was due to her seeing a child earlier in her clinic who’s appointment over ran, and the subsequent appointments were running behind. Unfortunately it is hard for us to predict medical emergencies and the length of time they will take, however, we do build blocks into the clinics to allow clinicians time to catch up and prevent delays to patients. On this occasion the ACP was still running behind. Reviewing her consultation she did full diagnostics for a chest infection, she enquired if you had tried anything prior to the appointment and you advised over the counter treatments. She asked if you had tried things in the past that had worked for you and you advised antibiotics and inhalers. She documented a treatment plan and a safety net then prescribed antibiotics. This is in response to her findings and your responses. With regards to your opinion of myself, I’m not aware that we have ever met, but I am happy to arrange a meeting to discuss your issues further with regards to the practice. We welcome all feedback and encourage our patients to feedback and suggest improvements. We also encourage you to join our Patient Participation Group that meets regularly. This group often discusses challenges that patients face and help work with the practice staff to resolve and improve our services. If this is something you would be interested in please contact our reception and ask for the Office Managers who run the PPG. I am sorry for the distress that this situation has caused you. We are appreciative of you bringing this to our attention and providing us with an opportunity to learn and make any necessary changes going forward. I hope that we have been able to fully address your concerns and questions. Please do not hesitate to contact me at the surgery if you feel that you need to discuss this further. If you’re not happy with our final response to your complaint and would like to take the matter further, you can contact the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman. The Ombudsman makes final decisions on complaints that have not been resolved by the NHS, government departments and some other public organisations. The service is free for everyone. To take a complaint to the Ombudsman, go to www.ombudsman.org.uk/making-complaint or call 0345 015 4033. It is important that you make the complaint as soon as you receive our final response as there are time limits for the Ombudsman to look into complaints’.

reviews.text: For the third time this year I've been disappointed with the service I've been given by this practise. First of all asking for injections to travel after many earlier attempts when I didn't have time to wait on the phone to make an appointment I was told my injections needed to be called for 2 months in advance (I was six weeks in advance of travel) when fellow travelling companions at a practise in another area of Bolton had no problems two weeks in advance to get their injections and I was informed by one of the travellers who works for the GMC that these vaccines are always in-house at the GP practise ??? Second problem having read on social media that Kearsley medical center where taking part in the lung cancer check that was taking part at a mobile unit on Tesco's carpark I called to ask if I as an ex smoker could get an appointment only to be told that Kearsley medical centre was not involved and to call Farnworth Health center who where far from impressed by my call and didnt understand why I'd recieved this information from Kearsley. I then with some searching and checking managed to arrange this appointment for myself. This morning whilst not expecting to receive the medication I've been given for years to help with panic attacks and anxiety ( I appreciate I'm older and medical procedures have changed!) I was told there was no other help for me unless I went private or perhaps contacted a travel clinic for support. So much for empathy and understanding checking if a possible other medication could be considered. I have been at this practise since I was born other than the years working abroad and over this time had treatment from some fine GP 's who went out of their way to help and understand their patients Dr Wall springs to mind, those days are sadly gone and perhaps it's time for me to check out what else is available in this area. Whilst understanding the pressures within the NHS surely the bottom line is understanding and the care of your patient.

reviews.author: Alison
reviews.text: Can't get a appointment at any time the new system is terrible you might as well go to A and E cause you will have the same wait time as getting a doctor's appointment Practice response date: a year ago Practice response: Dear Alison, thank you for your feedback. We are sorry you had a poor experience from the surgery. Total Triage is a new approach recommended by NHS England, to improve accessibility to Primary Care services. The main objectives are to enhance the quality of care our patients receive, to ensure that they are given the most appropriate appointment or advice to meet their needs and that this is done in a timely way. All patients will complete a short form, either via our website, or by the reception team who will complete this form on the patients behalf. This is to ensure that our patients who are unable to access the internet or do not have a smart phone have the same accessibility. The form is triaged by the triage GP who will decide which member of our healthcare team is best placed to help, the most suitable time frame for the appointment and whether it is best suited to be via telephone or in person at the practice. The new system also aims to reduce the 8am rush on the telephones, as patients can bypass our reception team and access the forms themselves via our website and at their leisure. Already, the practice has seen an increase in capacity with more appointments available to patients within a shorter time frame. We have to put capacity limits into the system so that both patients and staff are safe, and once our safe limit has been reached for the day you may be told to try again the following day. If it is an emergency you will be advised to attend A&E, as this is best placed for a medical emergency that cannot wait 24hours. We hope to support patients and their families/carers to get used to the new way of contacting the practice and to become comfortable with this over time. We will, of course, provide additional support to those patients who are unable to use online resources. We continue to advise that if you cannot use the internet for any reason, please call us – we will enter your details into our website for you. This may take longer than our previous system, so please be patient. We apologise again and will take your feedback on board.

reviews.author: Vicki Jones
reviews.text: Can't fault this surgery! When my little one was poorly they got him registered, did a phone appointment and saw him all within 3 hours. The reception staff are all lovely and have been so helpful. I've never struggled to get an appointment both over the phone and face to face. Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your positive feedback! This will be shared with the team. Kearsley Medical Centre

reviews.author: Steven G
reviews.text: I’m sure that the NHS strain shows with any GP, but I’m actually quite happy with my experience today. Seen the paramedic for an unusual ear infection with significant hearing loss last week, called up and was seen and out the door with a plan & prescription same day - despite the large queue on the phone in the morning. Booked and seen quickly on my follow-up to confirm that the infection is clearing ok and there are no other clear signs of other issues like a cholesteatoma which was raised as a concern during the first appt. I feel looked after and on the mend, that deserves a review in my eyes. I’ve even had calls relating to my long-term prescription requests to keep me up to date. Quite happy so far Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your positive feedback! This will be shared with the team. Kearsley Medical Centre

She undertook an examination and took my wife through all the potential medical issues that she maybe experiencing and potential solutions. Dr Ahmed would definitely be a great asset to the practice. 👏👏👏

reviews.author: Tom J
reviews.text: We only came here to ask for some help regarding CCTV and honestly, i have never come across a receptionist so rude, entitled and obnoxious. She was more concerned about making us put on face masks before engaging in any form of conversation, she stepped away to ask a manager about CCTV and then asked us to step aside to deal with other customers for us to then be simply told they couldn’t help us 10 minutes later - why not just inform us of that when you returned to reception from asking your manager? While we were waiting she was so bothered about this one gentleman’s mask being over his nose while and mouth while talking to him that she repeatedly couldn’t hear what he was saying and he was essentially sharing his personal business to the whole reception area as to why he was there. I felt so bad for the gentleman, completely unacceptable. This woman needs a masterclass in customer service and should learn how to talk to people in a polite manner minus the chip on the shoulder. After all, judging by the other reviews here it seems to be a regular occurrence! Do better Kearsley Medical Centre.

reviews.author: Joanne Harlow
reviews.text: I was in the Surgery this morning waiting to see a Paramedic for my Granddaughter... A lady came in(she looked in her 70's) and went to the receptionist ...people couldn't help but hear her describing how she had been feeling.. She said she kept having crushing pains in her chest and kept going all light headed and just didn't feel well at all, she asked to see or get an emergency appointment with a Doctor or an appointment for the next day, the receptionist said all the apps had gone and they were also booked up the rest of the week, The poor lady then said I'm OK now at this minute but it keeps happening... To that the receptionist said, well all I can do is put you down for a Doctor to ring you at some point today, I don't know what time but the Doctor will ring you... The lady said Thankyou and went. Now is it me or don't you think that this lady should of been seen straight away with what she was describing she was going through!... Meaning it could of been an indicator of a Heart attack!...(and no I'm not a bloody Doctor but come on) .. You seriously need to have a word with your receptionists and teach them a few things!... That's if you can be bothered!.... Absolutely disgusted!... And I wasn't the only one that felt like that!... You should be ashamed...

Having got up extra early by 7:45am and no Doctors call she eventually got through to be told a mistake had been made and they meant next Thursday, my partner explains to the receiptionest that that's no good as we will be away, she politely asks to speak to a doctor, shortly after she gets a message from Doctor saying there's no need for me to call you as there's nothing wrong with you!!!!! reviews.author: Courtney Nicole
reviews.text: If I could get away with giving 0 stars I would. As a new member of Kearsley Medical Centre i am extremely disappointed with the service I have received from them today! The receptionist who I came across this morning, at my appointment time was rude! Had the cheek to tell me I was late for my appointment after standing in the que for 5 minutes. Then rolled her eyes at me telling her, I didn’t have a mask. Then to have to go for a health check booked in prior to joining this practice, to have my blood pressure checked only and her staring at me for me to ask ‘are we done’ I must of been in the room not even 2 minutes. Was no health check at all. To then be told my repeat prescription from my old doctors had been sent to the pharmacy across the road (which they wouldn’t repeat the prescription until I saw the lady and had waited over a week for this appointment) to only be more disappointed going into the chemist and not being registered and having no prescription sent over!! Complete utter waste of time and nothing but disappointment! I’ve waited a week for an appointment to still not have my prescription (that I need asap) and to be looked at like you have a TV on your head. No communication and not professional one bit. On the bright side the only lady that’s a credit to the team and has been helpful over the phone is a lady called Jade.

reviews.author: Katie Himsworth
reviews.text: Just rang to make an appointment with a doctor and was told off by the receptionist for ringing at the wrong time. She told me i had to ring first thing in the morning and then went on to rant about the 40 appointments they had already booked. Im sorry but how am i supposed to know how many people have already rang! Also the phones are answered from 8am each morning, it was 8:30 when i rang. It doesn't tell you on the automated phone system that you have to ring first thing and it also doesn't say anything about ringing at certain times on the website. What happens if people are unable to ring at 8am sharp, what happens if the line is busy at 8am? I have a newborn at home who ive been up all night with, i managed to snatch an hours sleep from 7 to 8 am so i only just got the chance to ring at 8:30. I was made to feel stupid by the receptionist, i appreciate that they are busy but they shouldnt take it out on the patients. They need to update the automated phone system and the website to reflect the preferred ringing times that way people won't be faced with a ranting receptionist like i was.

I saw the MSK Practitioner Tracy Parry and asked to be referred as I was convinced that I had some kind of acute injury that hadn't been discovered. She refused to refer me. 8 months later it was discovered I had an undiagnosed fracture all along. To make matters worse, the practice manager Lauren Leckie simply abandoned my complaint to the surgery and failed to get back to me after promising she would. I have now been sent a letter by her deputy completely whitewashing the entire incident. I will be going to the PHSO as I think this is very serious. Walking on a broken foot for 20 months isn't fun.

He took on board her fear of being left in serious pain (sci) and explained to myself how the combination he was giving was better than the current pain meds. This allowed me to then go through it all with the patient once home ( she has memory issues ) and patient is happy with how she was spoken too, the empathy that was shown and also how the dr explained things, not only to the penitent but also to myself. He was firm but fair and has given the patient some confidence in any future visits that may be needed.

reviews.text: Booked appointment as both knees are playing up feel like they are pulsating and have given out on numerous times shoulder feels like its grinding on bone index finger has swollen and not gone down in 2 months yet felt like I wasn't being listened to gave me a piece of paper with some exercises are you kidding me im very active as is and the exercises on the paper im already doing as I've looked into these injuries myself and can even require surgery if not healing properly im lookingt ogo now to go private as I feel this place has lost all credibility

reviews.author: Jade Mary Marie
reviews.text: I had difficulty with my prescription, online services kept crashing Everytime I went on. I asked for a paper prescription when I picked my pick up, ( this medication is repeated) I was not given this, pharmacy explained to speak to gp. I phoned the pharmacy to say I've completely ran out of my inhaler, i definitely need an emergency today- go to Gp they said. Short story - refused to prescribe me a needed medication despite my explanation of I know it's not normally done on the phone etc but I'm having trouble. 9 times I rang them today going back and forth, I managed to get a pharmacy to help me and they rang the gp for me from their end told me to go to pharmacy at 5:30 prescription would through on the system. Arrived at the pharmacist no prescription ready, hasn't been sent through from gp side. I rang again the 11th time and explained the situation, told I had to wait for gp to sign of (perfectly understandable but told me it would be ready as a one off emergency) then proceed to tell it would be ready for 6 when the pharmacy they are sending it too closes at 6 I said if they close how I am supposed to get this emergency medication I've spent nearly 5 hours fighting to get. Long story short, I was spoken to in vulgar ways by more than one member of staff who accused me and the pharmacy i went to ;of lying. I got upset so my partner took over the call, getting no way, the pharmacy stayed open longer than needed to try and help but nothing, my partner expressed that what if I had an asthma attack or needed to go to a&e because I have no medication which they could of sorted out hours ago before and refused? Said it wasn't my problem 🤣 So basically saying jn a nut shell, if you can't breath or stop breathing, despite telling us you need medicine that we could have prescribed and prevented 5/6 ish ago it wasn't there problem. Imagine me sitting in A&e telling them I'm there because gp won't help me prescribe my medicine. I appreciate protocol and procedures, busy times etc, and I too add I am normally very on top of my medicine but on this occasion I have ended up with difficulties, ran out unexpectedly (being busy, didn't realize how low I was) but they had more than appropriate time to help me get some medicine, it wasn't five minutes before they shut. Absolutely applaud of the attitude I've received, the way I've been spoken to and the lack of curiosity and compassion. Blaming me for their failures and telling me it's all recorded like I'm in the wrong. Will be changing gp surgery asap

reviews.author: amy
reviews.text: Honestly this place is very good. Waiting times are a little long but that's a nationwide issue, not the surgery's fault. Helpful receptionists, knowledgeable, and honest when they are unsure of something. Always helped to point me in the right direction, and helped to send me to different doctors for separate issues. The Women's Healthcare specialist is fabulous, Dr. Karim is genuinely caring and a great listener. I really wish the staff here were given better facilities because they are a credit to this community. The pharmacists next door are so friendly and helpful too. Would have given 5 stars, but every GP service in the country is criminally underfunded, so naturally unable to reach their greatest potential.

reviews.author: vishal Sharma
reviews.text: Very poor service. I suggested to all that don’t be the part of that surgery. They will not be able to attend you. I did that mistake.

reviews.author: Michael Bell
reviews.text: You've got better chance of booking an appointment with a GP in the rainforests of Africa. My wife has spent 3 months trying to get an appointment because of her knee (which has gotten worse) and even as I write this review, she still doesn't have an appointment, She has been refered to an online Medical Forum with a consultation booked in 2 days to talk to a 'Medical Advisor (in Leeds). I'll be filing a complaint with GMC & CQC.

reviews.author: Maddy Wins

reviews.author: Anthony Smith
reviews.text: The receptionist was a rule to herself very snooty and told lies by saying my wife's prescription was not there yet after the bank holiday it was processed meaning my wife went a full weekend without medication i would score -10 if i could what a complete shambles this place is

reviews.author: harry capstan

reviews.author: Steven Maher

reviews.author: Elise Pattison
reviews.text: If I could leave 0 stars for this place I would. My mum who is a cancer patient had an appointment last week and arrived 20 minutes early for her appointment. The first bad thing to have happened was they gave her the wrong place to go to for her appointment, she asked for help from the receptionist (long blonde hair in a pony tail,and in her mid 30s) who was as useless as anything. The woman rudely told my mum how it was at a different doctors. My mum asked for help as her phone was dead and needed a taxi as she was still early and could have made it to which the woman said "you should really have your phone charged for these things as it makes my job easier". She was condescending, argumentative and falsely accused my mum of trying to pick a fight, and was happy to see a cancer patient stranded. She cancelled the appointment for no reason even tho she still had time to go and it's only because the pharmacist next door saw how upset my mum was that she helped her. The receptionist at the sister surgery was wonderful and reinstated the appointment and looked after her. If it hadn't been for her it would have been a disaster. To leave a patient stranded is disgraceful and people like that have no business working with sick and disabled people.

reviews.author: Ioana Rob
reviews.text: Worse reception service ever. She is just rolling eyes on my request for the second time. Over the phone the secretary was very helpful, but of course the receptionist has a rude attitude. Fiona was lovely, but the other receptionist is something else. She must change her job if she doesn’t like dealing with people. She didn’t have her badge on to see her name.

reviews.author: Adele Aspinall
reviews.text: This is a five star review for a lovely receptionist, who sorted out my medication problem out today, wish I had remembered her name. I was very stressed and she got everything sorted quickly. Thank you.

reviews.text: Words cannot describe how incompetent and how pathetic the services are from stonehill medical centre an independent enquiry should be carried out to highlight failings, reception staff arrogant unhelpfully I am sure their main goal is to prevent you getting through the door, doctors below par since Dr silvert left this place has just fell apart, Dr chowdary who is in charge just does not have a clue how to run a surgery the results speak for itself. reviews.author: Nichola MATTHEWS
reviews.text: Stonehill practice, has refused to provide face to face appointments to a disabled service with a visual impairment and several learning disabilities over three years, When the patient complained of lack of treatment and appointments. They deducted them from there surgery, failing to inform the patient, when they know the patient is unable to recognise words numbers and colours,fortunately they are being persued by judicial Review

reviews.author: Abi C
reviews.text: We couldn’t ask for a better Practice. I have consistently found all the reception staff to be efficient and very empathetic. Both the doctors and the nursing team deliver a highly professional service. Even during the height of the pandemic I was still proactively contacted by the practice for health prevention screening. I have always been given timely appts with the clinicians for my daughter and myself. If the phone lines are busy and you have to wait to be dealt with, it’s because the reception staff are dealing with another patient who needs that time to explain their problem. I am confident that when it’s your turn, you too will be given the time and responded to in a kindly manner. Stonehill has been our Practice for over twenty years and never once has the service they provide let me down.

reviews.author: Charlene Cunningham
reviews.text: Stonehill medical centre should not be in practice after contacting you after Christmas with an eye infection you diagnosed me with conjunctivitis over the phone! I had already told you I had been using the eye drops and didn’t work you didn’t listen you insisted I give them another try a week later I rang again yet again you refused to look at my eyes and tried to send me to an emergency optician there were no appointments! After another week I rang again 3rd time shock horror you gave me a face to face appointment you then diagnosed me with blepharitis today 2 days later I have ended up at Bolton a and e because the swelling on my face around my eyes has got worse today I was informed YOU should have prescribed me antibiotics as I have also got a skin infection which you failed to notice on my face to face appointment you should have looked at my eyes on day 1 of me contacting you instead you have allowed the infection to get worse you really are a horrible practice and I have now decided to complain through PALS I will also be contacting the ombudsman and register at at Frederick street as from what I’ve been told they have doctors that are qualified and actually want to help patients

reviews.author: Tom Kielty
reviews.text: Poor to say the least, after a phone appointment that took 2 weeks to happen was told they would book an appointment for me. No appointment booked except for a text to say call to book one. 7 times today Ive called and always 20+mins on hold. Gave up, no patient care whatsoever, absolutely disgusting practice

reviews.author: AB
reviews.text: Had to call the surgery twice this week with health concerns and have spoken both times to Jennifer. Just wanted to say thank you for being so understanding, caring and taking responsibility for the help that I needed, it was greatly appreciated 😄 …

reviews.text: There is nothing to share!!! Because you can't see them 😡😡😡 …

reviews.text: Contacted surgery and was told there where no in person or phone appointments available and to use online consult form. Did this and received text to say book an appointment. Now after 3 phone calls(tacking approx. 90 min.) I have a phone appointment on 15th Nov.this would not be acceptable service in any other setting.

reviews.author: Kian Baggaley
reviews.text: Called up due to severe earache and throat pain, they said it would have to be a routine appointment as I don’t have a fever despite being f advised by Babylon virtual GP that I needed antibiotics following a face to face assessment. The lady on the phone told me to fill out an online consultation as I’ll get seen to quicker, I have done this and have been told by the form to contact the practice directly as I need antibiotics and I now can’t get through. Shambles.

reviews.author: Kay Thomas
reviews.text: Absolutely appalling service. Long phone winded phone menu to spend over half an hour on hold to be told there are no appointments for a week when you are in agony and literally can't move and are told back pain (from an injury not just something thar is ongoing and they are already aware of) isn't a medical urgency. They would put a request in to doctor for some stronger tablets but no guarantee I would get any and if I did, it would be two days before they were ready. I had already explained that over the counter strength codeine wasnt touching the pain, which you aren't supposed to take for more than 3 days without seeing a doctor as they can become addictive, but what can you do if you have to wait a week for an appointment because you are told it doesn't warrant an emergency one? The "highly trained receptionist who can sign post you to the right course of action" asked no questions about whether there was any numbness or tingling in the legs etc (which could indicate something more serious). When I was having a miscarriage (which is an emotional enough situation as it is) I was told to "leave it a few days and ring back" so i just took myself to the early pregnancy centre at the hospital. No wonder so many people just turn up at A and E. They are going to miss something really serious with someone soon. You're reminded more than once that calls are recorded and they have the right to put the phone down on you, luckily I'm very calm but I can see why they put this on, they probably get so many people seething and making a fuss because the shocking service makes them feel worse when they are already ill! I emailed a complaint once but didn't even get a response. We are looking for an alternative GP surgery but dread ending up walking into something worse! I've spent many years working both reception and other customer facing roles so I am well aware of how hard it is sometimes dealing with the public, but I would certainly have been sacked by now if our service was so terrible. It's so sad and feels like nobody cares.......

reviews.author: debra coucill
reviews.text: Was told a sick note would be available after requesting it a week ago went to collect was told oh come back tomorrow argumentative snotty staff all sat doing nothing its the worst doctors I have ever been registered at in 40 years

reviews.author: charlie cornwell
reviews.text: this review is for my dad, after suffering for 2 years with stomach pain and being told nothing is wrong my dad eventually got an endoscopy on the 2 week rule , he was told chronic gastritis and lots of stomach damage, dr chowdry had brushed it aside for to long , looking for a new doctor now as this practice is just about making money and not patient care. a shame as when run by dr silvert it was one of the best.

reviews.author: Big Stevie B
reviews.text: A daily struggle. Dr Milner specifically looked like she'd just rocked up from a heavy nite. I've never experienced such conduct, unbecoming of a certified Doctor.....1 star is 1 star too many. reviews.author: Muhammad Abdullah 01
reviews.text: Last Friday, they called my mum to discuss my blood report here is what happened that very day: - they didn't give my mum details of my blood test results and didn't send it to my home by post.. - they also said to my mum" your son needs to give us consent to speak on his behalf and discuss the blood test report with you"... When my mother questioned about the blood test report and why they can't tell her anything about it... Absolutely Ridiculous....

reviews.author: Judith Hemming
reviews.text: My mother belonged to this medical centre. But stayed at Farnworth Care Home. I was told several times by an ambulance crew that they requested the doctors to visit my mother. That would not go and see her. I was disgusted and appalled by this. Even the hospital was not surprised at this. Previous to that the doctors at this surgery was requested to see my at the care home several times did not see her. It took four times for them to visit my mother. My mother died early this year. I would not recommend this place at all. Keep well away. They don't care about anyone especially people in care homes who cannot answer for themselves.

reviews.author: Kathryn Mulvaney
reviews.text: Phoned this morning for a routine appointment. As I have had trouble with the online procedure previously, I'd been told to contact by phone...which I did. I got a receptionist who told me to do it online. I tried to tell her what I was told before and could she book an appointment as I was speaking to her. She refused. She said I was using the wrong thing on-line. She had no patience or empathy at all. She only offered to tell me how to so it when I became exasperated with her. Some if the staff need some retraining in their telephone soft skills.

reviews.author: Indeeka Harwood
reviews.text: I phoned up to make an appointment for the family planning clinic, on Wednesday 25th March, to be then be told that they couldn't give me an appointment as the rota wasn't up for next week but to phone up on Friday (25th march). I phoned up on Friday and the lady on the phone was really nice and bared with me as signal was rubbish on my phone. But, I was told there was no appointments available until the 19th April but the rota again, wasn't up for that week yet. I just want a repeat prescription, never had an issue before but this taking the mick.

reviews.author: Ziyad Ilyas
reviews.text: An absolute poor run medical centre with inexperienced management structure and unqualified staff who clearly do not have the basic ability to communicate and complete patient requests Contacted the surgery on Wednesday to book my father who is unwell an appointment to then be rudely directed to "go check online" Replied back: Sorry but I have checked online first and there was no appointment available so I have rang through Replied well I ain't got any appointments for your father go and fill the online consultation form. And somebody "will be in contact within 48 hours" I then filled the consultation form and had to work from home for the proceeding two days in order to help my father facilitate the call (as he struggles expanding and explaining on the phone about his health)..... Suprise surprise no one contacted us within the 48 hours. After 48 hours: Rang to speak to the receptionist to clarify why I was not contacted to be informed rudely "well the duty doctor is very busy "we have other patients too you know not the end of the day you will be contacted by the end of the day" Comes towards the end of the day: (rang again - was on hold for 38 mins) RE Explained the above points to be told well we booked your father in on Tuesaday for an appointment face to face. How am I meant to know that my father has an appointment if no one contacted us to notify us? To be told well we messaged you.... utter nonsense I received no message and gave them my direct number to contact me... (excuses) No compassion no explanation..... Strongly strongly advice the reader(s) if you have anyone ill or frail in your family or have any complex medical needs (yourself) please consider joining eles where or think before joining this practice. The practice will not be able to meet your needs.... No wonder A&E (s) are over run... no GP appointments available. The Saga continues....

reviews.author: Lee Frost
reviews.text: Had an appointment this afternoon at 4.15 and was fobbed off when i asked (4.45 and again 5.20)how much longer it would be. I was then told i would get a call from the doctor at the end of his surgery. I got a call (1 ring ) and he immediately hung up!!!! What a joke this place is!!!

The Receptionist (didn’t catch her name) on today was so lovely too, she seemed so rushed off her feet but willing to help everybody!

reviews.text: After hours of being on hold, then passed back and forth from the pharmacist reception staff to the doctors receptionist we were really struggling with communication about a repeat perscription. Eventually we spoke to a receptionist at the doctors named Jacinta. What a pleasant, empathetic, sympathetic, caring person. Within in minutes she had resolved all our problems in a caring, proffesional manner. Can't thank or praise her enough.

reviews.author: Nick & Natalie Jones
reviews.text: Oh dear oh dear.... don't even know why I'm bothering leaving a review, nothing will change. Firstly their 'highly trained staff' - we're triage nurses now are we? Hmmmm. So i rang these folk half an hour before my appointment to say I was stuck in traffic. Once I got past autobot and into the queue at position 7, by the time I arrived at the surgery I asked the receptionist if their phones were manned; I'd dropped to position 2 after 40 minutes, no doubt because people were just hanging up. I won't say the young recpetionist was rude, or curt, or very direct, but she very much wanted me to know (wait for it, stock answer....) 'Yeah it's COVID, we're short staffed'. On the upside though, I have had a good few telephone conversations with a student doctor, a doctor, a senior nurse, so hey at least there's conversation going on. So I did actually manage to see a real human, success there. I know the NHS is having trouble but come on... sort it out. No doubt I'm blacklisted now for this review eh.

reviews.author: Cat Ann
reviews.text: Trying to book an appointment and they seem to intentionally give you days and times you are busy. Good luck if you are working, you won't be getting an appointment, or anything of use, but will be getting a lovely argument with the the receptionist. Waiting for over half an hour on the phone after 30 attempts to get through, just a massive waste of time. In fact, getting any help from this place is unlikely, at best they will send you to A&E. They will claim they have informed the A&E you are own your way and then when you get to the hospital, they will have heard nothing from them. Changes to medications without being contacted, refusal to switch them back. Medications will always be whats cheapest. Test results given over the phone by a receptionist, they will have no idea what the results mean and will suggest you "google it". I'd move doctors but farnworth is blessed with just this place, which is also connected to highfield.

reviews.author: Mike Garstang
reviews.text: Poor cant get appointments ever.wouldnt see 3 week old baby due to and quote as they said "covid" resulting in us taking her to a n e.neva answer phones went down to speak to somebody 3 receptionist sat behind desk yet being inside the surgery I found I never heard a phone ring once.🤔.must be the only doctors surgery where a phones doesn't ring. .not everybody is computer literate and they need to get rid of the online booking system I'm dyslexic and struggle. Partner still waiting for 6 week postnatal check after section. Baby is four months now and still waiting after being told dont call us we will call you. reviews.author: L W
reviews.text: I have been with this practice since childhood. I was with Dr Silvert at Farnworth HC. Firstly I have nothing but praise for the doctors and qualified health care staff.....if your lucky enough to get through the reception staff who seem to believe they are medically trained. I am a qualified health care professional with with 18+ years of frontline NHS experience, and never in all my career have I met reception staff who not only try to explain to me what could be causing my symptoms which in itself astounded me, but when I tried to explain that, the small amount of information she knew was not my only symptoms and I would like to speak to a practitioner, she became unbelievably rude. I have worked with many reception/ clerical staff in hospitals over the years but have never experienced service like this. It is not acceptable and I can only hope the practice manager puts further (much needed) training in place. And before you respond the same stock answer of "we have highly trained staff bla bla bla...." I urge you to listen to some of your recorded phone calls. Im sure they will be enlightening. Your front line staff who are the "face" of your surgery are rude and unprofessional.

reviews.text: Tried and tried to make a appointment, could not get past the receptionist, was so rude, she told me to book online, tried to do this and you need a username and a password and guess what you have to phone the receptionist for this. No wonder people are going to A&E.

reviews.author: Edward Walsh
reviews.text: My wife and I have been with Stonehill/Highfield Medical Centre for about 20 years now. reviews.author: Ellis Birtles
reviews.text: I have been a patient at this practice for over 10 years and unfortunately the quality of care has declined significantly. I have been suffering with rectal bleeding and recurrent abscesses for several years, and despite repeatedly asking for further investigation, I have consistently been dismissed. Last week I attended the surgery with heavy rectal bleeding. The doctor would not make eye contact, did not offer a chaperone before asking me to lie on the bed with my underwear down, and carried out no proper examination such as pressing on my abdomen. When I tried to explain my symptoms, I was told to leave the room for being “rude”, even though I was in distress. No help was given, and I was simply told to book another appointment six days later. Because of this, I contacted 111 who sent me to the hospital within an hour due to the seriousness of my symptoms. This is not the first time I’ve had to go through 111 or A&E because the practice would not help. Over the years, my abscesses have repeatedly been dismissed as “boils” and I have only been given mild antibiotics. I have now finally seen a dermatologist who believes my symptoms may be linked to inflammatory bowel disease, something I have been worried about for years but the practice refused to investigate. The reception staff often come across rushed and unfriendly, and I leave most interactions feeling patronised and unheard. Even when I raised my concerns with the practice manager, I felt dismissed again. All I want is to be listened to and to receive proper care. After years of pain, worry, and being ignored, I can no longer trust this practice with my health.
