From the moment you walk in or call, you’re greeted with ,professionalism, and genuine kindness. Nothing ever feels like too much trouble thank you so much Elaine.

reviews.author: gemma
reviews.text: Takes an age to get through on the phone. Receptionists often book you in for the wrong appointment, meaning you have to be turned away and re booked after scheduling time off work. This has happened to myself and my daughter on several occasions. Manager unavailable or does not return your call when wanting to address this issue. Two stars because some staff are friendly when you do get seen.

reviews.author: Matthew Hillyard
reviews.text: A terrible surgery, with incompetent/lazy receptionists, cannot believe the surgery has survived as long as it has... examples of incompetency, failing to book you in due to them being busy chatting resulting in a 40 minute wait that was never going to end. Abusing customers as they leave the surgery not realising that patients in the waiting room can hear. Calling me up with someone scan results and telling me the full results for me to reply "this isnt me?", zero data protection or any confirmation as to who I was before the confidential information was given... do not sign up here, if anything, it needs closing down or a full overhaul of front desk staff due to their incompetence.

reviews.author: Hristo Rankov
reviews.text: The surgery makes discrimination against my disability + some of reception staff and management been totally ignorant dealing with my personal data in unprofessional way, member of staff called Elaine been discriminating against my origins as obviously in not British. I notified IBC and ICO and will follow up to NHS England and the Ombudsman so hopefully they don't do that to anyone else.

reviews.author: Hannah Norris
reviews.text: I was 4 minutes late to my appointment and would have been happy to rearrange if needed but no one said a thing. Waited in the waiting room for 5-10 minutes after check in. Dr then called me through and said I was very late for my appointment to which i said I was 4 minutes late at most but I apologised and said thank you for seeing me. I gathered then that I wasn’t going to get anywhere with this dr as her attitude was disgusting towards me. She asked me if I did any exercise as to which I started explaining and she just cut me off and asked if I did any set exercise. I said if she would have just let me finish I would have told her. I mentioned that my mum who is a nurse had pointed out some changes on my bloods and had said I should go back to the drs if I was still having concerns. She then asked if my mum was a dr to which I replied no a nurse. At this she rolled her eyes while looking at her computer screen. She offered me no help other than things that I have already tried and just kept repeating there’s nothing wrong with you. I wouldn’t be at the drs if I genuinely thought I was ok. At this I got up and said I wasn’t having her attitude anymore and that she was no help and left the room. When I went to reception I politely asked if I could have a note on my record stating I did not wish to see that dr again. The receptionist then stated that this is yet another dr I do not wish to see. I will point out that the other dr I did not wish to see told me to get over my depression and to just get on with it when I went for a review of my mental health/medication. So yes I do not wish to see a dr that doesn’t take my mental health seriously. Back to today I was left feeling utterly hopeless and that I cannot go to this surgery again. They have some lovely drs, nurses and receptionists at this surgery but when you are not listened to and just made to feel unheard it doesn’t fill you with confidence in the surgery itself.

reviews.author: Bethany Cowley
reviews.text: Came in for an appointment Wednesday evening, I usually find the staff to be quite pleasant however, tonight I spoke with the receptionist Elaine who I found to be quite rude and not very approachable. Not great customer service at all, attitude was not very nice.

reviews.author: Hristo Rankov
reviews.text: There is a new system to book appointment because of which the surgery started open discrimination against me as for some stupid reason I'm unable to book appointment online and they are saying go to Fairfield hospital instead, I think is time to get a solicitor and sue and change the surgery of course...

reviews.author: Amy Bicknell
reviews.text: So hit and miss depending on who answers the phone. Last week rang just after 8am, selected the appointments line and after a 30 min hold got through and got an appointment the same day. Do exactly the same today to be met with quite a hostile tone from Elaine in that I should have filled in the form on Ask my Gp. I wasn't aware this was the procedure given I've always secured an appointment by ringing. I explain I got one last week by ringing and just get told well I shouldn't have. No, apologies that was our fault, our procedure isn't actually to do that etc. When you're a tired mum who's been up all night with an uncomfortable baby (and even when you're not) a kind and empathetic tone goes a long way compared to being 'told off'

reviews.author: Edit Olah
reviews.text: I have a 14 weeks old baby boy. Ive been to the GP 4 times to have “his 8weeks check up and immunisation” First appointment was in 24 October when he was 8 weeks old! I went to the GP and been sent home saying the Nurse is not there and they booked him in 4weeks later on the 24 November without letting me know! In Bury its Woodbank Surgery. Then i came back on the 24th November but been sent home with my 14 weeks baby as they didnt book him in with the right person! I told them that i was supposed to see MrsJoanne Clarkson thats was in my text message! On the same they 30 minutes later the Practicioner Nurse Mrs Joanne Clarkson rang me asking if im still at the reception with my baby because she was supposed to give him the 8weeks injections “ she obviously knew im not there thats why she rang!” I told her that Ive been sent home but they booked him back in for tomorrow “25 November” so i asked her if she can give him those injection tomorrow and she said No because she fully booked! .Then went back on 25th Nov at the GP i told at receptionnto let Joanne clarkson know that my son is there so if she has time she can give him those injections! He was seen by a Dr but no injections as its only the nurse does and they said “she is not in” so i still had to go back 2 days later just for an injection! He was supposed to get when he was 8 weeks 12 weeks and next will be 16 weeks. My son is 14 weeks old! And he only has 8weeks injection! I am a single Mom i dont drive im walking and had to go to gp 4times just to have a 2 minutes job done should have been done when he was 8weeks old!!! Very dissapointed! Worst Gp ive ever been! They dont care about babys! I hope the Managger read this and will do Something about it!!!

reviews.text: Poor service

reviews.author: Luke Hayat
reviews.text: This place is very strange, I asked for medical reports for my wife's daughter at the end of January. I was told it could take up to 24 days. 4 months later and still nothing. Every time I go back to enquire about it I'm told sorry and it's going to be next week when it's ready. My wife also had to have her private parts looked at, the doctor needed assistance, and got it from a receptionist that didn't have a clue. It felt very awkward and unprofessional. It has to be the strangest doctor's I've ever seen. Definitely would not recommend.

reviews.author: Lauren Douglas-Holt
reviews.text: I’ve been registered at this GP since birth but recently it’s become a disgrace. I requested my son’s prescription a week ago and it’s not been approved - it’s prescription formula so he needs it to eat! Tried ringing for the last 2 days and no answer just a queue that never goes down. My son has a medical condition that no doctors have any knowledge on so they’re relying on google. I went myself for an appointment and the doctor had to google when I next needed my vaccination. AskmyGP is useless it can take a week for a response. Will be switching ASAP because they can’t be relied on especially when my son needs medication and formula!

reviews.author: Hajra Mirza
reviews.text: Receptionist

reviews.author: Anne Needham

Special mention must go to the lovely Jen and the team on reception and Nurse Lisa for care and compassion and the times they have gone the extra mile. Over the last 2 days we have both received absolutely outstanding care, with immediate attention to resolve medical issues. We are so very grateful for the excellent service from all concerned with the Practice.

reviews.author: Claire Willan

reviews.text: Moved to this practice a few years ago in the last year fell ill prior to this they were brill loads of appointments after falling ill they have done nothing but look after me real good professional practice run by lovely people Went on holiday to Blackpool and got bitten by a horse fly phoned the doctors and did ask my gp with in an hour I had antibiotics sent to a pharmacy in Blackpool What a great service and great guys looking after us thank you so much your all awesome Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your review!

From my experience, the NHS is performing a brilliant service, and I applaud and thank the efforts of all those people involved in the process. Thanks Woodbank. Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your review!

reviews.author: Shaun Leonard
reviews.text: Title: Exceptional Care and Support at My GP Surgery! I have been a patient at my GP surgery for the past five years, and I cannot speak highly enough about the exceptional care and support I have received. The staff at this practice are truly remarkable - kind, friendly, and always willing to go the extra mile to meet your needs. From the moment you step through the door, you are greeted with a warm and welcoming atmosphere. The reception staff are incredibly friendly and efficient, ensuring that your paperwork and appointments are handled seamlessly. They make you feel valued and cared for right from the start. The medical professionals at this practice are second to none. The doctors and nurses are not only highly knowledgeable, but they also possess a genuine empathy and concern for their patients. They listen attentively, take the time to understand your concerns, and provide thorough explanations and treatment options. What sets this GP surgery apart is their exceptional response time. Whenever I've needed assistance, whether it's booking an appointment or seeking medical advice, the staff have always been prompt in their response. They understand the importance of timely assistance and make it a priority to address your needs efficiently. Overall, my experience at this GP surgery has been outstanding. The staff's dedication to providing compassionate care, combined with their efficiency and responsiveness, makes them a standout choice for anyone seeking reliable healthcare services. I wholeheartedly recommend this practice to anyone in search of a top-notch GP surgery. Thank you to the entire team for consistently delivering such exceptional service. Your commitment to patient care is truly commendable! Mr Leonard - Woodhill Bury. Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Thank you for your review!

reviews.text: Shocking. I have been a patient at this surgery for over 30 year it has gone downhill rapidly As myGP is another Joke. reviews.text: I joined this practice 3 years ago and have found the GP staff including the former practice manager "Lisa Gregory" to be very unhelpful. He often drew pictures to hand into the reception desk and he often discussed patient' cases over the reception desk. Because I am a patient on benefits with an Aneurysmal Bone Cyst of the clivus, I missed 3 appointments due to insufficient funds with my Neuro consultant because a locum refused to book patient transport, accused my friend of being confrontational and told me that the only people entitled to patient transport are the elderly. Atfer receiving letters stating that I have been missing my appointments, I had a mental breakdown with my depression and requested that I be referred to a therapist, however the referral never left the surgery. The nursing and reception staff are absolutely lovely however the GPs and former practice manager are horrendous. I have no opinion on the current practice manager however only time will tell. I am extremely reluctant to give this review even one star.

reviews.text: Ive been with this practice since the day I was born. Im now 74 this year. I remember walking over to the practice when it was in a big house on Tottington Road with my mum when we were kids and had measles etc. Our Drs were old Dr Garson and Dr Mcguinn. Both really polite and respectful. Ive got nothing bad to say about this practice as I have had nothing but kindness and respectfulness from young Dr Garson, Dr Siegler, Dr Chacko and Dr Hubber. And all the nurses. Everyone ive spoken to on reception have all been lovely and always ready to help with appts. etc. I wont have a bad word said about them. I find if you are polite and respectful towards people you will get the same back. They are all working under very bad conditions. Yvonne Ashworth. Bury Lancs. Practice response date: 10 months ago Practice response: Thank you so much for your thoughtful and heartfelt feedback, Yvonne. It's truly special to hear about your long-standing relationship with the practice and your memories going back so many years. We're really pleased to know that you’ve consistently experienced kindness and respect from our team, and we’re grateful for your recognition of the challenges faced in general practice today.

reviews.author: Matthew Bentley
reviews.text: They're not so bad maybe a little over run? I had told them that I was desperate , threatened self-harm and suicide and they simply ignored my calls for my meds. The practice manager is the person you complain to and these individuals are a certain type of person. They think they are higher than any GP. Couldn't diagnose my depression and in their words "just smile more" and "what you depressed for your just a kid". Had a spot problem being a teenager gave me an alcohol liquid which actually burnt like anything and told to come back in 6 months. Went back 6 months later, I said it wasnt working and was just burning my skin. Got told it was working and to come back 6 months later. Sacked off the alcohol stuff and bought some proactive plus 2 weeks later my spots where gone. Had a telephone conversation about my toe, that turned out was a fungal infection, but without even seeing it was adamant that I had "banged my toe" I hadn't. Bought some fungal infection treatment 1 week later the toe had gotten better. Went with a back problem 12 months of its a UTI its a kidney infection went to the hospital to be diagnosed as "drinking too much water" had a white blood cell count in my urine of 745. Which aparantly the normal amount is 20. Also had given me high doses of pain killers to just mask the pain in which they claimed was due to "crushed kidneys". Turns out my back issues was due to a crooked spine and I'm now seeing a chiropractor after no doctor could actually deal with it. I've been to about 4 different doctors . I've currently had 5 sessions with my chiropractor and I can actually no walk more than 10 minutes without being in constant pain. There are many more issues, but these are the ones that stick the most, also I could rarely see my actual assigned doctor and was just sent to any random person who couldn't diagnose anything.

The nurse who recommended morphine without any risk assessment is left to carry on.The GP also to blame but the Palliative Nurse a danger and she turned my life and partners upside down The people of Bury deserve better and please stay away from heartless and arrogant nurses and doctors ., that is those who give morphine out like it was toffees. I hope that Bury Palliative Care Team under a new trust will have risk assessments in place for vulnerable clients. But please be aware that they are not necessarily on the side of the patient, client and family. reviews.author: Faiz ul Haq
reviews.text: I would like to leave negative feedback regarding Dr. Hussain’s behavior at this surgery. Whenever we ask him for medicine, even for our small children, he always responds by saying: “Go and pick it up from the shelf.” Most recently, my wife, who is pregnant, needed medicine. Whenever she calls, despite the language barrier, Dr. Hussain should at least try to understand that a patient is in need of proper medical advice and prescriptions. Instead, he simply tells her to “get it from the shelf.” I want to ask: if we always have to buy medicine directly from the shelf, then what is the point of having a doctor or a surgery? What role is he fulfilling? During the last call, my wife explained that the medicine he had prescribed previously did not help her at all. She requested an alternative. Instead of listening, Dr. Hussain told her she must not be using the medicine properly. My wife clearly said she knows how to take it, but it was ineffective. At that point, Dr. Hussain disconnected the call and again told her to “buy it from the shelf.” This behavior is extremely unprofessional, dismissive, and rude—especially towards a pregnant woman and parents with small children. A doctor should listen carefully, show empathy, and provide proper medical guidance. Unfortunately, Dr. Hussain’s attitude shows the opposite. I strongly believe that this kind of conduct is unacceptable within the NHS. If doctors are not willing to provide proper medical care and instead simply tell patients to “buy from the shelf,” then they are not fulfilling their responsibility as healthcare providers. I will also be submitting a formal complaint to the NHS regarding this matter. In my opinion, Dr. Hussain should consider retirement, as he does not treat patients with the respect, care, and professionalism that is expected from a doctor.

I suffer mental health issues so it is very easy for me to say no when it actually is. 3 times I have had an appointment that they didn't write down what had happened in the appointment so the next one they didn't have a clue what was going on. The doctors have messed with my meds 4 times without consulting the hospital. Absolutely useless! I'm currently looking for a new doctors. They really don't care for their patients.

reviews.author: margaret miller
reviews.text: Over the last few months I have needed a few appointments. To my surprise these appointments have been easy to get. Usually I phone between 8 and 9am, I've been number 1, 2 or 3 in the queue, but, I have still been given an appointment for the same day. For non urgent appointments, these have been offered at alternative times at Moorgate, which is helpful for work purpose. I have seen a few different doctors and each and every one of them has been lovely, efficient and responsive to my needs. They always have time to listen to you and wish you well. I've never felt rushed. The nurses who run the clinics and do bloods etc are so nice, it's good to chat and laugh with them. The office staff are always polite and ready to help if they can. The young man on reception has improved over the last couple of years. It's a good medical centre, though could do with decorating and making it feel a bit more welcoming.

reviews.author: Gabberdabberdoo
reviews.text: I have recently had to change my GP after 30 years of being with Huntley Mount. This was due to so many things going wrong with this practice the last couple of years. The main problem is the male receptionist who usually answers the phone. It always feels like he’s not listening and several times he has told me “we’ll look into that for you” and tried to end the call without even asking for my name. I also called the surgery when I became pregnant a year ago and was told that Bury residents have their antenatal care at Oldham and given the link to register with Oldham hospital which is incorrect. This mistake ended in me having to transfer my care to North Manchester late in pregnancy and only getting my first midwife appointment at 32 weeks pregnant. I have also had nurse appointments made for me at the surgery when I needed a GP appointment, resulting in the nurse calling me to say she doesn’t deal with that and me having to call the surgery to rebook. Another problem I’ve had is that I paid for the doctor to fill in some travel insurance forms for me and waited 2 months to receive them back. I chased them up several times, once being told they were waiting for a member of staff who comes in once a week to do paperwork - then the next week being told it had been passed to Dr Butt. Several times I chased them up and they said they’d be ready in a few days and never got back to me. I even attended the surgery in person one time for an update and after looking in the computer the receptionist told me they were waiting for me to have my nurse appointment for my immunisations for travel - I asked what this was for as the forms I needed were for a holiday cancellation (to a country I would not need to have jabs for - Spain!) and he seemed totally confused. It seems they lost the forms for a few weeks but kept making up excuses to hide that. I understand how busy the GP is, but I don’t think they should be picking up what they call “private work” if they don’t have the spare time to be doing it. I could’ve paid an actual private doctor to do it for me within a couple of days. The running of the surgery seems to be a complete mess which is a shame as I have been with Huntley Mount for most of my life and have only recently started to have problems. I am already getting much better service at another surgery and I only changed over to them a week ago.

reviews.author: Lilliana
reviews.text: Lovely GP practice with amazing staff and services! The one star complainers below have so much entitlement it’s unbelievable 😂 how about you trying working in an NHS service and see how you get on? It’s not easy and the staff are doing their best to cater to your needs, however they are not miracle workers. There is only so much they can do, you should appreciate whatever it is that they can offer. If you have to wait for something, you have to wait, end of story, and this is for ALL medical practices, no matter where you go. And if you’re rude to staff, how else are they supposed to respond? They do their best to be professional with you and offer their support but you’re not happy with it? Sounds like a you problem. If you’re that entitled and think you deserve higher treatment than anyone else, go somewhere else. I guarantee you the next practice you go to won’t tolerate your behaviour either. As for GP appointments, they only do them on the day and don’t pre-book them like other practices do because then they won’t have a back log of appointments. You’re lucky to even get them on the day! My previous practice never had appointments for a GP available for at least two months because of all the patients they had pre-booked! You would be complaining a hell of a lot more if this practice did the same thing, which thankfully they do not. NHS 111 is always an option if you don’t manage to get an appointment. Honestly none of you know what you’re talking about (evident in the way that a majority of you one star reviewers can’t even spell) so if you’re that unhappy, transfer somewhere else. The staff here don’t deserve your awful attitudes and complaints. Best GP in Bury!

reviews.author: Leanne K
reviews.text: I've always been made to feel welcome at this practice and received the highest level of care, that's from the reception staff and nurses, right through to the GP's who are fabulous. Dr Butt in particular, I find to be a very kind and caring doctor, who I feel understands my history and despite his very busy practice, seems to remember me and my medical background. In the few years I have been with this practice, I've never received anything but the highest care and been treated with kindness and respect. I have moved house since originally registering, so the practice is not as close as it was, but I haven't / wouldn't want to move to a different / closer GP practice, simply because the care my baby boy and I receive here, is second to none. I don't envy the staff here though, as it can be a difficult environment to work in. On several occasions I have witnessed them having to deal with some very difficult / rude patients, but I have always found that even under pressure, they are consistently polite and helpful. I am a busy working mum in a senior leadership role in Manchester centre, so it's not always easy for me to take time off work or make a f2f appointment even when I need to, so I have always appreciated the fact telephone appointments can be available. However, recently, when I have been particularly poorly and needed to be seen & checked over, they booked me in and a GP saw me at short notice. Even during Covid, when I gave birth to my baby boy, I was worried about a lump developing on the back of his skull. Face to face appointments weren't taking place at that time, however when I brought him in for his routine vaccines, Dr Butt ensured he came out in between his appointments to check over my newborn and alleviate any concerns I had. Again, nothing but the highest level of care from all staff at every touch point, phone, reception, nurses and doctor. I wouldn't go anywhere else. Thank you to all at Huntley Mount. Leanne S

reviews.author: Ivona Rykaczewska
reviews.text: Horrible experience. I've been told by the doctor not to book emergency appointments when my baby is unwell (usual appointment waiting time 2-3 weeks) and find advise for treatments online instead (baby had 39.6 temperature for 3 days). On multiple occasions I have been told to take my 1 year old to a&e, without getting her seen by gp (the case of high temperature and strong cough), this also left hospital workers questioning the situation. I've been joked at when booked two appointments (for 2 different problems) on the close up dates 'Again you, I just seen you yesterday'. One of the receptionists has her input as well, by either refusing the appointment as unnecessary or telling 'how did you left it for so long?' and this is not in the appropriate polite tone I would expect this to be asked if that is the part of their job. Overall, no compassion or understanding of situation, no patience to explain or sometimes even to listen out the problem. I've once been asked 'So what it might be you think?' after describing the symptoms. I developed an anxiety and am afraid to seek help due to this place. Avoid it if you can.

reviews.author: Daira-Emma Hopwood
reviews.text: No sense of urgency whatsoever. The staff often treat your healthcare like it's an unimportant afterthought; you have to pester them to do their jobs again and again and again. I cannot count the total time wasted waiting for them to handle paperwork or send test results. I'm trans and have ADHD. It took months and months of back-and-forth between me, my private ADHD healthcare provider, and this practice to get the tests and info needed before I could be prescribed ADHD meds, and the delays were almost all on the side of this practice. Some of the receptionists are extremely rude, especially when handling phone calls. I know that's probably a rubbish part of the job for them, but the alternative would be trying to get stuff done in 10-minute GP appointments each of which takes 3 weeks to get, which is hopeless. They had no over-the-phone prescription ordering and no in-person GP appointments for a long time during the pandemic, which is extremely ableist and probably broke the Equality Act. (I get the risks of in-person appointments, but it could have been done safely when needed.) None of the staff wear masks, which casts doubt on both their competence and their empathy with clinically vulnerable patients. (This review is in April 2023, but they also haven't done so for most of the pandemic so far.) The GPs are often exasperating. They don't listen and need to be told everything. Being trans I'm used to essentially having to be my own doctor and tell the GP what they need to do, but it's exhausting, and it is worse with this practice than several others I've been enrolled with. The best I can say is that they haven't, as far as I can tell, been actively and intentionally transphobic to me; they're just so slow at doing anything that it feels like it. But that's just the NHS for trans people these days, I guess :-( When you're actually in an appointment, the GPs I've seen here (Dr Faizy is the one I've had most contact with) are quite personable and not too obstructive, modulo the above issue with you needing to do their jobs for them a lot of the time. I have occasionally got good healthcare from this practice. If that were all there is to providing a GP practice then I guess it would be fine. The lack of organisation, and as I said, any sense of urgency in the practice as a whole lets it down, and I can't recommend that anyone enrol here.

reviews.text: Having moved from Essex to Manchester, I’ve done my due diligence to find a highly rated GP service, I signed onto Vallance Medical, and I believe in giving praise when it’s due. I have never come across a surgery so helpful and efficient whilst remaining highly professional. If you ring up to speak to a doctor, they usually ring you back within 30 minutes. They are warm and caring in their approach and if needed, offer you a same day face to face appointment. Where necessary, doctors will phone you with results from tests too. Since moving to Manchester, I have had to ask for a referral to the wheelchair service, which was done immediately - nothing is too much trouble for them. I think this can-do attitude filters from the top down. The courteous receptionists are not like Dragons trying to block your path from seeking medical attention, in fact it is the reverse, they are always trying to help you connect with whatever service you need and have good communications with the in-house pharmacy. In conclusion, I know I will be leaving Manchester within a year and if one could (which I know you can’t) I would travel from Essex to Manchester just to see this medical practice - they are without doubt, the best practice and as a professional who has worked in the NHS for over thirty years, I cannot praise them enough. Maria Conyers

reviews.author: samrita shankar
reviews.text: MEDICAL NEGLIGENCE! After having a horrible experience with Robert Darbishire Practice, I registered with Dr. Ngan and Partners in February 2023. At first, I was very impressed with how quickly I was able to get appointments with the doctors. However, things quickly took a turn for the worse. 1. A severe and persistent headache started on 2nd February 2023 and lasted for the whole of the month. This headache did not subside with any medications, even those for migraines. I then had two telephonic consultations with Dr. Ngan and Partners during which time the doctor agreed that it was probably a sinus headache and not a migraine. He prescribed sinus related medications both times, but the pain did not reduce. By this time three weeks had passed since the headache had started. I informed the doctor that the pain was excruciating and had me bedridden most of the time. I also requested the doctor for an MRI or CT scan during the second consultation but this request was denied. I was also not referred to a neurologist or an ENT specialist despite the nature, duration and intensity of the headache. 2. I also informed the doctor that I had visited the ER earlier in the month as the pain worsened but could not see the doctor due to the long waiting time, hoping this would convey how severe the headache gets sometimes. 3. I contacted Dr. Ngan and Partners for the third time on 24th February and got an in-person appointment for the same day. After conducting physical examinations, the doctor diagnosed it as a migraine and prescribed a migraine medication AGAIN, even after I told her that literally no medications were working. I requested for an MRI or CT scan referral twice during the consultation but my request was denied for the third time! She said "there is nothing specific that we are looking for that would turn up in the scans". Instead, she said she would refer me to a neurologist if the headache persisted for a few more days. By this time, it was the start of the 4th week since the headache had started. 4. On 26th February 2023, I had to call an ambulance as the pain exponentially increased, so much so that I felt like my right eye was about to pop out! I had fever and vomiting. I was told that because my vitals, etc., were normal, they will not be able to take me to the ER. I called Dr. Ngan on 27th hysterically crying and explained my situation. I requested for an urgent consultation with the doctor but was told that there was no possibility of getting an appointment that day or the next as all slots were full. 5. I told the doctors that I was first on Co-codamol as prescribed by the previous GP but the intensity reduced. I was then asked to use Ibuprofen during first consultation with Dr. Ngan. During the last consultation I told the doctor that I had been on Ibuprofen for 10 days straight but she still asked me to use it to control pain. 5. Having felt completely and utterly abandoned by the GP, I had to fly home, to India, on 28th to receive urgent medical treatment. It was a gruelling 22 hours of travel during which the pain almost killed me! Upon investigation after getting admitted in India, it was found that I had a rare and an extremely severe infection in the Sphenoid sinus. The scans revealed that the infection had progressed so much that if I had waited for a few more days to get treated, I would have lost vision in my right eye or suffered brain damage! The infection had broken down the wall between the sinus and the brain and had started seeping into the brain, and the only way out was to have an immediate surgery. I was also told that the constant use of the painkillers prescribed by the GP was the reason why I had started puking blood on 28th February. 6. PATIENT HISTORY MATTERS! I had told the GP that I had suffered a scuba diving injury in 2020 after which I suffered similar headaches. However, this was completely ignored. The doctors in India found out through scans that this infection had likely started after this incident, with its final trigger starting in 2023.

reviews.author: Mella
reviews.text: If I could leave 0 or minus stars, I would. Changing to this practice due to catchment area was the worst decision of my life, they have stopped my healthcare without any follow up for the past 8 months. The receptionists have to call their higher ups who are offline by 2pm, although I have not been assisted in urgent and emergency situations. Taking off someone’s daily psychiatric medication is a breach of duty of care. Can you imagine your daily medication being taken away from you suddenly? Calling every single 111 line you can possibly imagine, taking days off work, experiencing withdrawal? A GP should never endanger the life or health of a patient. Suddenly, ailsa Craig cares about the law and guidance they operate under. For 8 months, they have not while I’ve been in their care. Unacceptable behaviour from every single member of staff who allowed this to happen. My health had become a toy to play with daily apparently, at the mercy of a GP who cannot ask for a piece of paper in 8 months. If you need to change your GP and you’re on psychiatric medication, do not go for Ailsa Craig. Be careful with every practice in Longsight and ardwick as they don’t prescribe it and likely won’t bother to involve the specialists needed on time. Double triple check everything when you change and write it down/ record it if needed for later. Experiencing immense pain that requires this lifesaving medication which I’m being denied is disgraceful. Doctors (Dr Bates) and the clinical pharmacist (Tracy Chong) give me conflicting and wrong information. I can only hope my complaint will be dealt with enough seriousness and that I can receive the bare minimum. Practice response date: 8 months ago Practice response: Thank you for your feedback. I want to assure you that I have received your complaint and am currently investigating the matter. Due to the sensitive and personal nature of your concerns, a public forum may not be the best place to discuss specific details. I will be in touch in due course with the outcome of my investigation. Kind regards, Karen Cullen

reviews.text: I have to say that the staff are mostly good. My gripe is how the practice is run and for whose benefit. One has to phone 8am but the lines are constantly busy. The receptionists advise that if you don't manage to get to phone at 8.00 then go to a walk in clinic, call NHS 111 or go to A&E. The question that I pose is that if I am a patient of the practice and the practice gets NHS funding for me, then why am I being directed to alternative places. Even during the day if one calls on the phone the caller is placed in a queue to go on the practice queue. This can be up to 30 minutes. My needs are very simple. Practice response date: 2 years ago Practice response: Hi Md, thank you for taking the time to leave feedback. The standard NHS GP appointment time is for only 10 minutes and in this short amount time GPs have to establish the problem, diagnose the illness and advise/prescribe and/or refer the patient. If the problem is complex or the patient arrives with many problems, whilst the GP may be happy to discuss these, they may also decide that it would be better for the patient to book a further appointment so that each of the problems can be given its own individual attention rather than several problems all vying for the same amount of time as one. I'm sorry If you feel that this was not explained to you during your appointment. I have shared your comments with our practice team. If you wish to discuss this further, please do not hesitate to contact me. Kind regards Karen Cullen, Practice Manager

reviews.text: Majority of my experiences in this GP have been good including receptionist and nurses. I actively leave them good feedback on follow up text. Moans about having to print off my results but HAS TIME TO MAKE TEA WHILST PATIENTS WAIT IN THE RAIN. Don't kid yourself that putting 2 chairs outside mean you got some sort of waiting area. She says you need to provide 2 days notice to get a printout. It's the 21st century but this receptionist has probably been around since the pyramids were being built. Practice response date: 3 years ago Practice response: Dear Salman. Thank you for your review. We are doing our very best to ensure that everyone is seen on time where possible, reducing the need to wait outside for long periods of time. With regards to our experienced reception staff, during busy periods it is not always possible to leave the reception unattended to carry out admin requests for print out of medical records and we actually ask for up to 30 days to complete these requests, the request form can be found on the website and/or at reception. We strive to provide the best possible patient care and I am sorry that it was felt that we were not able to do so on this occasion. I will take your comments to our next meeting where we discuss patient reviews and suggestions. Kind regards Karen Cullen

reviews.text: I was with this medical centre for 4 years whilst I was at uni. The receptionists are great and the nurse is good. In relation to the two doctors there - Dr Garson and Dr Locham - I would say this. First, I used Dr Garson: he seems to be a competent doctor, at least this was the impression I got from a few phone appointments I had with him. However, when I had my first virtual video-appointment (due to Covid-19) he disappointed me for his lack of manners. This is because I had more than one health issue to report/get his advice on, and as soon as I finished the first one and moved to the second, he said: 'now, we will treat this issue, and once this is sorted, you can talk about the others', and when I was trying to explain that they were related, he basically closed down the video-appointment on my face (just like that!). After this, I changed my GP to Dr Locham. However, this GP also has a problem: he rushes you like he needs to catch a train ASAP! This is particularly unpleasant when you are trying to explain a difficult health issue and he interrupts you and makes you feel like you are wasting his time. So, if you have other options and do not fancy being mistreated or rushed through, maybe look elsewhere. Having said that, both seem to be knowledgeable doctors though.

reviews.author: Junaid Ahmed
reviews.text: As a long-term patient (diagnosed with a life time illness since 2005) receiving continuous prescriptions and specialized care, I requested a paid private letter confirming the simple, medically accepted fact that chronic stress and hardship trigger flare-ups to my condition. The practice refused the request, claiming "insufficient evidence" a shocking statement considering my two decades as a patient for whom they have continuously prescribed, medication, are informed of my hospital ongoing treatment for years (Vedolizumab, etc.) and liaised with the hospital IBD team. This refusal demonstrates a failure to understand the patient they are treating. Crucially, this contradiction occurred even though I attached an older letter from my specialist consultant where this clinical fact was already written and acknowledged. This extreme administrative obstacle wasted significant time and energy, forcing me to change GPs due to their unwillingness to support a chronic patient. Practice response date: a month ago Practice response: Thank you for your review. We are sorry to hear this and if you wish to discuss further please contact the surgery. However of note , private letters are at the discretion of the GP and are outside of NHS work and therefore these do not need to be completed by the GP. This is stated on the website.

reviews.author: JUNAID AHMED
reviews.text: I was a long-term patient with multiple chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, arthritis, and migraines — all of which were regularly managed through prescriptions and hospital treatments. I requested a simple private letter confirming my diagnosis and how stress can affect my condition — something a hospital consultant had previously provided. Despite being willing to pay the £35 fee, the practice refused to provide the letter and didn’t offer an appointment to discuss it. As someone managing serious long-term health issues, I found this response dismissive and lacking in basic patient support. I’ve since moved to a new GP who I hope will be more patient-focused. I’m sharing this to help others understand what kind of support they might — or might not — receive here if they have complex or ongoing health needs. To the management: the decline in care became noticeable after COVID. If you’re genuinely reviewing patient experiences, it may be worth examining the internal changes made during and after the pandemic — because that’s when the ship started sinking.

They begin to loudly start trying to locate the doctor saying he never told anyone that he’s not going to be in and that he has appointments. They ring him and surpise surpise he’s not in, even though they 1- gave us the appointment with him, 2- rang at 1pm to confirm that it’s with him and 3- didn’t realise until 5 minutes before the appointment that he’s not even in. They then tell us sorry your appointments cancelled come back tomorrow. My husband has a foot infection and is already in pain, was hard enough to come the first time never mind coming again. Anyways we get an appointment the next day, the dr was good and took her time to check it thoroughly, spoke to other doctors took a swab and prescribed antibiotics. She even called back a few hours later and gave more advice. Can’t fault her at all, it’s the receptionists that give this place a bad name. The dr was told by someone whilst we were there to not send prescriptions to wise pharmacy as it’s closed due to the police blocking off the road. So she sends the prescription to Manchester pharmacy instead. We get to Manchester pharmacy and it’s also closed so we ring the gp back to let them know, the receptionist just says oh wait for tomorrow, not considering infections get worse without treatment, we tell her we need the antibiotics she says try a different pharmacy. We go to Asda pharmacy and they say ur gp needs to cancel it first then we can dispense. Rang gp AGAIN she just says oh no we can’t cancel it. We end up going to another pharmacy and they call the surgery themselves and got it cancelled. It took us 4 hours of running around just to get some antibiotics, absolute joke.

reviews.text: Where do I start with this place. Anyway I put in a repeated prescription on line on a Monday, went to pick it up from the pharmacy on the Thursday (Bearing in mind it should take 2 days to receive). I got to the Pharmacy only for them to tell me that this Medical center didn't send over the prescription. I called the so called Medical Center to see why my prescription was not processed. After a long time trying to get through to the receptionist I had to repeat my DOB nearly 6 times. I asked why they never sent my prescription over and she said it's because I need a review but she will get the Doctor to ring me back. The Doctor rang back and we made arrangements for me to get my prescription the following morning. To cut a long story short, l went back to the Pharmacy the following afternoon and my prescription was still not there. Again I rang the surgery and not one person could tell me what was going on. I now put it down to a language barrier within that surgery. They need to have staff that speak the same language like the minority of patients like myself who only speak English. I really don't know where to go with this because they only look after their own. I say this because last year I put in a complaint about one of their absolutely rude nurse and was told that someone will call me try and resolve the complaint I put in. I am still waiting for that person to call me back until today. I have no confidence in this place and I feel it is because I am a minority within that surgery. I must also make it clear that this has been my surgery for over 30 years and since the previous owners left, the place as gone completely disgusting. All I ask is that they treat everyone the same,we are all human beings. Trust me I am going to take this further, hopefully I can get someone who speaks English like I do. 😡😡

We continuously work to create a good patient experience, and we’re sorry to hear that we haven’t met your expectations. The standard NHS GP appointment time is 10 minutes, and in this short time, GPs have to establish the problem, diagnose the illness, and advise, prescribe, and/or refer the patient. If the patient arrives with many problems, the GP may decide that it would be better for the patient to book a further appointment so that each of the problems can be given its own individual attention rather than several problems all lying for the same amount of time as one. reviews.author: Jackie taylor
reviews.text: The Bodey Medical Centre is the embodiment of why our NHS was created. Compassion for their patients and the family that care for them. I found myself in a situation, where my father needed an urgent care plan, and I didn't know what to do, I felt as if I was drowning. I call my dad's GP surgery for help because I didn't know what to do. The initial call to the receptionist, was so calming and reassuring. Within 10 mins after that phone call, the Dr Patel called me and asked about my concerns for my dad. As I was explaining the circumstances, she paused the conversation and enquired if I had support and about my well being. That for me, was the most beautiful gesture that will stay with me forever. After getting all the information she needed, Dr Patel contacted the Crisis team. Within 15 mins of my ending the all with Dr Patel, I received a call from the crisis team. It took less than 4 hrs, from my initial phone call to the surgery, to my dad having a complete care plan in place and equipment installed for his safety. A perfect example of team work, that worked hand in hand with each other and have given my father and I the best outcome. I would like all who were involved in the creation of my dad's care, to know how grateful my family and I are, because if it wasn't for your actions, my father may not be here today. Thank you Practice response date: 3 weeks ago Practice response: Thank you so much for taking the time to share such a heartfelt review. We are truly touched by your kind words and are so pleased that we were able to support both your dad and you during what sounds like an incredibly difficult and overwhelming time. I will personally ensure that your feedback is shared with our reception team and with Dr Patel. Bodey MC

reviews.author: Paul Goodwin
reviews.text: Huge thanks to the receptionist team for always getting me in to see a doctor, even if I haven't mastered how to fill the online form in. He rearranged all his next two hour appointments and shared them with the other doctors and nurses at the centre. He then did not leave my side until the ambulance arrived. What a brilliant young doctor. He made me feel that there was noone more important for the entire centre team right at that moment. Thanks reception team, a huge thanks to Dr Han and to the whole of the team Practice response date: a month ago Practice response: Thank you so much for sharing this incredibly kind and detailed feedback 🌟 We’re delighted to hear how well supported you felt by the reception team and the whole practice, especially when you were feeling so unwell. Ensuring patients can access care when they need it most is extremely important to us, and your comments really reflect the teamwork involved in making that happen. Your praise for Dr Jonny Han is truly appreciated. We will be sure to pass on your lovely words to him and the wider team. It means a great deal to hear that you felt listened to, cared for, and prioritised during such a worrying time. Thank you again for taking the time to share your experience and for recognising the dedication of the entire team. We wish you a continued recovery and good health.

reviews.author: kazz
reviews.text: This practice has been the best practice I have ever been registered at. The receptionists who have a vital job as they are the first port of call, do not get enough recognition. They ate absolute stars! Every single clinical member I have spoken to or seen also have been compassionate, informative, sympathetic, understanding and patient and have got me through some tough times. I honestly do not know what I would do without their help and am extremly grateful. Bodey medical is an extremely fantastic practice, all staff included. The appointment system is easy to use, you are informed the same day if you will receive an appointment. Waiting times are great. I have been here around 7 years and Bodey looked after my grandmother before me.. My hat goes off to the practice. 10/10. Thank you :)

reviews.text: It was so difficult to get an appointment let alone be seen by GP, when I finally got a face to face appointment my GP thoughtless in general and specifically about filling out a medical exemption certificate she misinformed me by telling me to take the form to a pharmacy without actually knowing that it was an application form not an exemption till I read it and questioned it myself, she then apologised and told me to post it to an address but did not give me the envelope enclosed with it till I went back to reception and asked and the receptionist told me that they will post it for me. I’m perplexed by this experience.

reviews.author: Emilija Mac
reviews.text: The nurses and doctors at this practice are nice and helpful and I’d give them 5 stars, however wouldn’t say the same about reception. Have moved out of my old home over 2 YEARS AGO, Bodey Medical Centre was one of the first places I contacted to inform. Just found out that they’ve not changed it… And I have an ongoing issue, so I’ve been to the practice loads during those two years. I wonder how much time it would have saved me if they did and I received medical letters to my current address rather than the old one. A lady that works in the afternoon reception is incredibly rude and makes you feel like you’re dumb.. Another thing, although it is not the first time, but most recently I had a few appointments only to find out once I’m in the practice that I have no appointments for that day and time. Came the second time, apparently I’m too late although I’ve triple checked with the receptionist to be 100% sure while we were arranging the time over the phone. When I finally got to see the doctor, she said she had the same times and dates as me, and was waiting for me but I never showed up (I did, both times, but thanks to constant reception mess up, the doctor never knew that I was there waiting). So many work holidays are wasted on their mess ups.. Lastly, I was invited to make an appointment, and once I came to it, the doctor said that (again) it must be a reception mess up as I’m not due for that appointment until 2024..

reviews.author: SoniaLisa Roy

reviews.author: Libby Davison
reviews.text: Absolutely shocking experience, They refused to give me an emergency appointment to discuss my medication ( which I ran out of ) still refused to give me emergency medication. The workers are extremely rude and ignorant, hopefully the place shuts down. Very disappointed.

reviews.author: Katie Rae
reviews.text: Absolutely terrible staff especially as the reception who answer the phone. Called up to ask if my partner could have an appointment as she has epilepsy and needed emergency medication. Was told no as she didn't have all of her medical history sent over (we registered over 5 months ago after transferring gp's) and that we would need an appointment to talk about her medication. They gave her an appointment for the 20th. After calling 111 they said to get an emergency appointment for the same day which Bodey refused to give my girlfriend one. Went to Bodey in person and was met with a very ignorant woman who told us to leave despite my girlfriend at this point going without her medication for over 48 hours as everyone was refusing her any. My girlfriend ended up in hospital due to the unhelpful manner of all the women who we had both spoken to. They gave her another appointment for the 13th and didn't even bother to call my partner. Would not recommend.

Just takes ages to book an appointment as at any surgery but once you have one you're in safe hands.

Just the other day I went to the doctor saying they want to book an appointment, they tell me to call so I call immediately but no one answers I call the next day but no answer is always waiting. reviews.text: Went back today to get my blood taken and was so impressed by the nurse, she was so understanding, reassuring and professional (I'm scared of needles) and allowed me to touch her hand as she put the needle in which made me feel a lot more in control. I was also very impressed with the patience of the rest of the staff, there was another family waiting and perhaps English wasn't their first language (I've been there when I've lived abroad and its scary when you don't feel confident with the language when going to the doctors) and they were so patient and kind with them even though it took a little longer and there was a bit of a queue. It doesn't seem like much, and it should be normal to be so patient but having been in their situation I can tell you that not everyone is so kind. Makes me so happy to see so much compassion, even when the health service is going through a tough time. Thank you.

reviews.author: Nafeesa
reviews.text: I understand we are going through a pandemic but I was not impressed with the fact that 4 adults had to wait outside in the pouring rain. Once inside they had clearly spaced the chairs out in the waiting room so it was very unnecessary to have us all huddled together outside. ‘Will your elderly patients succumb to this treatment too’? Secondly the fact that I was told i couldn’t sit on the chair once I was in the consulting room was beyond a joke, why because the doctor said I could put my bag on the chair but not myself again bizarre and totally uncalled for. Finally I wasn’t allowed to use the toilet to clean my hands I was told to use the watered down hand gel in reception. Seriously Bodey’s where are your hazmat suits? I went to the hospital last week and was never treated like this this is ridiculous. On top of it I had some young man asking for my dob in front of strangers but didn’t ask for the ladies dob who was after me. Data protection and no consistency in asking questions to patients.

reviews.author: Ayden Irving
reviews.text: The worst GP I've ever been to. The booking system is absolutely awful, they put you on hold for ages, and IF they eventually answer there's 90% chance that all appointments have gone. If you require an emergency appointment you then have to wait hours for the doctor to call you back, before MAYBE being asked to go to the surgery. The reception staff are rude and unhelpful most of the time, and overall it's a very poor GP practice. One time they even told me they had test results I had been waiting weeks for, to only call back Monday morning and find out they had made a mistake and my results were not actually on the system, and never had been; again met with rudeness. They seriously need to reconsider their booking system and overall customer service, to get patients seen appropriately, and actually answer the phone, rather than a free-for-all at 8.30 every morning!

reviews.author: Alice
reviews.text: don’t register here if you enjoy such luxuries as; -speaking to a medical professional -having the phone answered -common human decency - access to medication, advice or gp appointments just don’t bother, why have a GP if you have no access to the resources they’re meant to provide 🙃

reviews.author: DillyMyra Stephenson
reviews.text: The staff, doctors and nurses are all very friendly, professional and understanding hence the 2 stars. However, the centre is insanely oversubscribed. I have been trying to ring to get an appointment since the beginning of November with no luck, and to book in advance you have to wait at least 3 weeks (which retrospectively would have saved me a lot of time). When you try to call the line is so congested you can't even get through to be put on hold, it will just immediately hang up on you. According to my call history, one day I made 82(!) calls from 8:30 when the line opens and still didn't even manage to get through on hold; the line hung up every time. Still haven't been able to make an appointment which I desperately need at this point and will probably be moving to a new doctors.

reviews.author: Nadia Ortiz
reviews.text: Imposible to talk on the phone... they put me on hole without saying anything, and impossible to get an appointment. I can't talk about the doctor service from the doctors as is imposible to get throw my mistake for choose this GP

reviews.author: Kathryne Cowhig
reviews.text: Deteriorated hugely in all aspects over last 4 years...detail too numerous to list - but all functions of service have nose dived compared to how this practice used to be. Practice Management needs to be removed abd replaced with individuals with more customer empathy and skill sets appropriate to the job.

reviews.author: Tajammal Hussain
reviews.text: Very unprofessional staff, unfair prices, took the money from us without giving any treatment. We booked for travel vaccination for 5 people charged us £125 over the phone and when we get there asked us to pay £465 to be vaccinated. Firstly nurse said you can either have one person be vaccinated in this price you have already paid tomorrow. When we came for one person to be vaccinated they asked to pay £80 more. They kept the money for nothing and not given any treatment. You would not expect a fair and decent treatment here, do not take the health risk.

reviews.author: M Mos
reviews.text: This has the potential to be a great practice - the staff are pleasant, doctors are kind and knowledgeable - but unfortunately there are a couple of points that really let it down. First of all, the booking system is a nightmare. Phone lines open at 8:30am for appointments the same day. By 9:00am you can be pretty certain that there will be none left (if you can get through). This is particularly stressful when trying to book a follow-up appointment for a medication review or for test results, as you are told that you will have to go through the same procedure the following day ad infinitum until finally you get through. I think the longest I have pursued this is two weeks, ringing every day at the specified time - constantly ringing, hundreds of times. This has resulted in not being able to access necessary medication and not being able to discuss test results despite being asked by the doctor to book a subsequent appointment. Because getting an appointment is so difficult, it is equally as difficult to see the same doctor consistently which can be troublesome when trying to resolve an ongoing issue and often results in taking up more time within the appointment. There was talk of an online booking system but at last look this wasn't operational. I understand this is a busy practice and that the same day booking is aimed at reducing the number of people that don't turn up for booked appointments but in reality, it serves to punish the people that always turn up.

reviews.author: Peter Job
reviews.text: My favourite medical center

reviews.author: ieuan Williams
reviews.text: Once you book your appointment the staff are all very helpful and consequently I have no complaints in that area, but actually getting to that point can be a nightmare. First, the booking on the day system is bizarre and, unless you can get through to book your appointment by about 9:30, it's unlikely you'll get a spot for that day. In addition to this, I have had to wait almost an hour to be seen in the past, which makes the whole process a pain in the arse.

reviews.author: Jonathan
reviews.text: I've never had any negative experiences with any of the staff, if anything I've found them to be quite pleasant. It's incredibly difficult to get through to them on the phone. You'll probably be told to call at 08:30 to make sure you get an appointment... good luck with that. Even calling in the afternoon can sometimes take up to 30 minutes. That being said, I imagine it has an above average number of people registered with it, so the delays in getting through are probably because it's busy, not because of anything wrong with the staff. If any of the staff are reading this: please, please, please either change the music you have to listen to whilst on hold and/or change the frequency with which it's interrupted by the lady saying "all of our staff are busy right now, please continue to hold". It's very irritating. I've probably heard her voice more than I've heard all of the GPs combined. P.S. I now have the music stuck in my head. Great.

reviews.author: Super Duper
reviews.text: I've been coming here for years so I have comments only as a young adult, I don't know how they are for children or the elderly. The practice operates on a "booking on the day" basis which if you try to do so over the phone, you'll very very occasionally get through. The online system via patient access only let's you order repeat prescriptions. So the best way to get an appointment is walking in as soon as it opens, although reception tell you to call. The staff are sometimes friendly, I've had some impatient and dismissive GPs and receptionists, and I've had very kind ones. TLDR I don't know if this is better or worse than other practices but IF you get an appointment it's ok...just don't bother calling between 8.30 am and 2 pm (12-2 is lunch)

reviews.author: Milka Boydell
reviews.text: Impossible to get through on the phone, rude reception staff. All the doctors & nurse in this surgery that we have dealt with were really good, helpful and caring. That's were the good things unfortunately stop. It is pretty much impossible to get through on the phone to arrange appointment. The system is to call in the morning, however there is no answer more often than not - one morning we had to call nearly 200 times, only to be told there are no more appointments left by the time someone picked up. See picture attached. If you try to ring during the day they simply don't answer the phone more often than not. And then switch all the phones off between 12-2pm for lunch break. If you go in to try to speak to someone in person, the reception staff are incredibly rude and just tell you to call in the morning to book. If you explain you tried that 200 times and couldn't get through, the just shrug their shoulders and turn away from you. They appear to simply not care. We were trying to get an appointment for my partner as he was running out of important medication that you can't just stop taking without talking to the doctor - we were told by the reception staff this was not emergency and as such urgent appointment was not offered. The only reason we had to go through this as well was because the doctor only prescribed 28 days and asked to come see him to reassess after this time. The reception refused to book an appointment for 28 days time and said we would have to call closer to time. Ridiculous! In the end we had to ring 111 and get it prescribed by a GP from there.

reviews.author: Rehab Sherif
reviews.text: I had an extremely disappointing experience with this dentist. My appointment was 25 minutes long and I arrived 7 minutes late, due to the car park being full, having to find and pay for on-street parking, and arranging (and paying for) a babysitter to attend the appointment. I explained the situation clearly to the receptionist and asked for it to be relayed to the dentist. Despite this, the dentist showed no empathy or flexibility. After waiting six years to finally register with an NHS dentist since moving to Manchester, I was shocked to be told I would be taken off the register for being late once — something that, having worked in two dental practices myself, I have never known to be standard policy. What made the situation worse was the dentist’s behaviour: instead of speaking to me directly like a professional, he avoided the conversation entirely and hid behind a wall, while incorrectly claiming I was “over 10 minutes late.” This felt dismissive, unprofessional, and frankly inhumane. After such a long wait to access NHS dental care, this experience was incredibly upsetting. Patients deserve understanding, honesty, and basic respect — none of which were shown here.

reviews.text: I have been with this gp since I was 5 im now 22, it used to be good but recently I have been appalled by their actions, I had a cough for about a month and a doctor sent me to the hospital for a chest xray I then had to wait three weeks for that to go back to my doctors. In which time I went back and told a different doctor that it was getting worse he said and I quote "it will go, iv been a doctor for 25 years with people coughing and sneezing on me and I dont get sick, you dont need medicine". So I asked to see another doctor because I wasnt taking his word after what he said I then seen another doctor on the same day and she said my chest sounds crackly, my blood pressure was up and my temp was low, she sent me straight to the ACU ward at the hospital where they did blood and the doctor said there that oh you're fine you can go home. I said to them I dont feel fine its hard to breath and I have asthma at this point im now coughing, fever, sickness, sharp pain in my arm and dizzy. I went home like they said and now on christmas eve all this things have gotten worse and I have collapsed 3 times in 24 hours and I have had an asthma attack. Iv been dealing with this for over three months now and I have been given 2 sets of antibiotics and then taken off them half way through the course. its got to the point everytime I cough I need my inhaler other I will stop breathing its ridiculous and im fuming. The hospital and the doctors say the same thing I dont know what to do im concentrating on making it through a day it feels like they dont care about their patients or what happens to them im seriously disappointed if it turns out that something bigger is going on with me im going to make a complaint and leave.

reviews.author: Parul Singh
reviews.text: I actually cannot fault this GP practice! I have been with them for around 18 months now, I’ve never struggled for appointment when I’ve needed them, they process my repeat prescriptions same day etc. I’ve seen various GPs at the practice depending on who is available and I have felt heard and supported by every single one, which is so rare in general but particularly as a young, disabled, neurodivergent woman of colour. I had my most recent appointment with Dr Aunet regarding a recent decline in my mental health following a traumatic event. I was struggling to articulate myself because of my mental state but she was kind and let me take my time. I felt my mental health was taken seriously and her priority was ensuring I was safe, then we explored some support options and she offered regular check ins with the GP No GP practice is going to be perfect given the pressure they’re under but that’s not always in their control and I’ve genuinely never had a negative experience and I couldn’t recommend this practice more Thank you to all the team here for restoring my faith in GP practices and doing your best to keep me in good health ❤️

reviews.text: I am totally disappointed with the service that was provided to me. I changed my GP based on Google reviews and then visited this GP practice. They told me they had made a referral for an abdominal ultrasound, and it has been one month; I haven't received any letter. I was told during my appointment that I would be contacted by the ultrasound team in two to six weeks for the appointment. I waited for more than a month and then called the GP practice regarding the ultrasound appointment, and then I received an email about it. It mentioned that I would have to wait another two months for a decision. When I inquired about this at the GP practice, they said they could not do anything with the referral. I asked if I could talk to a doctor regarding this; the reply I got was that I could have a routine appointment, and for that, I would have to wait for two weeks. I am disspointed because of the service provided. Update: Range medical care Helped me with the issue and sorted it for me. reviews.author: Sahar Hanifeh
reviews.text: Dr Arif is truly one of the best doctors I have ever met. She is extremely patient, kind, and attentive, always listening carefully to what I have to say. Despite the many health challenges I face, she has consistently given me great positive energy, comfort, and hope. I genuinely feel motivated after seeing her, and I was willing to endure my pain for days just to have an appointment with her.🌷 Unfortunately, at my most recent visit—after waiting a whole month for an appointment—I was shocked and deeply disappointed to find out, without any prior notice, that my booking had been changed and I was scheduled with another doctor instead. This was very upsetting, as all my patience and effort were for the chance to see Dr Arif herself. Overall, Dr Arif is an exceptional doctor, and if it were up to me, I would always choose to be seen only by her. I sincerely hope the appointment booking and management process will be improved to reflect the outstanding quality of her care, so that patients can have a truly positive and reassuring experience. Practice response date: 5 months ago Practice response: Thank you for taking the time to write such a detailed and heartfelt review. We are pleased to hear about the exceptional care you have received from one of our doctors. We are, however, sorry to hear that your appointment was changed without any prior notice, and we understand how upsetting this must have been. This is not the standard of service we aim for, and we will be reviewing our booking process. We appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

reviews.author: Asima Mahmood
reviews.text: Recently I had the experience of calling my parent's GP surgery (not the range medical centre). The way I had to navigate through the receptionist, the online form that is there to book an appointment that is x3 pages long was frustration on another level. Whilst I was filling that form to obtain an appointment for my poorly dad, I was thinking to myself my GP’s practice doesn’t have all this plava, how on earth can my 72 year old father who is not internet savvy possibly do this, no wonder he was going around in circles over the last month unable to get an appointment. Long story short “the range medical centre” is absolutely brilliant! Now that I have had the experience of other GP surgeries I can say that honestly, I always get an appointment, the ladies are lovely at the reception, the whole team are great!! I have never had an issue the 19 or so years I have been registered there. One star short is for the reception decor. Other than that the rest is all brilliant. Practice response date: 9 months ago Practice response: Thank you for taking the time to leave such detailed feedback. We're so pleased to hear that your experiences with The Range Medical Centre over the past 19 years have been "absolutely brilliant," especially when compared to the difficulties you encountered navigating another surgery's system for your father. We understand how frustrating complex booking processes can be, particularly for those who aren't internet savvy, and we are committed to keeping our appointment system as straightforward and accessible as possible for all our patients. We're glad you find our reception ladies lovely and the whole team great. We also appreciate your feedback regarding the reception decor; we do periodically review the surgery environment and will take your comment into consideration for future improvements.

reviews.author: Geetanjali Normandale
reviews.text: Prior to this GP I tried one down the road, they spent an hour on the phone and told me it’d take 28 days to register me. This GP It’s a way from me but I regret nothing, I called them and they registered me on the spot. I have moved a lot, and can honestly say this is the best GP I have had by miles. Every time I interact with them I am bowled over. Receptionists are friendly and helpful. The pharmacist is outstanding, first pharmacist who actually read the NICE guidelines for my conditions let alone took the time to ask me about the specifics and tailored the prescriptions to my needs. Today they issued my repeat prescription within an hour of the request. An hour! I’ve had private healthcare nowhere near as good. Kudos to the practice manager for maintaining an impeccable service in these trying times. Practice response date: 9 months ago Practice response: Thank you for taking the time to leave your feedback. It’s wonderful to hear about your positive experience when registering with us, especially after the difficulties you faced elsewhere – we always aim to make the registration process as smooth as possible. We are incredibly proud to hear you say this is the best GP practice you've had by miles. Your kind words about our friendly and helpful receptionists, and particularly your praise for our "outstanding" pharmacist who took the time to understand your needs and tailor prescriptions according to NICE guidelines, are very much appreciated. It's great to know that the quick turnaround for your repeat prescription was also noted. We are indeed very fortunate to have such a dedicated practice manager and team committed to maintaining an impeccable service, even in these trying times.

reviews.author: Guz Chuz
reviews.text: Avoid this practice if you have any other choices available. I have been using this practise my whole life, 26 years, since they were opposite the park. I don't much remember how things were when I was young and I haven't had much cause to go in my adult life. Every time I have though it has been a nightmare. When trying to book an appointment they usually don't have anything available for around a month so if time is an issue you have to book an emergency appointment on the day, even if you wouldn't class it as an emergency. When calling for an emergency appointment in the morning you will typically wait on the phone for 30-45 minutes. When you eventually get through to the rude reception staff you'll be asked for information about your emergency. The secretary, with no medical training, will then decide whether she wants to give you an appointment or not. If you tell them you'd rather keep the info between yourself and the doctor they will insist you tell them or refuse to give you an appointment. In the last 10 years I think I've actually seen a doctor 3 times, I'm not dead yet but this kind of treatment of patients in dangerous and unhealthy. Im not oblivious to the reasons here either, with so many people on the books they want to prioritise but treating everybody like a time waster is not a good way to do that. Once again, if you can sign up at another practice do so, it will save you unnecessary stress. Maybe your life too. Practice response date: 6 months ago Practice response: Thank you for taking the time to provide this detailed historical feedback. We are very sorry to hear about the issues you experienced, particularly with phone waits and our reception process at the time. We have since made significant changes to our appointment and telephone systems to address these exact problems. The treatment you describe does not reflect the standards we strive to provide for our patients today.

We want to reassure you that we have thoroughly overhauled our clinical and administrative protocols since then to prevent such incidents from ever happening again. The standard you describe is unacceptable and does not reflect our practice today.
