I want to see my doctor with an appointment time not sit and wait for goodness knows how long in a walk in centre to see a doctor who I don't know and more to the point does not know me or my medical issues. Rock Healthcare rated outstanding by CQC that was back in 2015.... I am sorry but if you are looking for a doctor's surgery look elsewhere because Rock Healthcare actually need to put the work CARE into ACTION, the reception/admin staff are the least helpful staff I have ever come across, they don't CARE! I was given an appointment for 22nd March 2018 (6 Days before I get to see my doctor, lets hope nothing to serious eh?)

reviews.text: I’ve been going here now for 3 years. Some experiences have been great and my usual doctor is good and knowledgable, nurses are nice and efficient. ... sometimes it’s obviously they don’t get much time per person (when you receive a letter asking to call them for results and then they ask YOU what you’re ringing for!). The admin staff however can’t seem to do their job! I’ve had numerous letters asking me to update my phone number because they have been trying to reach me... I’ve been in and stood there and updated it face to face... I’ve rang several times and update my number... and yet again another letter! The last letter, when I rang to update my details, I asked why they had been trying to get in touch.. nobody could give me an answer!! Was promised a call back.. didn’t happen. Seriously need to get their patient record system sorted, if it can’t keep a telephone number what other records is it losing!! Having said that... I’ve also had to drop copies of hospital letters in (that we’re sent to my GP with me copied in) because they weren’t on file!

reviews.author: Ludmila Tomasev
reviews.text: Review of GP Surgery – Dr. Kumari I am extremely disappointed with the level of care my family received from Dr. Kumari. My mother had an appointment due to severe stomach pain that had lasted for three days. She could barely walk, felt nauseous, and had intense cramping radiating to her back. During the appointment, Dr. Kumari only pressed on her stomach (which caused my mum to scream in pain) and then prescribed omeprazole — without carrying out any basic tests such as blood or urine checks. Shockingly, my mother was told she would have to wait six weeks for a scan. Later that same day, her condition worsened, and she had to be taken to hospital. She was diagnosed with acute cholecystitis, treated with IV antibiotics, and is now awaiting laparoscopic cholecystectomy. A simple urine test at the GP surgery would have shown signs of infection and helped avoid a potentially dangerous delay in treatment. The lack of proper examination and follow-up was incredibly irresponsible. In a separate case, the same doctor prescribed cream for my young nephew’s face, assuming he had psoriasis or dry skin. However, the issue turned out to be skin tags around his eyes, which clearly needed a different type of assessment and care. These experiences have left me deeply concerned about the quality of care and the lack of thoroughness shown during appointments. A more careful and investigative approach should be expected from any GP, especially when patients present with such serious symptoms. Practice response date: 6 months ago Practice response: Dear Ludmila, We apologise that the experience you have had with the practice has not been a positive one. The surgery endeavours to provide the best possible standard of care to all our patients and we will continue with regular monitoring and review to enable us to constantly improve the services we offer. Many thanks Practice Manager Bolton Medical Centre

reviews.author: Maria Ebteda
reviews.text: During my appointment, I faced some issues regarding hygiene and patient care. Despite requesting a tissue for the bed, this was denied, and I was informed that the beds were cleaned after each patient. While this assurance was provided, it didn’t address my comfort or concerns at the moment. Additionally, during a vaginal sonography, I asked for the equipment to be cleaned in my presence. This request was refused, and I observed the handles being placed on a desk without any sterilizing measures visible. This experience left me feeling uneasy about the infection control practices. I believe there’s room for improvement to ensure patients feel reassured and cared for during such procedures. Suggestions: • Consider allowing patients to witness equipment cleaning for reassurance. • Provide tissues or disposable covers on beds to enhance comfort and hygiene. reviews.author: Itsme Ayen
reviews.text: I went there this morning. But as usual they said they’re fully booked (I have been calling since two weeks ago when my illness actually started developing, at least 150 times every morning but never got any appointments) So I asked them to refer me to the pharmacy nearby. And the pharmacy referred me back to them as my temperature was high and I had chronic infection in my throat which clearly needed their attention. So I went to the GP straight from the pharmacy at 10.30 and my GP appointment was set at 11.30. I don’t have any voice now since Friday, and I was so tired of walking here and there just to see the doctor. At 11.20 I went to the reception only to be told to wait until they called my name. I couldn’t even speak because my voice is not coming out but I did come to the counter to ask for my appointment. It’s just to be sure because and I was feeling so fatigued and nauseous. Then I sat again at the waiting area until there’s no one left at 12. I quickly asked the receptionist when will I be attended? she checked the system and she said that I never showed up at 11.30 so the doctor has cancelled my appointment. She even told everyone there that I was late. The nerve she had to say that straight to my sick face was beyond me. She even asked me to go home. It was purely rude. I asked her to check the cctv and she said when I came at 10.30 I didn’t get to the counter for registration. It was true because I was way too early for my 11.30 appointment. So they kept blaming me and said I was late to everyone that’s there. I was so ashamed. I was shaking and crying myself out and asked them to check the cctv at 11.20 because I was positive that I did go to the receptionist to confirm my appointment but she only asked me to wait. But of course they won’t because they knew I was telling the truth. They kept arguing with me until I couldn’t take it anymore and I finally lost myself and my nose started bleeding so bad on the floor. This system is crazy. I really couldn’t understand how the Great Britain falls to this low level. I paid thousand pounds to NHS annually with my visa but not even once I get to use your services. And this time I am really ill I had no choice but to see the doctor physically. And this is how you treat your patients. You should be ashamed to be called a doctor when you refused to see your patients! Practice response date: a year ago Practice response: Dear Itsme Many thanks for your feedback. The doctor was kind and helpful, but the communication and urgency from reception staff needs serious improvement. reviews.text: Takes over a month to get an appointment. You can be left on hold for hours, even when the system says you’re caller number one. When the receptionist staff do eventually answer, they are often rude and unhelpful. Overall, a very frustrating experience.

reviews.author: Sani Vlogs
reviews.text: The reception staff are extremely rude and fail to provide clear instructions when their systems are down. Instead, they assume patients should already know what to do. Communication among reception staff is poor, and speaking through the reception desk does not work properly. As a result, patients are often told “we can’t hear you” in an aggressive manner, rather than the issue being addressed professionally. Even when booking appointments, inappropriate comments are sometimes made when more than one person requires an appointment. In contrast, the doctors are absolutely lovely. They communicate clearly, are respectful, and provide excellent support. Unfortunately, this positive experience is undermined by the behaviour of the reception staff. Reception staff clearly require additional care, communication, and customer service training. Regardless of experience or length of time in the role, rudeness is unjustifiable in a healthcare setting. Professionalism, politeness, and clear communication should be a basic standard at all times.

reviews.author: Nadeem Ahmed
reviews.text: My two young children were unwell, so I booked an appointment Hawthorn Medical walk in centre for 10:00 am. I finished my self-employed work early in order to take them to the surgery and arrived around 9:30 am, hoping to be seen on time. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing. The reception staff were rude and appeared completely uninterested. By 10:30 am, I noticed that patients with appointments scheduled after mine were being called in the walking centre (not GP ROOM), while we were still waiting. When I politely questioned this, I was spoken to rudely and told to go to A&E if I was “in a rush”. My children were crying and exhausted, having been unwell and unable to sleep properly all night. I was hoping for some reassurance and relief by having them seen by a doctor. To make matters worse, I overheard a patient with a 10:30 am appointment being taken straight into the walk in doctor’s room, yet my children were not seen until 11:30 am. I cannot understand why this happened. In total, the doctor saw six other patients before finally agreeing to see us, and only after my patience had completely run out as my children were coughing continuously. When we were eventually seen, I received nothing more than a hollow apology. The doctor casually advised me to continue giving paracetamol, despite the fact that my other two children had been prescribed antibiotics for the same condition just two weeks earlier. I felt that the doctor was displeased because I had stood up for my rights, but I strongly believe that had I not spoken out, we may have been left waiting for several more hours. The whole experience was sad and deeply frustrating. This incident makes me seriously question how this surgery has received an “Outstanding” CQC rating.BRIBERY perhaps

reviews.author: Brontë Schiltz
reviews.text: I had a frankly shocking experience at this walk-in centre. I spoke to a nurse called Jackie, who was rude from the outset, challenging my use of the term 'boils' (which is used on the NHS website and was used by a doctor I previously saw about the same kind of infection), then gave me instructions on treating insect bites when the bite I showed her was very clearly infected and my actual reason for calling was that it had transferred to my face, and a boil I had on my face previously became extremely painful and the NHS website says to see a doctor if you get one on your face. She finally agreed to see me after saying that I "clearly wouldn't accept that it was an insect bite" (I never challenged this, just stated that the bite was clearly infected and that I seemed to have spread that infection to my face, which was why I called), and as soon as I arrived, told me that I was overreacting, even denying that the boil on my face was red, hot and inflamed, which it very clearly was. A simple glance at my medical record would show that I have only sought medical attention twice previously since moving to Manchester in 2018, once when I couldn't breathe and once for the aforementioned previous boil, and I waited over a week to seek care in that instance because I have a bit of a phobia of medical settings. I showed her the scars from three previous boils for which I had not sought medical care, and she reluctantly agreed to give me antibiotics but said that I would ruin my immune system if I "kept taking them for things like this", to which I said again that I had not had antibiotics since the first boil on my face around Christmas 2020, and she just sarcastically said "okay". She then gave me a prescription for penicillin, and when I said that I am allergic to penicillin, she challenged this, saying that if all I'd had was a rash then I probably wasn't allergic. I said that I didn't know what my reaction had been since it happened when I was a young child but that it had been diagnosed by a doctor, and she chastised me for not mentioning my allergy sooner, when I had presumably reasonably assumed that it would be on my medical record. She was incredibly confrontational and condescending throughout, insinuating that I was wasting her time when providing healthcare is her job, there was nobody else in the waiting room when I went in, and she saw me 40 minutes after our agreed time, during which I was missing work at my job (at a homelessness charity) which I had to catch up on in my own time. I didn't complain about this because I understand that nurses are very busy, but I didn't appreciate being treated like a hypochondriac when I so rarely seek medical attention and my own time is also valuable. As I was leaving, she again reiterated instructions on responding to bites, which at this point I had stated multiple times was not the reason for my visit. I have a chronic pain condition and do not complain of pain unless it is extremely bad. Hugely disappointing overall.

We saw the “Nurse Paula “who was very abrupt and we was in and out within 2 minutes. My husband explained the pharmacist had told him to come as he needed antibiotics as it was Infected. She said it wasn’t infected and “the pharmacist had no right to say we could have antibiotics “ she also commented she would not give us them “ just because we were going away” The following day we travelled to Southampton. My husband developed a rash and became unwell. Again we visited the local pharmacy who said she did not like the look of the rash. She directed us to the local walk In centre. We were seen my friendly helpful staff who took the time to explain about the infection. The nurse requested he was seen by a GP. The GP reported my husband did have an infection and prescribed antibiotics. Such a different experience of two walk in centres. The staff were so much more helpful in Southampton than in our own city of Manchester. If I could award this walk in centre a zero I would.

reviews.author: Jodie Leigh
reviews.text: I’d be apprehensive to say this practice even deserves one star. I had been registered here for the past approximately 15 years and throughout attended this practice for multiple ongoing problems which I feel have been ignored and unseen to despite countless visits. The main problem is not the qualified healthcare staff but the overall system and management, I work in healthcare myself and understand that sometimes no matter how well patients are treated by staff they are still failed by the declining system of the NHS. Although I have felt ignored by some practitioners whose names I cannot remember, nurse Karen and mental health practitioner Ian have been great and have always listened to my health issues thoroughly. The reception staff answer calls with rude manner (I can’t say all as I have had kind receptionists previously but the majority of time not) and they appear uninterested in answering your queries and concerns. The appointment availability is unacceptable, attempting to arrange an on the day appointment at 8am often leaves you without one and trying to pre book an appointment leaves you with a 3-7 week wait and there is no acknowledgement of urgent symptoms. Sometimes they’ll tell you a GP will contact you over the phone on the day to assess your symptoms and then no one rings you all day from the practice. The final straw for me was when I rang last week describing tachycardia, feeling faint and CHEST PAIN and they told me they had no appointments for 4 weeks, neither did they advise me on what to do or where else to go for urgent medical attention. I have since changed practice and they have been a huge improvement.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I initially wrote a one star review as I got Appalling service by Dr K . This is also not the first occasion this has happened with this specific Dr (infact previously she was one of my favourite GPs especially when it came to children as I felt she was thorough). On this occasion I contacted the gp practice for my son who is under one who had a nose bleed. As a pharmacist I am fully aware of what pharmacy can offer and what knowledge we have and this needed further investigation. Instead of seeing my son she referred the query to pharmacy first for us to only be told this is not an appropriate query for pharmacy first and that my son should be seen by a gp and that this is a red flag. I was completely disheartened by the practice with the constant pushing me to another health care, usually pharmacy or some random resource but my faith has been restored by Sami as a result I have changed my review from a one star to a four star. Sami is an asset to the gp practice, kind and considerate and very polite and professional. I accidentally missed my blood pressure appointment and had the times mixed up and he didn’t make me feel guilty or bad or anything but rather simply booked me in the next day. Thank you Sami!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had my cervical smear test done at limelight on the 17th of Jan 2026. From the moment I entered the room I felt very at ease and calm. Suli ( the nurse practitioner ) was very likeable, friendly and knowledgeable. She explained what the test was for and reassured any of my worries. I was in the room for no longer than 5 minutes and felt very relieved to have got such an important test done. Suli is an absolute credit to limelight and nurses as a whole…. and the way she advocates for women’s health by simply being so reassuring and respectful at a time that many women feel vulnerable is faultless. Please get your smear tests done! Ask for Suli!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Afroz A
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Absolutely appalling service – avoid Limelight Health at all costs. I was booked a follow-up telephone consultation three weeks in advance. I stayed in all day from 7am, phone in hand, waiting for the call. Nothing. No call, no missed-call notification, no voicemail. When I rang the surgery, I was told the doctor apparently “called twice and I didn’t answer” – completely untrue. The receptionist refused to investigate, offered no apology, and just said “nothing can be done” and “we’ll just go round in circles”. I now have to start the entire process again and wait weeks more for the appointment I should have had. No accountability, no empathy, and what appears to be a falsified clinical record stating calls were made when they weren’t. Patients are being blamed for the surgery’s failures. Reception staff clearly need urgent training and better systems are needed to stop this kind of thing happening. Deeply unhappy and still without the medical follow-up I need. I do not recommend this practice to anyone.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Liv Zachariasen
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Keep dismissing me when I contact them when my toddler is poorly They just refer me to a pharmacy that I can't get to. If I want my toddler to be seen, I have to put through a complaint as it's the only way they'll take me seriously and the last time he turned out to have tonsilitis. My requests on AskmyGP just get closed off with a link to a pharmacy. I was never informed I'd have to be seen by a pharmacy first when I registered at this practice and it has never been communicated. They claim you'll be seen sooner, but before this we've always been sble to be seen on the day. I will never understand fobbing off parents who are worried about their small children and I get this every single time now. I have to always push to be seen and when they finally agree, I'm already so upset and stressed by the whole dismissiveness that I can't be bothered speaking to them. Not sure contacting a GP is supposed to trigger anxiety? It's more than reasonable to not rely on a pharmacy for diagnosis, especially for small children!! The last time he had a fever I didn't even bother contacting them as I couldn't be bothered with the thought of being fobbed off with a pharmacy referral. I get that the NHS is stretched and particularly GP practices, but you should be allowed a consultation every once in a while without a battle. I definitely hope nothing serious ever happens to myself or my family or we better hope the pharmacy can treat us. However having seen the pharmacist as they told me to, I'm none the wiser so what an absolute waste of people's time and energy to pass them round such a useless and inefficient circus. So disappointed as they have resorted to such a lazy way of dealing with their patients.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Shereen Simmonds
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Awful experience. Taken me off the database because I’ve moved from the area, even though I work 5 minutes away. I expressed that I would struggle changing gps because of underlying issues and they didn’t show any empathy. I expressed that my dentist etc were still in Manchester, as I am physically unavailable through the week to attend any appointments, working 6am until 8pm Monday to Friday. I stated that I’d had an ongoing condition, knew what it was but they had to test me. The first test they lost, the 2nd test they tested for the incorrect issue, the third they said I didn’t have what I thought. When I was referred to a specialist they confirmed on the day (within minutes of being tested) that I did in fact have what I initially thought! My family member used a doctor here when she was extremely depressed. When they asked what was wrong with her, she expressed that she didn’t know, to which they replied, “well if you don’t know how am I supposed to know.” For someone who was vulnerable at the time, that isn’t what you’d expect to be said from a health care professional. I believe if she wasn’t as strong as she was, just may have tried something unthinkable. When I sent a letter of complaint nothing was done. The doctors name is Dr Hoddes! They misdiagnose people, give them antibiotics or painkillers and they end up dying of cancer. Avoid at all costs!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: See See
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: If you want to die, not get referred or seen, visit this GP surgery!!! A family member visited this surgery on several occasions with stomach pains and weight loss. This GP surgery fobbed her off with painkillers and antibiotics. My relative collapsed at home, ended up in hospital via ambulance requiring 4 units of blood because of a burst ulcer. Another family member has had chest issues, she's been wheezing for months and the GP only prescribed her with antibiotics over and over again. No referral to find out what's happening. A friend is suffering from chronic pain in her leg due to having surgery. All they have prescribed her is co-codamol. She needs something stronger but can't get an appointment. The staff here are also rude. They have no compassion, come across as patronising and have no respect, especially the reception staff. As some have mentioned the staff are good, it makes me wonder if this GP surgery has it's prejudices. The only good respectable doctor they had was Dr Beresford and he retired. This surgery needs closing down. If I could give a zero star rating, I would.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Oj B
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: It's so heartbreaking to see this practice degenerate to this level. How hard can it be for people to be nice and professional? They have a lot to do in terms of training all their staff. And I mean ALL of them! From people's skills to civility, mannerisms, tone of voice when addressing patients and how to approach to patients who are already suffering. I've had so many unpleasant encounters with them that I don't want to mention. They make it look like they are doing a favour by attending to you. So appalling! They soon will be having no stars whatsoever if they don't make proper and needed adjustments on their people's skills. It really is appalling! Yelling at patients!! 9/03/2026 I can't believe that I am back here after 4 years to leave a very negative review of this establishment. Before, I go any further - I want to make it clear that, whatever issues patients are having with this medical centre are 90 to 95% front desk, admin, nurses and lesser staff (sorry, for lack of a better word to use.) The Dr's are unaware of the front desk, admin, and lesser staff issues - and yet bear the brunt of the end of the stick should the establishment suffer. I've had very unbelievable and excrutiatingly painful experiences with them from the beginning of this year. In short, (they put up lies and mark your profile, including your number should you call and then mete you undeserved shabby treatment by whoever picks your call, and for whatever reasons best known to them). From the tone of answering your call and how you are responded to is clear and obvious! It is like a syndicate in operation!!! Very evil and unprofessional!!! But we must continue to voice these issues until changes are made, and wrongs are righted. This afternoon I made a call to the centre, having moved to a new home, my daughter who had ran out of medication, due to pressure of moving into a new home and the process of registering with a near gp when settled; called Gorton Medical centre before the weekend to kindly ask for a repeat to be sent to the pharmacy for her to collect. It was not actioned. We called 111 for emergency prescription over the weekend. Today being Monday and on her last tablet, I called the pharmacy to ask if her prescription has come through from the gp, and they said it hadn't. I then called this medical centre to ask why my daughter's prescription had not been actioned and sent to the pharmacy since last week - Knowing she's been on same medication for several years and should not miss days? I was bluntly told by the reception to call back again,(of course, profile marking and syndicate operations in action.) I quickly reminded him how important her medication was, and he should please send it over to the pharmacy for collection. He said he was not in charge of that, and ended up pretending not to understand which medication was needed, (She's only on 1) and is in her profile. To cut the story short, I had no choice but to call 111 again. "Profile marking or spewed lies on the profile" was highly resonant in the voice at the end of the receiver too. I want to clearly state that these issues should be looked into by the right bodies in charge. People are being abused by those that should be providing care, and lives are lost due to these. (I nearly would have lost my life with this centre, cause i was refused care and gp appointment, and was bluntly told to do the worse I can not too long ago.) My daughter was refused duty of care, when she needed, and the excuse was, we had moved homes and was removed by the gp from their system- even when we had not yet registered with another gp. Where is the duty of care? What is the professionalism in this? This is gross misconduct and should be called out. And like I said in the beginning, Dr's are in consulting rooms doing their best and in very high cases are unaware of what goes on at the front desks, admins, and the rest. This types of evil must be called out and put away and far, please.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Unwilling to make reasonable adjustments (due to learning disability) despite the Equality Act 2010 and The Autism Act 2009. Not a suitable surgery for neurodivergent adults (ADHD/autism) with long term lifelong mental health conditions or/and learning disability, not unless you have a parent/family friend to speak on your behalf, book and accompany you to appointments. Admin staff not understanding or particularly helpful and hold grudges/make assumptions, no training in autism/learning disability. (Even if the patient is on the NHS Learning Disability Register). On one occasion I had a local authority social worker attend an appointment with me as an advocate and to see the challenges I face accessing lawful care. Complain or raise concerns and get told “go elsewhere”. Not a particularly modern thinking practice. Very much the “you don’t look autistic” attitude and “go for a long walk outdoors” when facing a serious MH relapse/crisis. Seem to have the attitude that anything mental health related means you must see the CMHT only and if not under psychiatric care they won’t help you. They don’t feel the need to update medical records despite communication from medical consultants. No excuse for treating vulnerable patients so ineffectually or cruelly.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Absolutely appalling experience with this surgery. You’re expected to call at 8:30am to book an appointment, but now with their new call system instead of being placed in a queue, your call is terminated if staff are busy, meaning you have to redial over and over most days, just to be told to try again tomorrow. No empathy from staff and no alternative solutions.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Silviya Nitsova
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I needed a same-day appointment but the open surgery was full, so I got redirected to another surgery for an appointment the next day. This was great. I had to leave a swab test for testing with my practice though. The doctor from the other surgery said I’d get the results back in 2 working days. I still haven’t gotten them back (6 working days and counting). I needed to be seen again rather urgently for the same unresolved issue, so I tried setting up a same-day appointment. It is practically impossible to get one. I called at 8.30 (on the spine) on two different days and was told that all receptionists were busy with other calls, so my calls were terminated. This happened 3 times each of the days. On the second day, I was able to get on their 10-caller hold line, being 9th in the queue. I moved up the queue to number 2 when my call was terminated. When I called again, there were no more appointments for the day. The first day I was told there were no more open surgery appointments for the day right away. The telephone booking system is terrible and dated. Will be switching to a different surgery.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: alan daniel
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Excellent team with excellent comms. Very caring and not rushed. I feel privileged to be one of their Patients.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: joe barber
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Been with this practice for around 23 years and always felt well looked after. Getting an appointment might be difficult but the doctors have been nothing short of fantastic over the years. Shout out to Dr Wilson in particular.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Emma Wilson
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I use this service with my in laws frequently. I can say it’s always been a brilliant service! Dr Hotchkies is great and always reassures you. Receptionist are lovely too!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: clare anderson

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: jaf jaf

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Rose Carbone
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Dr Atherton was absolutely great - as always - however it’s the whole booking/reception where there seems to be difficulty & errors - this last apptmt was at least the 3rd time where I’d been given incorrect information. This time it was an error in phone apptmt/face to face apptmt. Id been told it was a phone apptmt - whereas in fact it was supposed to be a face to face one - so I was waiting by the phone at home & no call came. One before I’d been given the wrong month info - so when I turned up at the surgery - my date & time was right but for the wrong month. Prior to that I’d been given a date and time but just before the booked apptmt I received a message from the surgery to tell me I couldn't actually have that apptmt as it had been booked in incorrectly & had been given an ‘emergency’ slot as opposed to routine - I had booked it 3 wks in advance - so then had to wait a further 3/4 weeks to finally speak to a doctor. Like I said when you do manage to speak with a doctor/nurse at the Practice they are brilliant - however some of the booking/reception team do let it down & it becomes very frustrating - especially if you are concerned about an issue. There were further errors - in a similar area but I have bored myself with this already - I’m only writing this because I was asked to & also hope that it can lead to an improvement in the booking system.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Lahb Singh
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: All good thanks, can do better to inform patients when they are running late

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Georgia Edwards

I very rarely have to go to the doctors but from 2023 when my 6 year old daughter became very ill and was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes I’ve had to deal with mistake after mistake in every prescription. The slack attitude from the staff in reception makes caring for my child with a chronic illness 10x harder and I can not imagine how they talk and treat elderly patients if they are so careless and unprofessional with me regarding my 8 year old. The same issues are tedious and frustrating. Please get some training on professional people skills and simply knowing how to do your job so this doesn’t happen all throughout my child’s life.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: The 5 Brothers Squad
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Benchill Medical Centre is no longer the practice it used to be. All the old doctors are gone, and what’s left is a team that seems to have no urgency, no compassion, and no sense of responsibility. My 12-year-old son developed a serious issue with his eye — it was clearly getting worse — and we spent over two weeks trying to get him seen. I called multiple times, explained that his condition was deteriorating, and still we were ignored. When they finally responded, they didn’t even book an appointment — they just sent us to a pharmacy, where we received no help at all. This isn’t just poor service — this is gross negligence. They failed to provide proper medical care for a child in pain, and they didn’t even follow up. The delay has made things worse, and we’ve had to seek help elsewhere. No examination, no urgency, no care. This practice has changed for the worse — it is now unsafe and unreliable. If you value your family’s health, especially your children’s, I strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: S Khan
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: They’ve failed me I’ve become more ill. They have delayed care for years when I needed it. I have put in a formal complaint. I think I should change GP.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Hayley Perry
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Trying to get an appointment is ridiculous, the receptionist tell you to call at 8am or do the triage form online. The form is only on for 2-3 mins and if you don't complete it in time, you get told no appointments they have reached full capacity. Especially if you are trying to do separate forms for two people i.e yourself and your child. You then phone, like they tell you too, your on hold for hours you could be number 23 in the queue, 10 or 4 but either way on hold for a so long and I am not exaggerating either. Even when I've been in the queue and I'm number two I'm still on hold for absolutely ages. By the time you get an appointment it's in a month's time, by then your problem may have passed. It's unfair ! When you have an appointment you have only 5 minute slots with the doctor, You feel rushed, you forget everything you wanted to tell them. You don't feel like you've been listened to as they are either rushing you out or they are behind massively on appointments. I WOULD NEVER recommend this doctors to anyone whatsoever!!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Amrit Kaur Swalley
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: During my call, I was advised by reception staff that I should take my mother to the dental hospital instead. This advice appeared to be a medical decision, which I found concerning, as reception staff are not clinically qualified to make such determinations. I later spoke with the reception manager, who confirmed that reception staff are permitted to make these decisions. This is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about patient safety and appropriate triage procedures. In addition, I do not feel that my complaint was handled effectively or taken seriously. There was no reassurance, clear explanation, or appropriate escalation of my concerns. I believe further training is required for reception staff, particularly regarding the limits of their role and the importance of not making or influencing medical decisions. As a patient, I expect clinical advice to be given by a qualified healthcare professional. This matter is particularly concerning given the Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements, which state that patients must be treated safely, appropriately, and with clear clinical oversight. I trust that this issue will be reviewed promptly to ensure patients are not placed at risk in the future. Thank you

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Erandi Samaraweera
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: ⚠️ Serious patient safety concerns – I strongly advise de-registering I am writing this review as both a medical doctor and a parent who has been genuinely fearful for their child’s safety while registered at Junction Surgery and Alkrington Surgery. Since registering in August 2025, I have experienced repeated safety and professionalism concerns. My child was once prescribed antibiotics without enough doses to complete the course and I was told that “missing a few doses won’t matter.” This is unsafe advice and only corrected after I insisted. My daughter had a persistent cough for several months and attended multiple times, yet no appropriate referral or timely investigations were arranged. When she later developed fever and blood-stained sputum, an out-of-hours GP was clearly concerned and requested urgent investigations. Despite this, our concerns were dismissed the following day, my child was not properly examined, and I was given incorrect medical information. False reassurance when a child is coughing up blood is unacceptable. When I later requested an urgent private ENT referral due to ongoing bleeding, I was asked to pay a fee during a highly distressing situation, despite previously being told such referrals were not chargeable. The supervising GP did not attend to assess my child in person. Overall, I felt unheard, disrespected, and unsafe. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise patients—especially parents of young children—to seriously consider de-registering and seeking care elsewhere. IF ANYONE NOT TRUSTING ME PLEASE READ THE REVIEWS IN OTHER WEBSITE AND CQC REPORT

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Paris Pinglaux
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a 6cm ovarian cyst burst, had internal bleeding, and needed a blood transfusion. I needed urgent surgery. I ended up in A&E - called the GP a day or so later relaying my very worrying symptoms and A&Es findings (projectile vomiting, diarrhoea, unable to keep food/water/tablets down, excruciating pelvic and full body pain, falling in and out of consciousness, blood in urine). A GP told me it was ‘nerves’, and gave no explanation as to why my symptoms suddenly increased tenfold. I was refused anti-sickness tablets many times while dealing with the unbearable nausea and vomiting, because they can become addictive apparently. The pain was unbelievable, I had to take the maximum dosage of cocodamol a day, and that barely touched the sides. Rather than showing concern for the severity of my pain, nausea, and other symptoms, conversations around pain medications became interrogations regarding addiction. I had a large cyst that needed to be removed urgently. They should have heard my symptoms and flagged them as concerning. They should have contacted my NHS surgeon with those concerns, urging them to bring the surgery date forward. They should have spotted the signs and symptoms of a ruptured cyst. Instead of trying to understand what could be happening to cause these very severe symptoms, they did nothing but minimise and ignore my concerns, while refusing me medications that were saving me from ending my life due to the constant, excruciating pain. What exactly are these doctors trained in? How could you be a trained doctor and miss the signs of an ovarian cyst rupture, especially considering my suspected endometriosis? I felt that something was seriously wrong despite this, so I pursued private surgery. If I did not have the means to do that, as many do not, I may not be here now. I could have gone into sepsis, I could have developed blood clots, and god knows what else. Not only that, I also had samples necessary for a referral to gastroenterology go missing three times in a row, which is just bloody odd. I am still in unbelievable amounts of pain, and have ongoing symptoms. I spoke to the practice manager yesterday. I wanted to try to explain how deeply traumatic all of this has been for me. According to her, I should have contacted my surgeon and asked for the surgery to be moved forward, not the GP. Like ???? I didn’t know I had a cyst! That is why I went to my GP for help, so that they could flag this as a potential emergency, justify my concerns, and potentially get my surgery moved forward or flagged as urgent. I am not a doctor, I went to my GP because I had no idea what was going on in my body, I was unbelievably ill, and scared. Is that not what you are supposed to do? However, my concerns were minimised, and I was made to feel dramatic. So, I just kept suffering until I could finally be booked in for a private laparoscopy. I explained that my dad (also at the same practice) has stage four cancer, and recently my brother passed away too, so my mental and physical health are very poor. She wouldn’t let me finish and responded very unprofessionally. I can’t remember her exact words, but it was something along the lines of ‘don’t start that’ or ‘don’t go there’ because her father passed away and she had been through a lot too. Honestly, I was gobsmacked, still am. I don’t understand why she thought it appropriate to respond like that. It is her job, that she is paid for, to be the practice manager. I hoped she would listen to my concerns and understand how negligent the practice had been, but I suppose that would be an admission of guilt. I am 24. I haven’t even managed to graduate university yet because of how much I have had to go through. All I want is to be healthy! I have been living a nightmare, and this practice has only made it harder. The doctors that work there traumatised me. If you do choose to join this practice, ask for doctor Nisha. She is truly lovely. The rest are incompetent.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a very distressing experience with Dr Tse Belmond and feel it is important to share this for transparency. I attended an appointment following a panic attack. As English is not my first language, I brought my partner for support. During the consultation, my partner was dismissed and interrupted, and I was pressured to speak despite being visibly distressed. I was prompted to discuss a traumatic experience, which caused me to become extremely upset. Throughout this, I was not offered reassurance or support, and the lack of empathy was noticeable. At a later appointment, I raised concerns about possible Autism and requested an assessment. This was met with a dismissive response, including laughing, and statements were made that Autism is rare in women and predominantly affects men. I found this response unprofessional and not in line with current understanding. I also have concerns about how suicidal thoughts I disclosed were recorded, as they were documented as “depressed mood – minor,” which did not reflect the seriousness of what was discussed. Overall, I left feeling unheard, belittled, and unsafe. I would not feel comfortable seeing this doctor again and would advise others to be cautious.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Gaz W
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Lack of compassion. Lack of professionalism. Lack of empathy. Arrogance. Rudeness. Failing of DPA. Ignorance. This all starts at the reception area. The ladies normally treat their patients like dirt. Very unhelpful with a “tough*” kind of attitude. Every other practice seems to work fine and use common sense, not Silverdale. For some reason you can’t book an appt using the My GP app for Silverdale, but other practices... no problem. You can call after 9am at most practices and book an appt for a GP.... not Silverdale. The poor service then trickles down to the GPs. I feel rushed. I feel things are not explained clearly. I feel they are more interested in hitting targets than curing the sick. Of course it all depends on the GP. I feel some GPs don’t listen to your needs, ailments or feelings and make massive assumptions and with any reason can’t wait to fob you off to a physio or hospital. I have been visiting this practice ALL MY LIFE. It has declined steadily and then rapidly. So after ringing up to book an appt with my GP for a later date, I’ve now been told I need to ring at 8am tomorrow.... WHY??? What difference does it make? Not only was I told this, it’s the arrogance and unhelpful attitude from the jumped up receptionist that is making me seriously consider switch GP. I’d you’re not registered with a practice, don’t bother with this one. It’s very amateur from top to bottom and the care no longer exists towards patients. UPDATE: what a mess. They are changing their system now. I’m certain this joke of a practice is making it deliberately hard for patients to speak to someone or make an appt. They even send texts saying “you have an appt on 02/09 at 2pm, this could be a phone or face to face appt, please contact the surgery for clarification on which it is” - WHY NOT TELL US IN THE TEXT?!? My god, this surgery was better in the 80s before we had computers and apps. I don’t think I’ve seen my GP face to face for 5 years. Absolute joke. UPDATE: after being told Curtis the physio is off sick AGAIN, I was asked to call to rebook an appt. Rang up and said I can’t do the rest of today as going to work. The lady said the nurse will be informed and call me to make an alternate appt. I got the call “we have appointments free all day with a GP” she said, I explained that I’d already said I can’t do this. I did however say, I can make a u turn now and come and see you “oh, we are booked up till 10:30” - the lady literally just told me they had a full free day?!? I eventually settled on 12:30 the following day. My text comes through to say my appt is 4:30pm the following day?!? I’m now sat here at 5pm and still not been seen to. This practice is a farce. No doubt I will get the usual reply from the practice manager where she takes no accountability nor responsibility for how dreadful Silverdale has become.

I don’t mind getting a call in the morning but nobody has made me aware the calls are made in the morning from 7am to what the doctor has stated via telephone today . When I called to make an appointment I have mentioned to the receptionist that I am not sure whether I need a call or a face to face appointment and clearly have stated what my problem is. The doctor called and said that I would need to a face to face appointment to get examined. Which I felt that I have wasted my time because with the pain that I have I could have been seen today and maybe the doctor could see my problem because the pain that I have is not always there. Which means I am not sure when I will get face to face appointment as it’s Thursday today and to get a face to face appointment would be slightly longer (possibly next week) which means I am not sure if I will still be in pain at the time of when I get seen face to face. Also for the doctor to say that even if we do all investigation referrals ect I should expect for the problem not to be solved and that possibly I will be on long term painkiller depending on the specialists will say. Now from the time that I was registered at this doctors, until now I was actually thinking that this practice and doctors are very caring towards their patients, I don’t mean by just solving the problems and providing medicine . But I would definitely except for the doctor to be more caring of how they speak to the patients too , that is part of the care too. I defiantly wasn’t asking Dr Cheema about what I expected or about my expectations were, when I see the specialist . This is not what I expect from the doctor at all. We are all humans a despite I have this is an on going problem and still nothing is found and this is not a blame at the GP. But it s really upsetting and as a person I am very worried about my health, but for the doctor to kind of tell me off about my expectations that I didn’t even ask about is a bit wrong and for the first time I felt that the conversation with the doctor was not caring towards me. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: deborah browne
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Towards the end of last year, I witnessed what I can only describe as a master class in customer service. I was waiting to collect something, as I noted Michelle take over a phone call from a younger receptionist, it appeared to be a difficult phone call. I moved away and took a seat. I couldn’t hear the caller, but from the time it took, and response by Michelle, I could tell that it took a lot of patience and calmness. There was a lot of warmth and empathy, and when Michelle finished, she introduced me to the younger new receptionist. I said to her take it from me you are learning from one of the best, and from what i observed, that was a master class in customer service. I think we forget that the front line staff in any medical centre, whether it is on the phone or face to face, do an extremely good job, and are faced with a lot of difficulties along the way, and are blamed constantly for things that are beyond their control. I know the Limes staff well, and they are all really hardworking and caring individuals. Please remember they are all doing their jobs, to the best of their abilities, and going through the same pressures of everyday life, as every one of us.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Tracey Fowler
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I, and all my family have been lucky enough to be a patient at Elliott Street Surgery for over 44 years, and the level of care we receive has always been outstanding. It has never failed to be anything less than 100%. I want to express my deepest gratitude to Dr Shah and the team for the outstanding care and support provided lately especially to my Mum following her recent operation when she fell downstairs and broke her Femur bone. When Mum was finally discharged to bed rest at home, from Hospital after a new days, she was complaining that the feet were sore I thought she could be developing bed sores, I called the Surgery at 5.00pm, and the next day at 9.00am a Nurse called to examine Mum when she put us at ease and luckily, it was not bed sores! A week later I was worried about Mum again as her good leg swelled extremely fast at the foot and doubled in size - so I called the Surgery and I was called back within 5 minutes to say the Practice was closing in 30 minutes but Dr Shah would personally visit Mum on his way home and he did within 40 minutes, the door bell rang and Dr Shah was stood waiting to see Mum – I initially thought she had a blood clot in her leg, Dr Shah thoroughly examined her for over 10 minutes and explained things to us in great depth, he explained the swelling could be just because she has had the operation and was bed bound and not able to walk and be mobile, that was one scenario or, it could be water retention and a few other scenarios were discussed too. Dr Shah advised he would send a Nurse to collect Mums bloods the next day to see what the bloods revealed if anything. The next day, sure as his word a nurse attended to see Mum – bloods were taken and sent off. The next day we were called that evening by Dr Shah to say the results had not come back yet and he would call us the next day. That evening a Locum GP Called and said the bloods were elevated and we needed to go for a scan an appointment was made for 2 days later. That day, Dr Shah called to discuss Mums blood results, and I explained what had happened. Anyway, as a precautionary measure, a scan internally and Mum - no clot Dr Shah and all the staff, have always taken the time to listen carefully, explain everything clearly, and make sure we all felt reassured at every stage of Mums recovery. Nothing ever felt rushed and every concern — big or small — was treated with genuine care. It’s rare to find someone who combines medical expertise with such kindness and patience. Thanks to their guidance, my mum has felt safe, supported, and confident throughout her healing process. We are incredibly grateful for the dedication and humanity shown during what could have been a very stressful time. The team ALWAYS go above and beyond to make patients feel heard and supported and welcome, even during busy periods. They are exceedingly compassionate. The Practice is also great for reminding you that you need to see the nurses for check-ups and also medication reviews etc. Another point I wish to make is they have been great with Mum as she has smoked for 68 years, and the Practice now supports her with patches so to my amazement, she has not smoked for over 2 months The reception staff deserve special recognition too. Their kindness sets the tone from the moment you walk through the door. This review seems mainly to be about my Mums care at this difficult chapter in our lives but when I or any of family ever need to see the Doctors, everything is always made so easy with so much empathy. I have never in 44 years experienced anything negative from the Practice. Our Community Practice is a true example of what excellent healthcare should look like. Again, I’m incredibly grateful for the dedication and hard work of the entire team. I would 100% Highly recommended. My final thought… In a time when NHS services are under pressure, this practice stands out as a true asset to the area. I feel fortunate to have such exceptional care right on my doorstep. Thank you, Dr Shah and your Wonderful Team x,

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Neil Shepherd
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Avoid this practice if at all possible. I have been registered with the practice for 13 years and initially all was great. Currently, every time I have to deal with them, something goes wrong causing stress and anxiety when help is needed most. I was sent to get bloods elsewhere and when I attended the appointment I was told that the surgery should have given me some paperwork which they hadn't. I called in on my way home and was told "of course you need paperwork" as though it was my fault. The text they sent confirming the appointment stated I didn't need any paperwork. I wasn't even aware what the test was for as there was no other contact. They recently put me on medication for high blood pressure. Initially, the "GP" I saw put me on a drug which caused my ankles to swell so I asked if it could be changed. Their remote clinical pharmacist changed the drug but when I read the leaflet, it stated that it shouldn't be taken by anyone on anti-fungal medication, which I am. Another drug was prescribed and sent to a different pharmacy. When I went to the pharmacy stated, they said they hadn't got the prescription as it had been sent to another pharmacy which was closed, so I was without the medication for 3 days. I have been sent another appointment with the clinical pharmacist for next week. The times don't fit around my work so I called in to ask for a later call and was refused. Dr Archer agreed I could have a flu jab due my lung condition. An appointment was made for this on the same day I went for a kidney function blood test and I was told I could have it at the same time. The phlebotomist was about to take bloods for a test she had already done about 4 weeks ago until I told her it was a kidney function test and informed her that I had been told that I could have a flu jab at the same time. Her response wasn't good, but suffice to say she didn't do it stating that she was thinking of retiring due to the stress that the admin team were putting her under. I went to reception and was told "no, you can't have a flu jab as you're not old enough". I really do think that this practice has gone downhill which is a great shame as I used to sing the praises of all the staff. I hope Dr Archer reads this and takes some action as some of the staff are rude, ignorant, uncaring and more importantly following unsafe practices. Not what you want from a GP surgery. I am quite willing to discuss things further with him if he wishes to call me. I am currently looking for another practice hoping things will be better there. In the meantime, if I can be bothered I am seriously thinking about contacting CQC. Avoid Avoid Avoid

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: PC Mumble
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am updating my review because after speaking to various friends who visit other GP surgeries across Trafford, I appear to be quite lucky with Washway Road. My friends have awful problems getting someone to pick up a phone, they're always number 20+ in the queue, they can't get an appointment. I rarely have to wait to speak to a receptionist, they have some lovely ones who answer the phones these days, very helpful. I have had some very pleasant experiences and interactions with both admin staff and GPs over the last 6 months so I actually cannot complain. The AskMyGP system seems to work well now they have changed it to logging a request between 8 and 10, it's no longer a race to get your request in before it closes/gets full. The on site pharmacist is very good, he can resolve a lot of medication queries so you don't have to wait to see a GP. ******* GPs do not take women's pain seriously. Was ignored and told that 3 periods in a month was absolutely nothing to worry about and was offered a flu jab instead. Completely uninterested so had to go private and seek a second opinion. Currently recovering from a total hysterectomy inc. ovaries and removal of severe stage 4 endometriosis. I also had Adenomyosis. When I wrote to advise them of this, they couldn't even be bothered acknowledging me. This practice has gone totally downhill in the last year or so. Utter disgrace. Edit - it's worth noting this same review was rejected by the NHS website 'because it includes a serious complaint about a specific practice'. So do not trust their NHS review score.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Abigail Awoyeye
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a very distressing experience at Medlock Medical Practice. I arrived on time for my blood test and waited as instructed, while several patients who arrived after me were seen first. After over 20 minutes, I calmly approached reception to ask for reassurance, as I was worried I had been forgotten. I am currently receiving treatment for anxiety and depression. Instead of reassurance, I was spoken to harshly and repeatedly called “rude” in front of other patients. English is not my first language, and I believe there was a misunderstanding, but my attempt to explain was dismissed. I was left feeling humiliated and extremely distressed and broke down in tears during my appointment. I would strongly encourage the practice to provide staff with additional training in compassionate communication, mental health awareness, and supporting patients with language barriers. Healthcare settings should feel safe and supportive, especially for vulnerable patients. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

I feel like I am completely not only listened to but also understood. Dr Khalid has been so amazing, she is truly beautiful inside and out. I actually can’t believe she is going to be leaving us soon. Medlock managers can we not get a petition to keep her with you. From a Woman’s perspective and please don’t take this in anyway than how it is intended, it has been refreshing to have a woman treat me who is so respectful of age and how our body reacts to it. Thank you Dr Khalid so much for your help, understanding and commitment to me as a patient. You will be so missed and a blessing to another practice.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Made an appointment for 3.10pm yesterday (12th November 2025) arrived at 2.55pm in plenty of time which i always do. Spoke to the receptionist (not sure of her name) she advised me of what waiting room to go to. Half hour after my appointment. I'm still sitting there, watching people come in after me and being seen before me. I didn't want to leave the waiting are as I was on my own, just in case my name was called. 2 hours later (to which I think another patient may have informed the reception desk) I was still there. She asked me to the desk. To my knowledge I was booked in She told me I had been put down as a non attendee. Apologised, then said they had been having problems with the computer system. To which I said obviously not, its the person inputting/working the computer. As I had seen approximately 7-10 people arrive after me and go in before me. So to me that's not a computer error, its a human error. She said I would have to come back tomorrow. I said absolutely not as I work early mornings, and could the doctor see me now as he finishes his shift at 5pm (it was 4.50pm) absolute sham. Luckily, for them to basically save face, I imagine. The doctor said he would see me.

The reception staff are lovely however the doctors, nurse practitioner don't seem to care whatsoever ever. In January after a visit to the GP I was given incorrect medication. After the issue was no better I went back, I was told by the GP the 1st GP was wrong. They gave me different medication. After 2 days and getting worse. I presented yo A&E and was kept on for 5nights. Being told each step of the way the GP was wrong. I should have been referred to podiatry on the first visit. The second I should have been sent to hospital... If I followed their guidance any further, I could have lost toes/feet. After hospital admission, I was sensitive to the medication so rang the GP to change it. They advised that technically I don't need medication anymore as I have had a course. Without even seeing me. But I did. That was my treatment plan from my discharge from hospital. This surgery completely exasperate medical conditions unnecessarily. It's almost like doctors don't care anymore.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Anish
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I’ve recently joined New Islington Medical Practice as I started to take more responsibility for my health issues, which lingered over the years. I’ve had a 10/10 experience through every consultation and clinician I’ve encountered so far. The facilities are clean and modern, and the reception/back office staff have been very polite and prompt in responses. The new appointment booking system has been very efficient. Having many personal/professional experiences at other GP practices as a GP doctor myself - I have to say New Islington Medical Practice is by far one of the best that I’ve encountered within the region. The waiting times are optimal. I’ve had multiple health issues which have either been resolved or I am now receiving further support for. For sensitive issues, the clinicians are non-judgemental and empathetic in their approach which makes a huge difference. Kudos to Dee and management for their successes thus far and keep up the great work.

The receptionist a lady is very very rude. Things need to change as they are not getting things done properly and efficient. If you’re sick that day you need an appointment and you can’t get it then you have to ring back the next day. I rang today to speak to Dr Zak toon make an appointment and he wasn’t in after I was told the other day that he’s back off his annual leave the staff. Do not care if they don’t like their job tell them to leave. I’ve read the reviews and it’s the same thing with the same receptionist over and over again. I’m an army veteran who suffers with PTSD anxiety night terrors. I have one leg and I’m trying to get my health back on track. Dr Zach is helping me but the receptionists are unprofessional. It feels that tbe lives and wellbeing of patients don’t matter its just a number. Very disappointed.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Dannie J
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I've been here for my whole life, I used to give 1 star but I do believe some aspects of the surgery have changed in recent years which is why I changed to a 3. A lot of the doctors here are absolutely lovely and compassionate (especially with mental health) and I cannot fault them on how they have cared for me - for this I would like to give a special mention to Dr Graham and Dr Duncan (this could be due to how recent they qualified as a GP and there now being more awareness of mental health). For anything fertility related Dr Wareing is next to none also! Dr Heron I've struggled with for years due to past experiences and I will not see him, however in pregnancy he has been decent which shows he does take SOME things seriously and is willing to help. The prescription service is very fast and all of my repeats have normally been approved and sent within an hour of requesting. I thought the reception staff had improved over the last year or so however recently they have gone back downhill and are back to being the stereotypical NHS dragons on reception who refuse to help or even acknowledge you past 9.01am when the slots are full - I have even had a GP apologise for this! However it must be said that for me the real star of the show in primrose is Nurse Sharon! She is one of the most kind and compassionate people you could ever meet and I'm sure anyone who has ever crossed paths with her would agree!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: john jowett
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I contacted Primrose yesterday 19/11/2024, through askmygp. I told the surgery that I had strained my neck, shoulder and bicep carrying a TV box. I told them that I was in excruciating pain and that I was hardly getting any sleep and asked for help and that I needed to see a doctor and needed some sort of strong prescription medication. I got a call from there reception and told the caller that the pain I was experiencing was unbearable. She said she'd pass it on to 'the doctor' whoever that was supposed to be. Then I got a call back telling me that the 'doctor' wanted me to go for physio. I had politely stated how horrendous the pain was. Got told I'd get a call the following afternoon from their pharmacist. I couldn't go through another 24+ hours suffering this agony. So I went to TGH., walk- in clinic and was seen in & out within 1.5 hours, with strong pain killers and advised on three exercises to carry out. Primrose, in my opinion on this matter we're terrible. No empathy or help for my medical problem from primrose. Very dissatisfied on this occasion.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Janet L
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Unacceptable and impersonal service especially when using the Ask My GP website. If these requests are not seen by clinicians how can patients be confident that the staff who are triaging them are sufficiently medically trained to judge whether a patient needs advice/help from a GP. I was advised by way of an impersonal on line response to an Ask My GP request to contact a pharmacy. When I did this I was then asked if I had contacted 111. How many hoops do patients have to jump through to be able to get help? Left in pain with a possible infection. It makes one wonder when you read media reports of patients who have ended up with sepsis or worse whether this is the right approach; I don't think so.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Robin Sumner
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Second class teatment which was a let down

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Dan
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: If I could give 0 stars if I could. I was born in Urmston and was at Urmston Group Practice til late teenage years, moved around and came back and signed back up. It's not the same doctors surgery that we used to know and love on Church Road. The receptionists need to go on a humility and compassion training course because their actions or there lack of are directly affecting peoples health and mental health. The receptionists also like to try and It seems to be a common theme that one or two of the receptionists (not all) do not seem to have any level of care or sympathy towards their patients. They forced me into crisis because I missed a phone appointment at 18:30 when my appointment was supposed to be 14:45. Apparently they tried to call me twice but number was dead. I know this to be untrue because not only did I not get any notifications that they tried to call but I also have a voicemail as well and they could have left a message. So when I call the next day )which was a friday) to find out what's happened and if I was going to have an appointment then rather than the one that didn't happen the day before. I was met with the usual "you've got to make an appointment, you'll have to call on monday" Despite the fact it was mental health tablets that I needed a review on, for them to use a poor excuse of "it didn't go through" when my phone is connected to wifi calls as well. I was so upset after it all I just told the woman if they aren't going to take me seriously I'll do something serious for them to take notice. No call back, no duty of care, no safeguarding, no making sure I wasn't going to do anything stupid. NOTHING. Then I received a very SNOTTY letter from the practice basically telling me off for saying what I said to the receptionist without even acknowledging that had they of cared or done their jobs, I wouldn't have been in meltdown mode and said what I said. So off the back of that, I have sent a complaint to them TWICE about the whole disgrace of a situation and I have yet to hear from them. Not even an acknowledgement. This review is my last hope that they see this and reply to me because if they don't then I'm going to go above their heads as it's becoming a joke at this point. Business are expected to acknowledge a complaint within 3 days and set out within that acknowledgement a time frame of when I should hear back from them. It's been months.

Obviously dislikes her job, but poor patients should not be at the receiving end of this. Of course my query was not resolved and I was blamed for that as well. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Humairaa Ahmed
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had an appointment today at 11:40 for an ultrasound scan which I had to have a full bladder for. I took a taxi to the place but as the taxi driver went the wrong way, by the time I got through to the centre was 11:43 and I explained to the receptionist that I’ll be 5 minutes. She said that was fine. I arrived at 11:50 and sat in the waiting area waiting for my ultrasound. When I arrived, was only 1 woman I saw go in and come out 10 minutes later. After that it was just me sitting there waiting. Nearly 20 minutes had gone by so I ask the receptionist. She said I am half an hour late and how I said I’ll be 5 minutes and that they won’t see me , even though I walked in passed reception at 11:50 to sit in the waiting area which was by the ultrasound scan room. I explained myself. Then she said okay just continue waiting. 25 minutes later the person at the ultrasound came out for me and explained how I’m too late and she can’t fit me in. Even though I’m the only one there and have been for the past 35 minutes. She said she’s been calling for me. No one called for me at all whilst I was there. Whatever I was telling her wasn’t going through to her at all. So after sitting there for nearly 45 minutes on a full bladder that I’ve had for 2 hours, I got sent home and a phone call after to re arrange. No thanks I would rather not have the scan anymore to find the issue of what’s making me ill rather than dealing with people like this. And bare in mind whilst I was waiting, one woman kept coming in and out of the room ‘checking around’ but never called my name or spoke to me. Wish I could give this place 0 stars

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: sophie butler
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Where to start? Half of the doctors don't listen, are rude, belittling and sexist and will just laugh at your problems or refuse to make referrals even if they can't treat you. If you want names- Dr Lyburn is extremely rude, condescending and just generally vile. Dr Badesha literally laughed at me over my skin problems. All the good doctors like Dr Ash seem to leave the practice. Most of the receptionist staff are extremely rude, then do their best to block you from making complaints. One of them tried to force me to give a personal reason for my visit to the GP and when I refused, I was refused an appointment. I was then gaslit by two reception staff over what happened. But I know for a fact phone calls are recorded so maybe they should start listening back to them if there is any confusion in their minds about what has happened. The practice constantly mess me around with my medication, saying they haven't received emails from my mental health team when they have clearly been sent. I have been left without medication and left on too low of a dose because of this. I will say the nurses are lovely and I don't take issue with any of them but unfortunately this isn't enough for me to stay at Sorrel Bank. Please find a different doctors practice if you are considering registering with this one, it's not worth it. I will be making a huge complaint about my treatment and then moving my whole family to a different GP practice. Edit: you will be able to see that the practice reponded to me suggesting I arrange an appointment with the practice manager. I did this. Practice manager did not bother to respond

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Anon Anon
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have been a patient at this surgery and Dr Kassam for many years. I never had any issues before but in the last 6 months it has been terrible service. I order my monthly prescriptions through the chemist as required by the surgery and I repeatedly have medication missed, which is my diabetic insulin! I have to phone monthly to chase this up with the reception team and I get a response that it has not been requested and they will put through now and will take another 48 hours. I am being left without the insulin for a day or 2 and this is becoming a concern. I have raised a concern in the last month and I got attitude from the ‘assistant manger’ which i find her approach very unprofessional and like she doesn’t want to be bothered. The practice manager is never on site to raise a complaint to and told to put in writing which I have and never got a reply from Patrick neither. I am going to have to transfer out as the care we are receiving is very concerning if I can not get my monthly medication at time when requested in time frame. The Reception team seem to be new and need training on how to request a prescription or get competent staff. This is a shame because for the past many years I have always been cared for and not had many issues as I know mistakes do happen, but this surgery has gone down hill.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Jeremiah Agenyi
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am disappointed with the level of service I have received from Mocha Parade Medical Practice. I visited their center to get registered when I first arrived in the UK, and they promised to get back to me in a few days. However, I did not hear from them after two weeks, so I reached out to them. They said that they could not find my records and asked me to register again. I did so, but I still did not hear back from them after another two to three weeks. When I contacted them again, they said that my records had been misplaced. I then submitted my records online, but it has been almost three months and I have still not heard back from them. I am concerned about the level of care I will receive if I need medical attention from this practice. I am also disappointed with the lack of communication and the apparent negligence of the staff. I would not recommend this practice to anyone.

From receptionist, practice management, pharmacists, Doctors. All polite, friendly, helpful and most importantly, professional. I would implore anyone using this practices wonderful services treat them the same. Of course problems arise and mistakes get made, but keep calm and this team will help find the best solution. I am happy to recommend this surgery to anyone.

The building and waiting areas were very clean and tidy and the free Car Park next to the building , which isn't the case at many doctors, was a blessing in the rain, as was the easy to use tablet device to register your vehicle for the parking pass. I wouldn't want to judge some of the previous comments as everyone can have a bad day and ill health can affect perceptions, but I've been to a lot worse Surgeries, this was a pleasure to visit today.

I signed in as soon as I got there and waited for 20 minutes before asking the receptionist how long roughly the wait was as I was the only one sitting there in the waiting room. All she did was ignore my question so I asked again and she said she can't tell me so I was left to wait while I was in a massive rush. It would have made it ALOT easier had the receptionist told me roughly how long I will need to wait. I ended up waiting another 20 minutes and saw that no one was calling me so I had to go. I decided that I was going to call the surgery again and speak to the doctor to tell her that I was in a big rush when I came in and had to leave and if we could reschedule the appointment. I was left waiting for very long before the receptionist finally answered my call and said that the doctor has finished for the day and that she can not transfer me over to her. I wondered how the doctor can finish afew hours before the practice closes but I never said anything and hung up! Around 15 minutes later the doctor tried calling me but unfortunately my phone was in silent so I never heard the calls.. I thought the receptionist told me she had finished for the day?? I have no complaints at the doctor they are directed at the receptionist who was very rude and made it extremely difficult for me and has left me now with no appointment and I am very unimpressed and unhappy!
