recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eugene Friday
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Absolutely ridiculous experience. Unprofessional staff. Arrived 10 mins early for my appoitment which was supposed to be 10:40 am, only to discover that their free parking was completely full, forcing me to find a paid parking elsewhere. I paid for 30 mins until 11:05 am but I wasn't called in the given timeframe. Thus, I had to extend my parking. I immediately informed the receptionist and asked them to let the doctor know that I needed extra few minutes to extend my parking. But they dismissed my notice and informed the receptionist that they wouldn't wait and asked to book a new appointment. Instead of showing basic courtesy, they just refused to wait extra couple of minutes, despite the fact that they were 25 mins running behind. So somehow it's acceptable for them to be late but the patients get penalised for circumstances entirely out of their control. If you expect punctuality, maybe start by managing your schedule and facilities properly. I won't be returning and wouldn't recommend this medical practice to anyone.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: ENGLISH WITH SABBIR
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Terrible Experience at NHS GP Practice The Absolute Worst I am writing this review to express my extreme dissatisfaction with Dr. Parkin's NHS GP practice. This practice is, without a doubt, the worst healthcare experience I've ever had. Here's a list of my grievances: Unbelievably Long Wait Times: Getting an appointment is a nightmare. Even after securing one, expect to wait in the waiting room. Unprofessional Doctors: I've had appointments with various doctors , and none have instilled confidence. They seem unconcerned about my health problems. I would recommend looking for alternative GP practices in the area. There must be better options out there with qualified professionals who genuinely care about their patients' well-being. If you're looking for a GP experience that will leave you feeling more unwell than when you arrived, then NHS is the place for you! Buckle up, because this is a tale of woe. Getting There is an Odyssey: Firstly, reaching a human to book an appointment is an act of pure masochism. The phone lines are permanently engaged in a game of dial tone torture, and the online system is about as user-friendly as a medieval trebuchet. Finally, you're ushered into the office. Prepare for a five-minute consultation. Don't expect in-depth examinations or thoughtful diagnoses. Here, a generic prescription pad are your only companions. I understand that the NHS is under a lot of strain, but that doesn't excuse the unprofessional and unacceptable service.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Amelia A
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I brought my daughter for an appointment and we were kept waiting 30 minutes past our scheduled time. When we were finally called in, we were then left to stand in silence for another 5 minutes while doctor Hassan typed notes from previous patients. While still typing and without making eye contact or examining my daughter, he asked why we were there. When I explained it was for a spot on her leg and that she’d had it for a few months, he immediately made a judgment and said it “must not be much of an issue” if we’d waited that long. He also commented that “they will ask why you haven’t brought her in for months” without explaining who “they” were, and before he had even looked at the spot. Only after making these remarks did he finally examine her leg and then told us it wasn’t serious and to return in two weeks with warm compresses. My concern isn’t the medical advice itself it’s the rude, dismissive, and judgmental manner, particularly when speaking to a parent about their child. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated experience. We have experienced similar rudeness from this doctor on multiple occasions. Between the repeated unprofessional behaviour, poor communication, and lack of respect for patients’ time, this is not a practice I feel comfortable bringing my children to, and I would not recommend it to other parents.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: L B
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: GP's and Nurses are brilliant. Always friendly and easy to talk to. Both nurses I've seen there have been bubbly, happy and chatty and put me at ease, even when having a cervical screening :') One of the reception staff comes across very rude on the phone at times which isn't great when you're ringing up about mental health issues. She has at other times when I've physically been in the surgery been fantastic and extremely helpful. I can sympathise with them to an extent as they must get a lot of abuse but it shouldn't be pushed onto others. When you're physically in the building though they're all spot on. Struggle to get through and get appointments if you don't keep trying to ring at 08:00. They do seem to have introduced a phone queuing system which helps massively. With there only being a limited amount of appointments I think the reception staff need to be firmer in turning time wasters away and directing them to the correct place (pharmacy/a&e/self care). Also, they should tell people who repeatedly don't attend their appointments and dont have the decency to advise reception they will be struck off if they don't have a valid reason. Surgery is bright, airy and clean. Chairs could do with being spread out a bit more in my opinion but I'm claustrophobic so perhaps a bit biased. Overall, best doctors surgery I've been too in Heywood and I would recommend. All surgeries seem equally difficult to get appointments so can't hold that against them. As for the occasionally rude receptionist, this is just my experience and how I perceive something that's been said and that will differ from person to person. We all have bad days, we're only human :)

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Keira Altimas
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Not had a great experience with this practice except for the help from 3 outstanding doctors Dr Hulme, Dr Shula & Dr Asad have been a life saver! I have had to make the decision to report this practice to the CQC and local inter grated care board and patient services team due to being treated appallingly as I have been treated extremely unfairly due to having a severe mental health illness and then being given a ‘warning letter’ due to receptionists assuming I am ringing about this ‘condition’ and approaching me in a rude and unfair manner to which with me only being human reacting in a fair manner it’s disgusting to just assume my appointments are solely for that. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Alex R

The admin staff taking the information are well trained and have clearly got some sort of triage system in place. When having a GP phonecall the worst part is waiting for the call but if during the call with the Dr they feel they need to see you they have always been prompt in getting me to come in for an examination. They were really supportive during my pregnancy and since the birth of my child a couple of years ago I've never had a problem getting him an appointment when he has been poorly.

The practice also fails to respond properly to complaints, leaving parents without answers or accountability. I have also personally experienced significant delays and poor communication when trying to get urgent care and test results. Repeated failures like this put patients’ health at risk. I was issued a sick note and sent on my way .I left the appointment feeling worse than when I arrived. I was later referred for further care however, this referral was not completed for several months because the doctor was reportedly off sick and no alternative arrangements were made. I find this particularly concerning, as I received a message from the receptionist regarding the referral shortly after the initial appointment, yet no action followed. Overall, the lack of compassion, poor communication, and delays in care have been distressing. I would strongly advise anyone who needs medical support to consider a different practice. My experience has been extremely disappointing. I will be changing doctors ASAP .

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Update: that online form is pointless. Takes a week for them to get back to you. The only way of getting sorted if you ring them up and kick off. So if there is something wrong with me ill probably be dead by the time I speak to some one. Sent online form asking GP to up my dosage of medication. Got a text saying everything has been sorted. 8 months later after being on said dosage, my records said i was on a much lower dose. In 12 months since arriving the standard of care for them has been amazing. I have had to book two appointments for myself also and the care from Fran who I think is a senior practice nurse at the Saddleworth practice and very recently the senior practice nurse at Delph surgery ( sorry the ladies name has slipped my mind) was fantastic on both occasions. Appointments have been arranged quickly and efficiently. Thank you😃

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Martha Beatriz Potter
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I'm writing this review as a frustrated patient who's had a shocking experience with this practice's service. I phoned at 8am and waited 25-30 minutes just to get an answer. I explained my situation - my consultant had asked them to prescribe more antibiotics for my lung disease, which makes any cold or flu linger and often leads to infections, making me cough uncontrollably and causing incontinence. It's a nightmare. The response seemed straightforward when I spoke to them, but then I got a call an hour later saying I needed to fill in an online form to be triaged. A nice lady helped me with this, but then... nothing. I phoned again at 2pm, was told they'd contact me, and... crickets. It's now 6:47pm. The worst part? This isn't the first time this has happened. I've ended up in A&E twice because their system is so appalling, and both times I've been told "this is something the GP deals with". I rarely use their service, but when I do, it's usually to be told to go to A&E or a walk-in centre. It's infuriating. To anyone considering using this practice, be warned: their system is broken, and it might end up costing you a trip to hospital. Not exactly what you want when you're already feeling well.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Alison Horsfall

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Barry
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Having recently had a medical issue whilst abroad I was advised to contact my Medical Practice at home. I have been a patient at Greenbank since the 1960s fortunately I have not had to attend on a regular basis however I was pleased to be given a prompt appointment and saw a doctor who was most pleasant and professional and was able to fully interpret the advice I had received whilst abroad. She arranged for me to have an ECG which was done within a week at Greenbank by an equally pleasant and professional person. The results of the ECG were conveyed to me later that day by the the doctor who saw me initiallly and she organised for me to see a specialist at Oldham Hospital within days. I remember that a few years ago I read in the local paper a review of the Greenbank Practice which was rather poor, however after contacting Greenbank I was given the opportunity, a few weeks later, to meet with the leader of the group who had produced that report which illustrated how easy it is to criticise particularly over petty issues. The second follow up report a few months later recognised the true value of the Greenbank practice and the practice was marked up as Good. I have also had recent visits to see the physio at Greenbank with my slight hip problem and again I received prompt and professional help. My golf is just as bad however my hip is on the mend.

I arrived early to the appointment, but the staff appeared to be preparing to close, despite the clinic not due to shut for another 30 minutes. The lights were off and cleaning staff were already present. When I explained that I had an appointment, the staff seemed confused and told me there were no appointments left for the day. I was questioned in a rather patronising manner about whether I was in the correct place or had the right day, but no one asked for my name or referral details, which surely would have been the most basic step in checking their system and clarifying the situation. I was ultimately turned away without any attempt to investigate further. I contacted my GP the next morning and they confirmed that the appointment had been correctly booked. I am unclear what went wrong, but it is frustrating to now have to rearrange the appointment and potentially take additional time off work.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Madara Luste
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: If I could give 0 stars, I would. Their incompetence and medical negligence is just unbelievable. Every time I raise a health concern they are just absolutely not interested. I went to seek help with heavy periods. DR Saraf just looked at me and said "what do you want me to do about it?" in the most condescending way possible. Her solution then was to put me on a mini pill. Without once checking my blood pressure before prescribing it or at any point during the 10 months I was on it. Result? I now have to take blood pressure medication for the rest of my life, it's affected my vision and I will need to see a cardiologist once a year for a foreseeable future. Are these meds being reviewed to make sure they are working? Of course not! I also have iron deficiency, due to the heavy periods. Was promised regular blood tests to make sure the levels stay in range. Upon the last request to have them checked I've just had the answer of "they were fine 5 months ago so no need to check" when I had clearly stated I'm getting the same symptoms as the time before when they were extremely low! Communication? Well, now you submit an online form to get an appointment. So far I've submitted 3. 2 got completely no reply. And the 3rd one featured a generic link with no option to respond or raise any further concerns. I could go on about the lack of care and unprofessional attitude, but I genuinely don't believe they will change anything. To anyone considering joining this GP practice, just don't. Might do more harm to your health than good as it's been in my personal experience!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: John Gardner
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: As I approach my 79th summer, I seem to pop more pills than a 1960’s Rolling Stones roadie. Which takes quite a bit of organising in terms of ordering them from my local surgery to keep the supply line flowing. When it comes to being business-like in such matters, on a scale of 1-10, one being chaotic and ten being hyper-efficient, I probably clock in at something like minus 5. That is in contrast to the present Mrs Gardner, who could probably re-organise Manchester United in the morning and the England cricket team in the afternoon. Anyway, the New Year being what it was, I thought I had ordered two sets of tablets from Leesbrook surgery at the dawn of 2026 when the evidence indicates that, in point of fact, I hadn’t. Doh! When this dawned on me earlier today, panic set in for I had consumed my very last Solifenacin tablet last night. We are warned to give plenty of notice when re-ordering prescriptions, particularly at this time of year when the whole NHS is so stretched. So imagine my surprise, delight and admiration when my hasty message to Leesbrook surgery was answered immediately. Together with the ever helpful staff at Well Pharmacy, they arranged for me to have the required medication in my hands this very afternoon. Thank you once again for your brilliant service. Happy New Year from John Gardner

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Stacey MacNaught
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I appreciate that GP services are incredibly stretched and it can be very difficult to balance offering in advance routine appointments with more urgent on the day appointments. I think this surgery, however, is striking the balance well. The last 3 times I’ve required fairly urgently assessing, I was seen on the same day and treated. Early on this year, after a bout of pneumonia, I suffered a follow up chest infection. I was seen the same day, prescribed antibiotics and the doctor sent a sample from my chest off for testing. I got a call a few days later saying the bacteria on my chest wasn’t the commonly found one and as such would not respond to the antibiotics I was given and he had sent a new prescription to the pharmacy. So instead of seeing me, prescribing something and leaving me to it, the Doctor has followed up, sought more information and then realised my treatment would need changing. Despite the huge time constraints they’re under, they’re still doing a thorough job. I was again recently seen the same day with another potentially urgent requirement. The surgery also now accepts appointment request forms - categorised as urgent and non urgent so you don’t have to wait on the phone. Trying to get through on the phones can be frustrating for sure. But this is, in my view, a Solid example of a clinic that does the best with the resources it has, despite huge patient loads. And doesn’t cut corners on healthcare just to save time. Thorough, understanding and incredibly hard working is my experience of the admin and medical staff I’ve encountered here.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Michael Keating
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I felt that my health problems were dismissed and was disappointed and frustrated with the consultation overall. I had registered with the surgery for the GP to consider shared care protocol for ADHD medication prescribed and monitored by a private company I have paid for monthly since January 2025. I'd been advised by the receptionist prior to registering that this would at the least be considered. During my first consultation I was told indefinitely that the practice had a 'blanket rule' against prescribing in this manner. I would have accepted that, as I did with my previous practice, however I feel I was then delivered misinformation that was disheartening and upsetting. The GP told me that 'these private companies will give anybody a diagnosis of ADHD', something which I feel particularly upset and frustrated by. I know for a fact, as a specialist nurse for psychiatry working in primary care that there are many people referred for an ADHD assessment that are not diagnosed but offered alternatives and private companies will make recommendations based on valuable assessments that patients benefit from regardless. For a medical professional to deliver this false information can be especially damaging to somebody in my position, having waited years and paid excessively for support with. I, like many other service users have found relief and in the very least been validated by a diagnosis of ADHD which has answered a lot of questions and provided a pathway to improved wellbeing and hope for the future. The GP also stated that these private companies do not offer a true 'shared care' approach, and that if there are any problems with prescribing in primary care there is no support available from them. I know that this is also false as I have been instructed to remain under the care of the private company and pay for six monthly reviews from the specialists working alongside primary services to ensure safe prescribing and management of medications. The GP also attempted to misinform me that private companies prescribe medications without ensuring safe titration and effective physical health monitoring. Again, I know for a fact that I was sufficiently monitored in terms of bloods, ECG and regular blood pressure and weight reviews since being diagnosed with ADHD in January 2025. In summary, I feel Albion Medical Group have been negligent and failed to deliver individualised care based on service user need. Not only that, but many of the false statements assumed by the GP could have been particularly damaging to vulnerable people with a diagnosis of ADHD, further marginalising people like myself trying to seek support for this disability. If the surgery have a 'blanket rule' against considering shared care protocols for ADHD medication, they should at least ensure the GP's are better informed and work harder not to further dismiss and discredit patients already struggling to access safe support and guidance.

I asked the receptionist, who told me to “wait another 5–10 minutes and the doctor will see you soon.” After waiting another 10 minutes, she then told me I needed to come back four hours later at 3:30pm. What a joke. I had children to pick up from school, so attending four hours later was impossible. I asked if I could be booked in for the following week instead, and I was told they had no availability at all for the next two weeks. Completely unacceptable and honestly disgusting. To make matters worse, while I was there another patient was arguing with staff because the doctor refused to see her child despite them having an appointment as well. That alone shows this GP treats multiple patients the same way. This is not the first bad experience either. On previous occasions the staff have been extremely rude. When complaining over the phone in the past, I was told things like: “Why don’t you change GP?” “Why don’t you move out of Oldham?” Disgusting attitude. Completely unprofessional. Shows clearly that this GP surgery does not care at all about its patients. Little Town Medical Practice needs serious improvement. People rely on their GP for their health and wellbeing, and this kind of treatment is shameful. I would not recommend this surgery to anyone.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Ayanna
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am writing to formally raise serious concerns about the continued poor standard of care and service I have experienced at your practice, which has now reached an unacceptable level. I had a telephone appointment scheduled for today at 10:00 AM to discuss blood test results I have been waiting over two weeks for. The doctor called but let the phone ring for barely a second—so briefly that my phone did not even make a sound before the call ended. This happened twice. By the time I looked at my screen, both calls had already disconnected. It appears these calls were made purely to be logged as “missed” without any genuine effort to reach me. This is not the first time this has happened. During my previous set of blood tests, I experienced the exact same issue with the same doctor. It is becoming a pattern, and I feel unfairly blamed for missing calls that I was never given a fair chance to answer. I contacted reception immediately after the missed calls and was told by one receptionist that the doctor would call me again by 3:00 PM. I waited all afternoon and received no call. When I followed up again, a different receptionist informed me that I would now need to wait until Monday to rebook the appointment. This lack of consistency and the conflicting information from staff is extremely frustrating and unprofessional. Had I been advised at the time of my first call this morning that it was unlikely I would receive a call back, I would have rescheduled immediately while appointments were still available. Instead, I have been left waiting all day, only to be told I now need to start the process again next week. This entire experience follows an already distressing and, frankly, concerning blood test appointment. During the test, the nurse attempted to draw blood from my left arm but was unsuccessful. She then inserted the same needle into my right arm, again unsuccessfully, and a third time into another site using the same needle. I was left with severe bruising due to how aggressive the procedure was. Afterwards, I looked into this and was shocked to learn that reusing the same needle for multiple injection sites is not in line with health and safety regulations. I find it deeply troubling that this occurred, and it has left me feeling not only physically hurt but also incredibly unsafe in your care. All of this is part of a larger issue I have faced at this practice: I have repeatedly had to fight to have my symptoms taken seriously, and even getting basic follow-up care feels like a battle. The reception staff regularly provide conflicting, inaccurate, or vague advice, which only adds to the confusion and stress. At this point, I feel neglected and disrespected as a patient. I will be looking into registering with another GP practice, as I feel the standard of care at this one has significantly declined during my time here. I hope this matter is taken seriously, as it relates not just to poor service, but to potential breaches in clinical safety and patient care standards

Today during an appointment I told him how he was making me feel and he proceeded to tell me I was projecting and it was my issue and I shouldn't be placing it on him. I then expressed that I then felt I was being gaslighted to which he said he didn't know what I was talking about and it must be "one of these new social media terms" and I should just speak English 😐 I then said I'd be making a complaint to which he replied to me" how do I complain about you?" I was genuinely gobsmacked, shaking, and spiralling into full panic. I said I didn't want the back and forth and I just wanted my prescription so I could leave. He continued to have a go at me. I expressed that I was done talking about the matter and I just wanted my prescription multiple times before he finally turned round and printed out the prescription. Then I com on here to see MANY similar complaints. Park view group practice YOU SHOULD DO BETTER. Do better to safeguard your vulnerable patients from DRs with zero empathy or decent social skills. And now I've seen a large number of the exact type of complaints about the same person on here, I'm extremely saddened that they continue to hire him as they must be aware of how he makes a large number of patients feel.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I’ve had a consistently positive experience with this GP practice. Appointments and communication have been reliable, and the staff are professional and kind. I never feel rushed, and everything is explained clearly with a thoughtful plan moving forward. I’m really grateful for the care and would highly recommend this practice. Dr Galvis has honestly had such a positive impact on my life. I spent years struggling with my mental health and not feeling properly understood in the past, but Dr Galvis approaches care in a truly thoughtful and creative way. The first time she “prescribed” me a book to read I was sceptical, but it ended up meaning so much more to me than being given prescription tablets with little explanation or support. She’s also given me the confidence and tools to move forward - to the point that I’m now going back to university to train to become a dentist. Thank you, Dr Galvis.

In our current climate of underfunding and lack of resources this practice continues to provide an excellent and exceptional service to its patients. I have always got through to the practice and have managed to get an appointment 99% of the time. Reception staff have been helpful and friendly. I have always been treated with courtesy and dignity having a long-term condition. I do think people should be realistic. Use the pharmacy or 111 for advice. Urgent problems go to ED. The practice is not a walk in and expectations that someone should get a same day appointment then get annoyed because they can't is unfair on an already over stretched service doing their best for the local community. Its a 10/10 from me. Thank you Gatley Medical Centre

Except for 2 of the GPs (who are great!), I had GPs looking up my symptoms on Google, same goes for medical terms I used with them. Extremely unprofessional and unprepared.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Poorly managed appointments process. Doctors that dismiss issues and don't follow up on test results. Blame everything on anxiety.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Dr. Nousha Ansari
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Absolutely phenomenal medical surgery 💐 The patient care and standard of treatment are second to none. The staff from the reception team to the doctors are the friendliest I have ever encountered. I love both my doctors, Dr Uzma Khan and Dr Emily Ironmonger are amazing and compassionate professionals who actually care.Thank you so much from the bottom of my heart ❤️ 💙 💜 💖

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Jayne Headleand
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Your receptionists need to know what your doctors actually specialise in, been fobbed off twice now. When by coincidence I found a dr did what I needed but reception staff said they didn’t do that

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: mehvish khan
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I’d like to leave a glowing review for Dr. Victoria Evans, who saw my daughter at the practice this afternoon. Although my daughter was quite unsettled, Dr. Evans was incredibly kind, caring, and professional throughout. She listened attentively to my concerns and handled everything with such compassion. I truly appreciated her thoughtful approach.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Fatima Riaz
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Absolutely amazing surgery. Even with high pressures now days, they work so well, give quick appointments (triaging is good) with an excellent team of doctors , nurses, physiotherapists and receptionists.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Amina A
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Excellent service very friendly, polite and professional receptionists. Quite rare to find these days at GPs across the country. Always fantastic service from doctors, receptionists and nurses across the board at Gatley Medical. Great work!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: louis salter
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Being given the wrong swab kit for microbiology very poor service for the doctor

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mike Hindson-Evans
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: On a first visit to this Cheadle Hulme site (having registered at the southern GP site in Handforth) we found some of the internal signage confusing. This practice is split across two sites but does not always show the road name (or even the postcode). Assuming that "everyone knows" might not be the best approach to successful communication with your customers. Just the first visit ever, early in September 2025.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Aniq Choudhury
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have waited for a month for my GP to write me a supporting document about my mental health as he is the only one who knows my history well but I have received nothing and when I call the practice, I get the same excuses all the time. Terrible service and the GP is not considerate of my condition as a patient of his.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Brian Timperley
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: It's nice to be dealt with when your issue is time relevant- not sorted yet but at least on a path way It's those stories where people are either without diagnosis or pass away waiting!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Brian Timperley
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Excellent service on this occasion

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mike Andrews
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Always receive very good service

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: dominic creighton
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Incredibly thoughtful and considerate doctors, really impressed with the four Ive had appointments with this last couple of years. They would all get five stars. However - the receptionist I dealt with yesterday, on my phonecall, with regard to a potential life threatening emergency, was AWFUL. One Star. Less to be honest. Rude, brisk, dismissive, uncaring, and absolutely a disgrace to the Medical Group, and the brilliant, professional doctors who actually work there. If I wasn't a stubborn man and really pushed this receptionist on my phonecall for my (absolutely necessary) emergency appointment, I wouldn't have been seen. It's appalling to think this receptionist could be responsible for potentially seriously ill people being ignored and dismissed. I wish there was some way of lodging a formal complaint but not sure how to go about it. And again, the doctors? Brilliant! Can't recommend enough 😊

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Last Week.
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Physio Steven Barrett. “On it !! ” Steven is a fantastic attribute to Cheadle Hulme Medical Practice. His qualities are. Respectful, Caring, Patient, and Persistent. Stephen, leaves no stone unturned. I have nothing but faith in his capabilities. We are very, very lucky to have him! THANK YOU 🙏🏻

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: maria spence
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Been with this practice over 45 years but feel the waiting room is disgusting,the chairs are filthy and full of bacteria,surely the staff can see this so why hasn't anyone addressed this issue.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Danielle Ashcroft
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I've nothing but positive experiences with this surgery so far. I've received same day appointments and been seen by caring and empathetic medical professionals. It's an adjustment to have to use the website to submit requests, especially when I'd prefer to speak to a person, but I've found the teams response to requests pretty swift. I haven't experienced any of the negativity cited in other poor reviews.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eileen Clifford
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have had an appointment today. My care once again from this practice was excellent. The doctor was very thorough, kind, friendly and approachable. I felt that everything was being done to investigate and improve my problem.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Helisa Bagheri
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am extremely disappointed with the service at this GP practice. Over the years, both my children and I have been misdiagnosed multiple times, leading to serious consequences for our health. One particularly alarming experience involved a senior GP dismissing my concerns about perimenopausal symptoms. Despite expressing that I suspected I was entering perimenopause, she laughed and told me I was too young, completely disregarding that perimenopause can occur at various ages. She prescribed me the wrong medication, which worsened my symptoms to the point that I almost ended up in a mental health crisis.When I reported this to her, she casually offered antidepressants and didn’t even arrange a follow-up to check on my well-being. I had to take matters into my own hands and consult a private GP, who immediately confirmed I was perimenopausal and prescribed HRT. My symptoms improved almost instantly. This kind of negligence is unacceptable, and I have completely lost trust in this practice. I’ve even witnessed doctors Googling information in front of me, which makes me wonder—why bother going to the GP if I can just look things up myself? It seems they are only useful for minor issues like colds or flu. I would not recommend trusting them with anything beyond that.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Nuland
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Receptionists massive rude and unhelpful, it's like they go out their way to not help you. Very little care & compassion

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Hector Heath
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: In the short time I've been registered at the practice I've sent a few letters to my doctor to describe an ailment and the doctor has usually responded in 36 hrs or so. I handed one in on the 17/5/22 and when I hadn't heard anything by the 26th (today) I enquired why. Turns out the incompetent clowns lost it before the doc even saw it.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: James Gaskell
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Just had a receptionist constantly being condescending and passive aggressive when all I was asking was if I've had a tetanus shot in the last 10 years (asked to after advice from consultant from 111). I told her I wasn't happy with her behaviour and she told me to be quiet then put the phone down on me. I've had abuse off this receptionist before months ago. I suffer from multiple mental health problems including serve anxiety so speaking over the phone can be quite stressful. This was after waiting 15 mins on the phone already. Rang up again and another receptionist was polite and friendly, after the 1st experience and having problems before it's just not good enough.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: DAJ
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Brilliant health centre :-) Great reception staff, quick to respond and generally great to deal with - very lucky to have this in our area :-)

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Zoe Hague
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Fabulous GP, they have been brilliant with myself and my young family - always speedy to reply and very knowledgeable. Very lucky to have them as our Doctor's surgery.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Gaynor Swindlehurst
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I go for regular blood tests, ecg and blood pressure checks and to visit the doctor when i'm unwell

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Nicole “Future distant”
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: At first I was puzzled how a nhs institution could even have some bad reviews as it’s not a subway or a convenience store etc didn’t know that was a thing but after going here three times early morning missing work, the doctor kept texting on his phone ignoring multiple patients and promised to do definite ‘ biopsies’, in 2 weeks then when the time comes literally saying ‘nah let’s see what happens’ receptions really pleasant and helpful on the positive but the main doctor never seen anything like it in my life was shocking/genuinely unforgettable.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Lily Alex
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Handforth health centre have always been brilliant with me. I’ve sent in request via the online triage system and my doctor and other Handforth health workers have responded to message within 2 minutes! I feel well looked after and listened to when I have had face to face and phone call appointments too. There is never a wait and I can get through to them easily, appointments are available too. I have found the nurses and doctors to be lovely, and the receptionists to be very helpful and kind. I can’t fault this practice at all and highly recommend to anyone looking for a local practice.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Colin Mc (Canadaboygb)
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Hi Guys. had my left big toe analyzed and some preliminary work done before being booked an appointment at Congleton Memorial. I just want to say how pleased I was with the young lady who carried out the initial consultation and subsequent work on my toe,she was professional,considerate and very detailed in what she did(unfortunately cannot recall her name) .My toe has now recovered 99per cent thanks to her dedication. You've got a gooden there . Regards,Colin McMurray

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Sabina
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I went for a dermatology appointment at Handforth Health Centre. From the moment I entered the door, I found the personnel not very helpful. Then, I was taken by a very unpleasant nurse (of Asian origin, I think) to see my dermatologist. She was very moody and stayed with me during the appointment. I came with a mole I was worried about, so the dermatologist suggested checking all my other moles. However, I needed to take off my clothes in front of him without any separate curtains for privacy. The nurse was sitting on a chair next to the door in the meantime during all apointment. I felt really rushed taking my clothes off and throughout the entire appointment. Then, when the dermatologist finished the examination, I wanted to ask a few questions, but after my second question, the nurse opened the door to signal that the appointment was over and I had to leave. I have never experienced anything like that with the NHS or any medical organization anywhere in the world. It was an absolutely horrible experience.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Vincent Davies
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Outstanding and committed practice team who through clear communication ensure that each patient is treated with dignity and as an individual with individual needs. The combined efforts made by the administrative team along with the medical practitioners make Hulme Hall Medical Group a much valued example of best practice in health provision and continued well being.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mike Hindson-Evans
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: An excellent service every time, BUT... Access. The Handforth site car park is tiny (cosy!), with one disabled space. Better to go to the Mother Ship up in Hulme Hall, which has a MUCH bigger car parking area, spread around three-plus sides of the site. The surgery uses ACCURX to manage much of the admin processes including "ask for a consultation". The England wide NHS App doesn’t get much of a look in. We are pleased to have found this for our local GP.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Caitlin
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Helpful staff, made me feel at ease during my visit Friday 21st :)

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eileen Clifford
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have contacted this practice several times recently and as always I have received prompt attention from Dr Davies, Dr Halewood. Dr Nucomb and Dr Slater. I have always been treated with care, respect and dignity also with positive outcomes of their treatments . I would have no hesitation in recommending this practice. I have had an appointment with Dr Slater who was kind and considerate and very thorough in his examination. He then telephoned me 2 days later to ask how I was. Thank you to him and the other doctors and reception staff for their care.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: christine wilson
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Tracey (practice manager) is amazing I requested a call back It didn't happen She discovered there was a call made but it didn't connect Probably no signal on my phone She has now put in place a system whereby if that happens in the future the patient will receive a text to say the call didn't connect Also the patient will in future receive a text to let them know what number they are in the callback queue

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mark Belcher
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Been at this practice for over 20 years - they have never let me down, simply put - fast and efficient!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: layla_W “layla_w”
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Impossible to reach for serious concerns, poor communication and staff, deeply unsatisfied with service

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Kate Swanton
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Dr Dodd was lovely and very helpful

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Ged Daniel
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Entered my symptoms on the patchs system and received a phone call within 5 mins from the Doctor. Prescription was issued for the appropriate treatment. Overall fantastic service which is very much appreciated. Thank you.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Frank Okuda
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I would like to leave a positive review for my GP practice following my recent appointment. The service was very good, and the staff were welcoming and professional. During my visit, I was attended to by Dr. Khandavalli, who was very helpful and professional. She listened carefully to my concerns, explained things clearly, and made sure I understood the next steps regarding my care. Her calm and supportive approach made me feel comfortable throughout the consultation. I appreciate the professionalism and care I received from the practice.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Julie
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I’ve not had much cause to visit my surgery for many years but for the last two whereby various ailments have arisen. In that time I have seen three to four different GP’s all of which have been thorough, helpful and informative. Appointments made via the Patches App also very easy and quick to respond. 👌🏻 …

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Patricia Millington
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Appointment was on time Dr Samuel was a pleasure to see and helped me enormously

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Stephen King
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Extremely fast and professional service from the Doctor at the surgery, with a nice touch of compassion.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Andrew James
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: While l can not fault what the doctors do The reception staff,in particular one member does have a real attitude problem and thinks she is above everybody else. lt is not for them to say when a physio appointment is given after a doctor asked me to book it after seeing them and, she totally refused. You need to be professional and sort you manners out you horrible woman

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Julie
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Recent experiences with this practise have been excellent

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: finn
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Walked in, stood directly infront of the receptionist for a minute or two then cleared my throat and she didnt look up let alone ask me anything , AI can replace her and i wont lose any sleep. Terrible service. A&E receptionists have better front of house and they are overworked and probably paid less! Ridiculous, will be moving to brookfield after that.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Catherine Sims
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Please don’t join this surgery if you want to see a doctor in person or if you would like test results to be given back to you if they are abnormal.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Sonjia Clarkson
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: This surgery has been my life line. Especially Dr Nichols and Dr Whittaker. They have supported me through a very difficult time. They really do go the extra mile. I find the Reception team helpful too. Highly recommended

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Wendy Reddington
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Impossible to get an appointment and have not implemented new government policy of online appointment booking being available 24 hours even though I suspect they have taken the additional money

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Michael White
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Where to even begin. You call and the voice message tells you unless it is an emergency to use eConsult but economy only opens at 6pm and then you log onto eConsult and at 6.09pm a message pops saying the surgery is taking no more eConsult requests. You call to see a GP and you get triaged to a nurse or a paramedic or a musculoskeletal specialist. All of which to be fair are very good and often more useful than a GP. The practice pharmacist is also very helpful, Honestly though do any doctors even work here anymore?

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Racheal Shawcross
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: One stat is one too much Absolutely the worse surgery and communication! IN THE HISTORY IF THE NHS. You can never get on econsult. They make you feel thick, and that your troubling them. You hold for upto an hour to get through. You get fobbed off. You get given what ever appointment suits the doctors. Not one that is mutually convenient. Then you have to get back on the merry go round of being in the que for an hour. Receptionists well are very hit and miss. There is one particular receptionist (I won't name and shame) who is frankly god dam awful. Real chip on her shoulder and thinks she is some hierarchy in the GP world. To save your self the stress and grey hairs. DO NOT SIGN UP WITH THIS PRACTICE. I actually sat in the reception once. I was the only person in there. Two receptionist chatty chatting. I rang the telephone number and I was 7th in the queue. Neither of them where on the phone!!!!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Eric Quirk
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: When you (as an adult) really need urgent attention, Brookfield is excellent. Twice I have had real concerns as a result of a test or chest pains. Each time I was given the choice of a same day face to face or telephone appointment (after the 8am rush hour period). If you need more than 9 minutes interview it is readily available. Caring and thoughtful doctors and staff (including many on reception) despite the heavy pressure of increasing patient numbers. Also often answering queries on the phone.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Jay Camenzuli
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Ring the phone, no answer, walk in and all the receptionists are laughing and joking while my call is ringing. No one waiting, no queue, nothing. What the hell is going on!!!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Andrew Hine
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Very friendly and helpful but currently very difficult to get an appointment. As a GP they do the job very well but as a service it is poor, simply because booking to see the GP is an obstacle. The PATCH system is a major weakness because it seems to run out of "credits" and stops accepting requests for appointments very early in the day. This puts reliance on the office admin who then have to mop up the calls.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Christine Forden
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Short wait to see doctor

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Vicky
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: A great GP with very friendly, personable and helpful staff, one of the best I’ve ever had.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Enid Smith
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Many thanks for excellent service given to to my Husband David Smith, by Dr Sumra recently, and also the reception staff

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: eric lane
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had a great experience as I always do the lady who took my bloods was a breath of fresh air

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Asim Ali
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Attended with my mother, I have always found the Barrington medical centre to be helpful, we saw Dr Hussain, who was very kind and explained my mother’s problem well, a very competent young doctor.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: David Cowsill
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Very pleased with the efficient treatment and kind attention I received.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Shuaib akib
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: It was nice and lovely visit with family. We had an wonderful consultation with Dr. Hussain. We wish him all the best for his future.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Lindsay Roper
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have visited Dr Hussain three times over the past three weeks He decided I needed to go to hospital on my first visit with low blood pressure and with the hospital help got me back on track with the two follow up visits and the referrals which are now all booked after finding blood in my urine he has been amazing and I am do grateful Dr Hussain had been great we have re visited my medication and made changes and he had Checked me out on both visits I am so grateful for all he has done plus the wider team at the surgery you are all amazing Thank you for all you have done for me Lindsay Roper

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Shikha Chauhan
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Dr Hussain was very attentive, patient and helpful in understanding the problem. He made sure I was comfortable and definitely that’s the kind of doctor visit that doesn’t make you anxious.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Bette Graves
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had a lovely experience with Dr Hussain. He was very helpful and also very lovely to speak to. He asked for my opinion on the online services and I reported that I had troubles logging into my GP services through the NHS app. Overall, he seems like a wonderful GP to have at Barrington and only wants to improve its services for the better.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: R YU
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Dr Hussein was extremely kind and helpful, he was addressed all my concerns.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Gill Hogburn
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Barrington medical practice excellent doctors and nurses and receptionists had an appointment made for my husband and myself 24hours later saw dr simona juverdeanu treated for our problems and medicine requirements sent to pharmacy what excellent service love the practice highly recommended 10 out of 10.grateful thanks to all staff john and gill.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mark O 'Connor
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Had an appointment with Dr Tom Earnshaw, fabulous GP who I have not seen for a few years.Very helpful caring and professional and highly recommended 👍 …

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Richard Williams
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I've recently moved to the practice from another nearby in Altrincham. So far so good, much better responsiveness and the doctors have followed up an ailment to ensure continuity. Very impressed with the efficiency of this practice compared to my old one.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Keith Hadfield
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Very pleased with my appointment today with Dr Wright. He was very helpful, and informative.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Susan Collard
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Positive recent experience of available appointments for myself and my children at a busy time of year with empathy and good advice and support given.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Ash Simpson-Davies
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: As a young professional new to the area, I was looking to register with a new GP and used an upcoming holiday as a good reason to check my travel vaccination history. Liz and the reception team were fantastic they transferred everything over from my previous GP and carefully went through my vaccination records with me. It turned out I didn’t need any additional vaccines after all, but it was great to meet the team who’ll be looking after me and my future health. Thanks again, Ash

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Mickey Puri
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had been told by a friend that St Johns was one of the very few surgeries that was doing something to find out if Statins would suit you. So I called them re this. A doctor called back same day but he said he was a Locum and was not aware of any test as this. Then at 7pm same day, Vanessa, the Practice Manager called me and said there had been a trial running that looked into this, and the trial was ending the next day. So she agreed to put me down for it and next day I took part in the trial. So its great that St Johns is taking part in such initiatives, and I was hugely grateful to Vanessa for calling me well outside normal surgery times and booking me onto the trial, that too in a Christmas Week. Very impressive and Well Done!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Charlotte Healey
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I am a big fan of the new booking system, having spent many an hour waiting for the appointment phone line to respond over the years. The doctors and nurse practitioners at this practice are first rate and now it’s even easier to book and amend appointments. The coordination of blood tests, prescriptions and results consultations is seamless. A great step forward! Huge thanks

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Tracey Leigh
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I visited St John’s recently with an issue with my ear . I got an appointment really easily . Dr Sangha was very attentive and helpful and I was referred very quickly . He is always very caring and a good listener

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: philgez
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Excellent doctor (Bethany) - clear and considerate and concise. Gave me the time I’m needed and was super helpful. A credit to the practice

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Graham Sadler
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Fantastic service. Saw doctor who was sympathetic and listened, with a few days, blood test and scans all done within a week.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Simon G
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Some good and bad experiences here. Was seen last year by a female doctor here who diagnosed me with anxiety and depression. I was referred for CBT treatment. The therapist, after many hours of talking therapy suggested that I may be suffering from a neurodiversity condition. I mentioned this to my GP on my next check in and was practically laughed at. The response was basically that we all experience these symptoms. I was embarrassed and didn’t raise the issue again. I was placed on a high dose of anti depressants and sent on my way. I’ve now stopped the medication abruptly as I am still experiencing the same problems - withdrawal is hell but I have no desire to return to this GP to revisit what was discussed with my therapist and have nowhere else to turn. Looking to transfer to a new GP to get the help I need

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Chuanjie Zhou
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have great concerns about this medical centre, and I have no issue with doctors, but their reception team was very rude. You will never expect them to give you a smile. We have made an urgent appointment 9 am today for our granddaughter, who has had a bad cough with a running nose. We arrived at the medical centre 9:10am and at that time only one receptionist attended, but was continuously using the phone. We were waiting patiently for over five minutes until she finished her phone call. Then she told us that the appointment was invalid because we missed the appointment by over 15minutes. We tried to argue with her that we arrived at 9:10 am and the appointment should be valid. Suddenly, five receptionists appeared at the reception desk, showing a very aggressive manner, and one of the receptionists even threatened to call the police. I have to say, this reception team is arrogant, rude, and has a total lack of empathy for the patients. The management team should look into restructuring the reception team! I have checked all 53 Google reviews of this medical centre, and 26 out of 53 were one star, with an average score of 2.6. So far, this 2.6 score is the lowest within Greater Manchester that I have ever seen. 16 of 53 were complaints about their receptionists, which should tell you something!

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Patrick Tarbuck
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: In a time when people find it easier to criticise our GP service and the health system, I think it’s really important to recognise truly excellent care. This is the best GP I’ve been at, they are patient, calm, accommodating and easy to deal with, which is even more remarkable when you consider how much vitriol and abuse they face on a daily basis. Well done to all the team at Altrincham medical practice, I feel very lucky to have this as my local practice.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Abhay
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I had an exceptional experience at Altrincham Medical Practice! From the moment I walked in, the staff were warm, welcoming, and highly professional. The doctors and nurses were incredibly thorough, taking the time to listen to my concerns and explain everything clearly. The level of care and attention to detail truly set this practice apart. The facilities were clean and well-organized, which added to the overall positive atmosphere. I left feeling reassured and confident in the care I received. I have always felt that they actually enjoyed their profession. My friends based in other surgeries can't believe the help I get from my doctors. The office manager is very capable; some of the receptionists can be a bit unpolished but generally, the service at the desk is very good. The building is clean and welcoming. Parking is not always easy but arriving a good 10 minutes before the appointment can help as people come but also vacate quite quickly.

I said she is 12 ( although she looks about 9) are you not going to give her a script, I asked him twice and he said no, you can buy over the counter, I said but she is 12. He said ' my supervisor will ask me why I gave a script out when it can be purchased OTC' , again I said she is 12. I went into the chemist, the lady said have they not given you a script, I said no and I told her my granddaughter was 12. £6.50 it was for these eye drops which I probably could have bought at Morrisons for less. My gripe is. If I as pensioner I was told to buy something OTC, even though though we are entitled, I would have paid it but a 12 year old. Disgusted with this practice if that is how they work. I think they need to look at who is entitled to what . End of gripe

His results showed that he scored 99% symptoms on every test and was told that there were only 7% of the population with such scores. Obviously now having a diagnosis he made an appointment to see his GP at Yorkshire street where he was told that they could/would not prescribe the vital medication he needs to live a normal independent life and relieve his symptoms. recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: Some of the doctors here are more thoughtful than others but overall they reflect institutional neglect. Tests have always comeback within their very broad definition of 'normal' and they refuse to apply any further clinical consideration to a patients' actual clinical picture. I asked for my medical records and I still haven't received the requested information three months later. I've complained but received no response. One receptionist a month ago completely ignored me. Then she dealt with me as if it was an inconvenience. The online triage system is now a grim joke. It frequently suspends the option to make an appointment for a week or more, and then every alternative method of contact filters you back to it. The clinic is at the forefront of a modern dysfunctional NHS where compassion disappeared decades ago. The patient comes very last in its considerations and it merely a source of LHA funding. Addendum : I am now discovering that the causes that I suggested for my illness and was laughed out of the surgery with ('Dr' Yazicci actually laughed at them) are indeed the issue and I am now self medicating with considerbale success. The dimissal of my theories by this surgery has cost me years of my life as I didn't act on it. Any attempt to complain to them is water off a duck's back to them. I've since changed surgeries. When I mentioned I was going to this, this one became even less responsive and more dismissive.

It seems a totally ridiculous way to run a doctor's surgery. The nurse practitioner is abrupt and rude and acts like the cost of a prescription comes out of her own pocket. When told that there were a couple of things that needed to be mentioned to her ( due to having had to wait a good few weeks to get an appointment) she responded by saying that she only had time to discuss one thing!!! Roisin the practice nurse is lovely and the most helpful member of staff at the surgery, and also seems to be the most overworked staff there too. recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Vikrant Kalukhe
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I visited the practice for an in-person appointment to obtain a fit note while suffering from flu symptoms, including a high fever. I had made significant effort to attend despite feeling very unwell. Upon arrival, I was informed by the receptionist that the appointment was actually a telephone consultation, which was not indicated when the booking was made or confirmed. I politely pointed this out, explaining that it appeared to be an administrative error, and suggested it might help to flag this to prevent similar mix-ups for other patients in the future (e.g., someone travelling unnecessarily while ill). Unfortunately, instead of acknowledging the mistake or apologising, the receptionist repeated that I did not need to wait in the surgery for the call – raising her voice and speaking slowly and loudly on the second occasion. This felt highly patronising and dismissive, especially when I was already feeling extremely unwell and vulnerable. In the end, the journey was wasted, and I left without the consultation proceeding as expected. Clearer communication about appointment types and better handling of patient feedback when errors occur would greatly improve the experience here.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Amanda Neville
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: A masterclass in how not to run a GP surgery. Reception staff appear to have taken on the role of clinicians, routinely dismissing concerns, deciding what does and does not warrant medical attention, and frequently redirecting patients to A&E or out-of-hours services for minor or ongoing issues. One wonders when this became part of their job description. GP consultations offer little improvement. Complex medical conditions, mental health concerns, and written recommendations from specialists are met with indifference or ignored altogether. Listening appears optional; empathy entirely absent. Complaints are treated with the same enthusiasm as patient care — acknowledged, if at all, then quietly disregarded. Patients are spoken to in a patronising manner and left feeling foolish for seeking help. If you are looking for accessible, patient-centred care, this is not the place. If, however, you enjoy being dismissed, redirected elsewhere, and made to feel like an inconvenience, this surgery may be exactly what you’re looking for.

The receptionists are the rudest, most inept people I’ve ever had the displeasure to come across and should have their parole revoked (I’m assuming they’re on parole given the aggressive behaviour they show anytime you ring up). As for the administrative staff, they seem to be incapable of reading a clinical letter, ignorant of how their ineptitude affects patient care, or blatantly money-grubbers. The practices operate a “total-triage” system that is a choice given to them by the government to abandon patient care in favour of increased subsidies. I probably don’t need to explain at this point; they took the subsidies! They don’t care about patients, and If they ever did they were incapable of doing anything about it.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Deborah Walton
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I have had a horrendous experience being registered with this group practice. I made a complaint about a senior admin worker who denied receiving 3 letters from my solicitor after waiting 12mths for a copy of my gp notes . Then my Gp notes were destroyed vindictivly I am amazed that the practice manager didn't know it was gross Misconduct and a criminal offence to tamper, alter or fix a patients notes. I know this by comments passed to me at a practice managers meeting. I had no option but to report this to the GMC who passed it to NHS England to investigate. My case was to serious for them to investigate as they should do because I named 2 Gp s who I had apts with and went in, sat down. The Gp looked at his screen and didn't speak when I told him my reason for going to see a Gp, he totally ignored me and after what felt like 30 mins of silence I got up and left his room. I had no idea Dr's behaved this way and happened twice with 2 Gp's. NHS England conducted a corrupt investigation without a single meeting with me. I found out 12mths later that the GMC worked with NHS England on this investigation, they don't work together. All this came to the senior Gp at the practice who was responsible for the surgery, I now know he took early retirement before the investigation got going. Ever since I have been treated very badly by every Gp I have seen at several practices. I am denied Healthcare, treatment and medication across the board even mental health services have been closed to me. I have been set up by mental health nurses who requested a urine sample under the order of a consultant. The drug test they did came up positive for every substance you can think of but my prescribed medication didn't show up on the drug test, codeine and pregabalin are both controlled drugs and medication I take every day. Think this proves it was all staged and a set up, you don't expect this from a mental health nurse. Had I taken any kind of class A drugs I wouldn't have given anyone a urine sample. I was left bent in half with horrific back pain the Gp practice I was registered with Mark Street Surgery refused to review my pain relief or increase it. I am now disabled for the rest of my life and under a spinal surgeon at Salford with a life curve of my spine. I could go on forever I am now registered in littleborough and denied any kind of Healthcare Treatment and medication. Just today I've been denied antibiotics for a chest infection and have COPD. They are trying to kill me off for daring to make a complaint. I am advising everyone not to make any complaints against any Gp's if you do your life will be turned into a living hell just as mine has. If you do you will get invented diagnoses, lies out and out lies all on your care summary and cannot be removed, only they do remove notes and letters and remove all names of Dr's and nurses from your Gp notes this is tampering again with my life. My whole life and the birth of my Boys has been wiped out how dare they do this to me ? I have a right to complain I cannot sit back and take being labeled a druggie, this is now one step to far I've been given no option but to go to the Nursing and Midwifery council and The royal college of nurses and midwives. I can't be punished anymore than I have been and still taking this off Gp's and bardoc Dr's, who put the cuff on to do my BP and don't inflate it they then walk out of my home without a word. A Gp at the practice I am registered with looked in my ear after earache for 2wks and bleeding from inside and said it was OK Really ?? I also had a swelling under my arm and lumps he failed to examine me and have a family history of breast cancer. He smirked at me in a very sick way, he's training to be a Gp. District Nurses refuse me compression bandages requested by my vascular surgeon but then go on to lie and document I couldn't tolerate them. I am totally disgusted with all of them I am now self managing leg ulcers because they refuse me home visits and dressings. Don't complain its not worth it.

recent_reviews_across_manchester.author: Sandeep Tandon
recent_reviews_across_manchester.text: I ordered my repeat prescription via the app several days ago. When I attended the pharmacy, I was told the prescription had not been authorised by the doctor. On Thursday, I attended the surgery and was informed by the receptionist that the particular doctor was “not in”. I explained the urgency and asked for the prescription to be pushed through. I was then assured that my medication would be ready to collect from the pharmacy on Saturday morning. Today (Saturday 17/01/26), I attended the pharmacy at 1pm, only to find that it was closed. Both the pharmacy and the GP surgery are now closed. As of today, I have completely run out of my prescribed medication, including Ramipril and Atorvastatin. I have disabilities and suffer from high blood pressure, and being without this medication places my health at risk. I am extremely concerned that the online prescription service is being promoted, yet it is ineffective if prescriptions are not authorised in a timely manner. The system only works if doctors take responsibility for approving patients’ medication. I would like this matter urgently reviewed, an explanation provided as to how this situation was allowed to occur, and assurances that this does not happen again. I also request immediate advice on how I can obtain my medication as soon as possible. I look forward to your prompt response. Yours faithfully, S
